title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄序
嘉靖甲午是當貢士之年監
察御史王〔鎬〕被
簡巡按江西諸憲務既貞爰舉試
事先是巡撫副都御史王〔燧〕
飭吏平民務承
上意暨提督軍務僉都御史陳〔察〕
===
相與協誠賚于茲士士宜殫
力于學而人亦歡然願見賓
興之盛舉也于是提調則左
布政使王〔遵〕左參政張〔大輪〕
監試則副使胡〔德〕僉事盧〔䀈〕
〔麒〕御史聘〔文澤〕暨教諭陳〔錠〕
爲考試官而同考則教授徐
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄序

嘉靖甲午，是當貢士之年。監察御史王〔鎬〕被簡巡按江西，諸憲務既貞，爰舉試事。先是，巡撫副都御史王〔燧〕飭吏平民，務承上意，暨提督軍務僉都御史陳〔察〕相與協誠，賚于茲士。士宜殫力于學，而人亦歡然願見賓興之盛舉也。於是，提調則左布政使王〔遵〕、左參政張〔大輪〕；監試則副使胡〔德〕、僉事盧〔䀈〕〔麒〕。御史聘〔文澤〕暨教諭陳〔錠〕爲考試官，而同考則教授徐
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

The jiawu year of Jiajing [1534] was a year for presenting scholars as tribute to the court. Investigating Censor Wang Hao 王鎬 was selected to conduct an inspection of Jiangxi. Once the various duties of censorial oversight had been set in order, he undertook the examination arrangements. Before this, Grand Coordinator and Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Sui 王燧 had disciplined the officials and brought peace to the people, striving to carry out the imperial will. Together with Chen Cha 陳察, Assistant Censor-in-Chief and Superintendent of Military Affairs, he worked in concert and sincerity to bestow benefits upon the scholars here. The scholars ought to devote all their energies to learning, and the people, too, eagerly wished to witness the grand occasion of honoring and advancing worthy men.

The Proctors were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Wang Zun 王遵 and Left Administration Vice Commissioner Zhang Dalun 張大輪. Supervising the examination were Surveillance Vice Commissioner Hu De 胡德 and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Lu [given name transcribed as 䀈麒, reading uncertain]. The censor invited Wenze 文澤 [surname missing?] and Instructor Chen Ding 陳錠 to serve as Examiners, while the Associate Examiners included Professor Xu…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
〔元孝〕教諭蘇〔秉彝〕楊〔琨〕鄭〔守〕
〔思〕趙〔勑〕陳〔建〕戴〔高〕高〔蘭〕張〔邦〕
〔學〕尤〔時熙〕咸至右布政使陸〔杰〕
右叅政陸〔深〕左叅議郝〔世〕
〔家〕按察司副使劉〔可〕邵〔煉〕吴
〔章〕僉事林〔應標〕朱〔孔陽〕周〔相〕
曁都指揮同知曹〔震〕僉事吴
===
〔山〕皆恊賛于外右叅議朱〔紈〕
僉事王〔琇〕都指揮僉事李〔時〕
先期入
賀按察使任〔忠〕副使夏〔邦謨〕未幾
遷去固嘗加意試事而主事
〔林山〕以有事至亦樂于是成
者也建置之宜區畫之及或
punctuated: 〔元孝〕、教諭蘇〔秉彝〕、楊〔琨〕、鄭〔守〕〔思〕、趙〔勑〕、陳〔建〕、戴〔高〕、高〔蘭〕、張〔邦〕〔學〕、尤〔時熙〕咸至。右布政使陸〔杰〕、右叅政陸〔深〕、左叅議郝〔世〕〔家〕、按察司副使劉〔可〕、邵〔煉〕、吴〔章〕、僉事林〔應標〕、朱〔孔陽〕、周〔相〕曁都指揮同知曹〔震〕、僉事吴〔山〕，皆恊賛于外。右叅議朱〔紈〕、僉事王〔琇〕、都指揮僉事李〔時〕先期入賀。按察使任〔忠〕、副使夏〔邦謨〕未幾遷去，固嘗加意試事；而主事〔林山〕以有事至，亦樂于是成者也。建置之宜，區畫之及，或
translation_en: …[Xu] Yuanxiao, together with the Instructors Su Bingyi, Yang Kun, Zheng Shousi, Zhao Chi, Chen Jian, Dai Gao, Gao Lan, Zhang Bangxue, and You Shixi, all arrived to serve as Associate Examiners. Lu Jie, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Lu Shen, Right Administration Vice Commissioner; Hao Shijia, Left Administration Assistant Commissioner; Liu Ke, Shao Lian, and Wu Zhang, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Lin Yingbiao, Zhu Kongyang, and Zhou Xiang, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; Cao Zhen, Regional Vice Military Commissioner; and Wu Shan, Regional Assistant Military Commissioner, all assisted outside the examination compound. Zhu Wan, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner; Wang Xiu, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner; and Li Shi, Regional Assistant Military Commissioner, had gone to court beforehand to offer congratulations. Ren Zhong, Surveillance Commissioner, and Xia Bangmo, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, were transferred away shortly afterward, but had already devoted particular attention to the examination arrangements. Secretary Lin Shan, who arrived on other business, likewise gladly helped bring the undertaking to completion. As for the suitability of the facilities and the thoroughness of the planning, some …

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
前此所未備而矢心奉
命若御史者竊意以爲不易得也
下是合提學僉事李〔舜臣〕所
選士三千有奇而三試之得
中式者九十五人幷錄其文
之優者以
獻而〔文澤〕竊有願以告之諸士
===
子者曰吾讀人物表而見古
今人之不齊也才不才若是
分者可知矣剛柔者其生也
强情者其志也過不及者其
履也善惡者其歸也是故先
王執中以立教君子隨分以
成才故教化者先王所以致
punctuated:
前此所未備，而矢心奉命若御史者，竊意以爲不易得也。下是合提學僉事李〔舜臣〕所選士三千有奇，而三試之，得中式者九十五人，幷錄其文之優者以獻。
而〔文澤〕竊有願以告之諸士子者，曰：「吾讀《人物表》，而見古今人之不齊也。才不才若是分者，可知矣。剛柔者，其生也；强情者，其志也；過不及者，其履也；善惡者，其歸也。是故先王執中以立教，君子隨分以成才。故教化者，先王所以致
translation_en:
…what had previously been lacking. Someone like the censor, who devoted himself wholeheartedly to carrying out the imperial command, is, I venture to think, not easily found. Thereupon [?], more than three thousand candidates selected by Li Shunchen 李舜臣, Education Intendant and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, were assembled and examined in three sessions. Ninety-five passed, and the best of their compositions were transcribed for presentation to the throne.
I, Wenze 文澤, also venture to express a wish to these scholars, saying: “I read the Table of Figures and see how unequal people, ancient and modern, have been. That the talented and the untalented should be so differentiated is understandable. Firmness and yielding belong to their inborn natures; forcefulness and feeling [?] belong to their resolve; excess and deficiency belong to their conduct; goodness and evil are their ultimate destinations. Thus the former kings held to the mean in establishing their teachings, and gentlemen developed their abilities according to their individual endowments. Moral instruction and transformation were therefore the means by which the former kings brought about …

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
齊于衆問學者君子所以自
宜其躬是以隆盛之世聖哲
者興揖遜而吁俞肩摩而踵
至也其次者未必聖且哲也
而皆不失爲材剛柔不同其
于協德一也小大不同其于
適用一也故曰寬而栗也彊
===
而義也自夫先王之敎不行
聖哲之風益遠于是始有不
治之朝而有不適用之士故
太上獨行其次質任次庸最
次不肖庸若不肖不足言也
質任者或失則陋或失則冥
而獨行者亦未爲得何也工
punctuated:
齊于衆，問學者君子所以自宜其躬。是以隆盛之世，聖哲者興，揖遜而吁俞，肩摩而踵至也。其次者，未必聖且哲也，而皆不失爲材。剛柔不同，其于協德一也；小大不同，其于適用一也。故曰：「寬而栗也，彊而義也。」
自夫先王之敎不行，聖哲之風益遠，于是始有不治之朝，而有不適用之士。故太上獨行，其次質任，次庸，最次不肖。庸若不肖，不足言也。質任者，或失則陋，或失則冥，而獨行者亦未爲得。何也？工
translation_en:
…bring the multitude into accord; inquiry and learning are the means by which the gentleman makes his own conduct fitting. Thus, in ages of flourishing prosperity, sages and wise men arose, bowing and yielding to one another, exchanging counsel and assent, their shoulders brushing as they arrived one after another. Those of the next rank were not necessarily sages or wise men, yet all possessed useful talents. Though differing in firmness and gentleness, they were alike in harmonizing their virtue; though differing in the greatness or smallness of their abilities, they were alike in being fit for service. Thus it is said: “Generous yet disciplined; strong yet righteous.”
Once the teachings of the former kings ceased to be practiced, and the influence of the sages and wise men grew ever more remote, there began to be courts without good government and scholars unfit for service. Hence the highest were those who pursued their own course; next were those who relied on their native disposition [?]; next came the mediocre, and lowest of all the unworthy. The mediocre and the unworthy do not merit discussion. Those who rely on their native disposition may lapse into narrowness or into ignorance; yet those who pursue their own course have not necessarily attained what is right either. Why is this? They are adept…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
于其習而不能原乎其始故
曰不適用之士也則不得不
取質任者而用之乃質任者
顧又無所見聞于義而無所
監慕于行雖有善者旦夕之
爲安十一而偶得耳其不善
者所謂冥頑與陋者舉不足恃
===
而竟敗也人見其敗也又思
有以易乎是者始務滌濯其
躬而覬震曜于世是故行欲
脩也而惡矯也志欲潔也而
惡亢也辭欲明也而惡核也
矯則易僞亢則易厲核則易
誣而去道遠矣故曰至危無
punctuated:
于其習，而不能原乎其始，故曰不適用之士也。則不得不取質任者而用之，乃質任者顧又無所見聞于義，而無所監慕于行。雖有善者，旦夕之爲安十一而偶得耳。其不善者，所謂冥頑與陋者，舉不足恃，而竟敗也。
人見其敗也，又思有以易乎是者，始務滌濯其躬，而覬震曜于世。是故行欲脩也，而惡矯也；志欲潔也，而惡亢也；辭欲明也，而惡核也。矯則易僞，亢則易厲，核則易誣，而去道遠矣。故曰：「至危無
translation_en:
…in their accustomed practices, yet unable to trace them back to their origins; hence they are called men unfit for practical service. One therefore has no choice but to select and employ men of straightforward disposition. Yet these men, in turn, have neither observed nor heard anything of righteousness, nor have they models of conduct to look up to and emulate. Even where there is something good in them, their daily actions yield good only once in ten times, and then by chance [?]. As for their shortcomings—their so-called obtuseness, obstinacy, and narrowness—they leave them altogether unworthy of reliance, and they ultimately fail.
When people see this failure, they again seek some way to change such conduct. They begin to devote themselves to cleansing their persons, hoping to shine brilliantly before the world. Thus, conduct should be cultivated, but affectation is abhorrent; aspirations should be pure, but haughtiness is abhorrent; words should be clear, but censoriousness is abhorrent. Affectation readily turns into deceit, haughtiness into harshness, and censoriousness into false accusation, taking one far from the Way. Hence it is said: “Utterly perilous, without…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
當雖貴不盛貴乎學者各成
其才以適于用而已今
上聰明仁聖至化融洽側席賢良
常若弗至諸士子以薦且將
試于南宮以對于
大廷爲
明天子用宜思有以成其才者庶
===
幾虞廷所謂九德而不但爲
獨行之士又況矯與亢與核
者足爲有司慮哉
河南開封府鄭州儒學學正
楊文澤謹序
punctuated:
當，雖貴不盛。貴乎學者各成其才，以適于用而已。今上聰明仁聖，至化融洽，側席賢良，常若弗至。諸士子以薦，且將試于南宮，以對于大廷，爲明天子用，宜思有以成其才者，庶幾虞廷所謂九德，而不但爲獨行之士。又況矯與亢與核者，足爲有司慮哉？

河南開封府鄭州儒學學正楊文澤謹序。
translation_en:
… fitting; though esteemed, they do not flourish. What matters in learning is simply that each person develop his abilities so that they are suited to practical service. Our present sovereign is intelligent, humane, and sagely; his consummate transforming influence spreads harmoniously everywhere. He leaves a place beside him for worthy and capable men, ever anxious lest they fail to arrive. Having been recommended, these scholars will soon sit the Metropolitan Examination at the Ministry of Rites and present their responses in the imperial court, to enter the service of our enlightened Son of Heaven. They should consider how to develop their abilities, aspiring to the nine virtues spoken of at the court of Shun, rather than merely becoming men distinguished by individual conduct. How, then, could affectation, haughtiness, and censorious scrutiny give the responsible officials cause for concern?

Preface respectfully composed by Yang Wenze, Instructor of the Confucian School of Zhengzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan.

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖十三年江西鄉試
監臨官
巡按江西監察御史王　鎬〔宗周直隸灤州人　己丑進士〕

江西等處承宣布政使司右布政使王　遵〔舜典直隸宣城縣人　辛未進士〕

===

punctuated:
嘉靖十三年江西鄉試。

監臨官。
巡按江西監察御史王　鎬〔宗周，直隸灤州人，己丑進士〕。

提調官。
江西等處承宣布政使司右布政使王　遵〔舜典，直隸宣城縣人，辛未進士〕。
江西等處承宣布政使司左參政張大輪〔用載，浙江東陽縣人，甲戌進士〕。

監試官。
江西等處提刑按察司副使胡　德〔仁叔，直隸桀□縣人，戊辰進士〕。
江西等處提刑按察司僉事盧耿麒〔全之，直隸婺源縣人，癸未進士〕。

考試官。
河南開封府鄭州儒學學正楊文澤〔德孚，浙江鄞縣人，乙酉貢士〕。
廣東韶州府仁化縣儒學教諭陳　錠〔用賞，福建長樂縣人，己卯貢士〕。

同考試官。
直隸淮安府儒學教授徐元孝〔子順，順天府大興縣籍，餘姚縣人，己卯貢士〕。
湖廣德安府應城縣儒學教諭蘇秉彝〔民仲，四川忠縣人，丙子貢士〕。
湖廣岳州府華容縣儒學教諭楊　琨〔貴之，直隸定遠縣籍，廣西護衛人，己卯貢士〕。
直隸蘇州府崑山縣儒學教諭鄭守恩〔宗慶，福建長樂縣人，己卯貢士〕。
湖廣荊州府監利縣儒學教諭趙　勑〔惟誠，四川內江縣人，乙酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Jiangxi Provincial Examination, the thirteenth year of Jiajing (1534).

Supervising Official
Wang Gao, Investigating Censor on inspection duty in Jiangxi, courtesy name Zongzhou, was from Luanzhou, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the jichou year.

Proctors
Wang Zun, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi, courtesy name Shundian, was from Xuancheng County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the xinwei year.
Zhang Dalun, Left Administration Vice Commissioner of Jiangxi, courtesy name Yongzai, was from Dongyang County, Zhejiang. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the jiaxu year.

Examination Monitors
Hu De, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Jiangxi, courtesy name Renshu, was from Jie□ County [?], Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the wuchen year.
Lu Gengqi, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangxi, courtesy name Quanzhi, was from Wuyuan County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the guiwei year.

Examiners
Yang Wenze, Director of the Confucian School of Zhengzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, courtesy name Defu, was from Yin County, Zhejiang. He was a tribute student (gongshi) of the yiyou year.
Chen Ding, Instructor at the Confucian School of Renhua County, Shaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, courtesy name Yongshang, was from Changle County, Fujian. He was a tribute student (gongshi) of the jimao year.

Associate Examiners
Xu Yuanxiao, Professor at the Confucian School of Huai'an Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Zishun, was registered in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, and was originally from Yuyao County. He was a tribute student (gongshi) of the jimao year.
Su Bingyi, Instructor at the Confucian School of Yingcheng County, De'an Prefecture, Huguang, courtesy name Minzhong, was from Zhong County, Sichuan. He was a tribute student (gongshi) of the bingzi year.
Yang Kun, Instructor at the Confucian School of Huarong County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, courtesy name Guizhi, was registered in Dingyuan County, Zhili, and was from the Guangxi Escort Guard. He was a tribute student (gongshi) of the jimao year.
Zheng Shou'en, Instructor at the Confucian School of Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Zongqing, was from Changle County, Fujian. He was a tribute student (gongshi) of the jimao year.
Zhao Chi, Instructor at the Confucian School of Jianli County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, courtesy name Weicheng, was from Neijiang County, Sichuan. He was a tribute student (gongshi) of the yiyou year.

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
福建福州府候官縣儒學教諭陳　建〔廷肇廣東東莞縣人戊子貢士〕
浙江處州府縉雲縣儒學教諭戴　高〔師中福建閩縣人壬午貢士〕
直隸鎮江府丹陽縣儒學教諭高　蘭〔汝佩山西陽曲縣人戊子貢士〕
湖廣漢陽府漢川縣儒學教諭張邦學〔時敏廣西桂林中衛人壬午貢士〕
直隸真定府元氏縣儒學教諭尤時熙〔季美河南河南衛人壬午貢士〕
印卷官
江西等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷姜舜夫〔咨政湖廣武昌縣人監生〕
江西等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷盧　溥〔文博直隸長洲縣人監生〕
收掌試卷官

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子之燕居申申如也夭夭如也
中也者天下之大本也和也者天下之達
道也
是故君子有終身之憂無一朝之患也乃
若所憂則有之舜人也我亦人也舜爲
法於天下可傳於後世我由未免爲鄉
人也是則可憂也憂之如何如舜而已
矣若夫君子所患則亡矣非仁無爲也
非禮無行也如有一朝之患則君子不
患矣
===
易
六二不耕穫不菑畬則利有攸往
上九畀王鉉大吉无不利
是以明於天之道而察於民之故是興神
物以前民用聖人以此齊戒以神明其
德夫
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子之燕居，申申如也，夭夭如也。

中也者，天下之大本也；和也者，天下之達道也。

是故君子有終身之憂，無一朝之患也。乃若所憂，則有之：舜，人也；我，亦人也。舜爲法於天下，可傳於後世，我由未免爲鄉人也，是則可憂也。憂之如何？如舜而已矣。若夫君子所患，則亡矣。非仁無爲也，非禮無行也。如有一朝之患，則君子不患矣。

易

六二，不耕穫，不菑畬，則利有攸往。

上九，畀王鉉，大吉，无不利。

是以明於天之道，而察於民之故，是興神物以前民用。聖人以此齊戒，以神明其德。夫
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

When the Master was at leisure, his manner was relaxed and cheerful.

Centrality is the great foundation of all under Heaven; harmony is the universally followed Way of all under Heaven.

Thus the gentleman has concerns that last his entire life, but no anxiety over a single morning’s misfortune. As for what concerns him, there is indeed something: Shun was a human being, and I too am a human being. Shun became a model for all under Heaven, worthy of being handed down to later generations, while I still [?] remain merely an ordinary villager. This is indeed cause for concern. What should one do about this concern? Simply become like Shun. As for the gentleman’s anxieties, there are none. He does nothing contrary to benevolence and undertakes nothing contrary to ritual propriety. Should a single morning’s misfortune occur, the gentleman does not let it trouble him.

Book of Changes

Six in the second place: Reaping without plowing, obtaining cultivated fields without first clearing them: then it is favorable to have somewhere to go.

Nine at the top: Bestowing a carrying bar upon the king [?]. Great good fortune; nothing is unfavorable.

Thus, understanding the Way of Heaven and discerning the circumstances of the people, they brought forth divine objects to guide the people’s use of them. With these, the sages purified themselves and observed abstinence, making their virtue spiritually luminous. Now …

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
德夫
履以和行謙以制禮復以自知恒以一德
損以遠害益以興利困以寡怨井以辨
義巽以行權
書
詩言志歌永言聲依永律和聲
若作酒醴爾惟麴糵若作和羹爾惟鹽梅
天壽平格保乂有殷
惟公懋德克勤小物弼亮四世正色率下
罔不祗師言嘉績多于先王予小子垂
===
拱仰成
詩
羔裘如濡洵直且侯彼其之子舍命不渝
羔裘豹飾孔武有力彼其之子邦之司
直羔裘晏兮三英粲兮彼其之子邦之
彥兮
子孫其湛其湛曰樂各奏爾能賓載手仇
室人入又酌彼康爵以奏爾時
相在爾室尚不愧于屋漏
punctuated:
德夫！

履以和行，謙以制禮，復以自知，恒以一德，損以遠害，益以興利，困以寡怨，井以辨義，巽以行權。

書

詩言志，歌永言，聲依永，律和聲。

若作酒醴，爾惟麴糵；若作和羹，爾惟鹽梅。天壽平格，保乂有殷。

惟公懋德，克勤小物，弼亮四世，正色率下，罔不祗師言。嘉績多于先王，予小子垂拱仰成。

詩

羔裘如濡，洵直且侯。彼其之子，舍命不渝。羔裘豹飾，孔武有力。彼其之子，邦之司直。羔裘晏兮，三英粲兮。彼其之子，邦之彥兮。

子孫其湛，其湛曰樂。各奏爾能，賓載手仇，室人入又。酌彼康爵，以奏爾時。

相在爾室，尚不愧于屋漏。
translation_en:
…virtue indeed!

Through Treading (Lü), one brings harmony to conduct; through Modesty (Qian), one regulates ritual propriety; through Return (Fu), one knows oneself; through Constancy (Heng), one makes virtue steadfast; through Decrease (Sun), one keeps harm at a distance; through Increase (Yi), one promotes benefits; through Oppression (Kun), one lessens resentment; through the Well (Jing), one distinguishes what is right; and through the Gentle (Xun), one exercises discretion.

Book of Documents

Poetry expresses intent; song prolongs the words; musical notes follow their prolongation; and the pitch standards harmonize the notes.

If I were making wine or sweet liquor, you would be the yeast and malt; if I were making a well-seasoned soup, you would be the salt and sour plums. Heaven would grant long life, peace would arrive, and the Yin dynasty would be preserved and well governed.

You, Duke, have diligently cultivated virtue, attending even to small matters. You have assisted and guided four generations of rulers, leading your subordinates with a dignified countenance; none has failed respectfully to follow your words. Your splendid achievements under the former kings have been many. I, the young one, sit with robes hanging down and hands folded, relying upon you to accomplish good government.

Book of Odes

His lambskin robe gleams as though moist;
Truly upright is he, and fine.
That man
Will give his life without wavering.
His lambskin robe is trimmed with leopard fur;
He is mighty in martial prowess and strength.
That man
Upholds rectitude in the state.
How splendid his lambskin robe!
Its three ornaments shine brightly.
That man
Is an outstanding worthy of the state.

The sons and grandsons delight in drink;
Their enjoyment is joyous indeed.
Each of you, display your ability.
The guests take partners for toasting [?];
The household members enter and return the toast [?].
Fill that great cup,
And present it at the proper time.

Look to your conduct within your chamber:
May you have nothing to be ashamed of even in its darkest corner.

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
侯亞侯伯侯旅侯彊侯以有喰其饁
思媚其婦有依其士有略其耜俶載南
畝
春秋
冬州公如曹〔桓公五年〕
鄭伯以璧假許田〔桓公元年〕　晉人納捷
菑于邾弗克納〔文公十有四年〕
鄭公孫舍之帥師侵宋　公會晉侯宋公
衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒子邾子滕子薛
===
伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭　秋七月己未同
盟于亳城北　公至自伐鄭　楚子鄭
伯伐宋　公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊
世子光莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾
子伐鄭會于蕭魚　公至自會　楚人
執鄭行人良霄〔俱襄公十有一年〕
春王正月舍中軍〔昭公五年〕
禮記
是故禮者君之大柄也所以別嫌明微儐
punctuated:
侯亞，侯伯，侯旅，侯彊，侯以，有喰其饁。思媚其婦，有依其士。有略其耜，俶載南畝。

春秋
冬，州公如曹〔桓公五年〕。
鄭伯以璧假許田〔桓公元年〕。晉人納捷菑于邾，弗克納〔文公十有四年〕。
鄭公孫舍之帥師侵宋。公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭。秋七月己未，同盟于亳城北。公至自伐鄭。楚子、鄭伯伐宋。公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚。公至自會。楚人執鄭行人良霄〔俱襄公十有一年〕。
春，王正月，舍中軍〔昭公五年〕。

禮記
是故禮者，君之大柄也，所以別嫌、明微、儐
translation_en:
…the overseers, the elders, the field workers, the strong men, and their helpers: they eat the meals brought to the fields [?]. Affectionate are their wives; dependable are their men. Sharp are their plowshares as they begin work in the southern fields.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In winter, the duke of Zhou went to Cao. 〔Fifth year of Duke Huan.〕
The earl of Zheng used a jade disk to obtain the loan of the fields of Xu. 〔First year of Duke Huan.〕 Men of Jin attempted to install Jiezi in Zhu but were unable to do so. 〔Fourteenth year of Duke Wen.〕
Gongsun Shezhi of Zheng led an army to invade Song. The duke of Lu joined the marquis of Jin, the duke of Song, the marquis of Wei, the earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the earls of Xue and Qi, and the viscount of Lesser Zhu in attacking Zheng. In autumn, on the jiwei day of the seventh month, they jointly swore a covenant north of Bocheng. The duke returned from the attack on Zheng. The viscount of Chu and the earl of Zheng attacked Song. The duke joined the marquis of Jin, the duke of Song, the marquis of Wei, the earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the earls of Xue and Qi, and the viscount of Lesser Zhu in attacking Zheng; they assembled at Xiaoyu. The duke returned from the meeting. Men of Chu seized Liang Xiao, the envoy of Zheng. 〔All in the eleventh year of Duke Xiang.〕
In spring, in the first month according to the royal calendar, the Central Army was abolished. 〔Fifth year of Duke Zhao.〕

Book of Rites
Thus ritual is the ruler’s great instrument of authority: by it he distinguishes doubtful matters, makes subtle distinctions clear, and receives as guests …

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
鬼神者制度別仁義所以治政安君也
禮時爲大順次之體次之宜次之稱次之
小大相成終始相生倡和清濁迭相爲經
溫良者仁之本也敬愼者仁之地也寬裕
者仁之作也孫接者仁之能也禮節者
仁之貌也言談者仁之文也歌樂者仁
之和也分散者仁之施也儒皆兼此而
有之猶且不敢言仁也其尊讓有如此
者
===
第貳塲
論
王天下有三重
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢置三老孝悌力田常員詔〔文帝十一〕
年
擬唐以左光祿大夫陳叔達爲禮部尚書
誥〔貞觀六年〕
擬宋詔貸江州義門陳兢粟謝表〔淳化元〕
punctuated:
鬼神者，制度，別仁義，所以治政安君也。
禮，時爲大，順次之，體次之，宜次之，稱次之。
小大相成，終始相生，倡和清濁，迭相爲經。
溫良者，仁之本也；敬愼者，仁之地也；寬裕者，仁之作也；孫接者，仁之能也；禮節者，仁之貌也；言談者，仁之文也；歌樂者，仁之和也；分散者，仁之施也。儒皆兼此而有之，猶且不敢言仁也，其尊讓有如此者。
第貳塲
論
王天下有三重。
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢置三老孝悌力田常員詔〔文帝十一〕年。
擬唐以左光祿大夫陳叔達爲禮部尚書誥〔貞觀六年〕。
擬宋詔貸江州義門陳兢粟謝表〔淳化元〕
translation_en:
…ghosts and spirits; [examining?] institutions and distinguishing benevolence from righteousness: these are the means of ordering government and securing the ruler. [?]
In ritual, timeliness is paramount; compliance comes next, then embodied form, then appropriateness, then proportion.
The small and the great complete one another; endings and beginnings generate one another. Leading and responding, clear and deep tones, alternately serve as the guiding pattern.
Warmth and goodness are the root of benevolence; reverence and caution are its foundation; generosity and magnanimity are its expression in action; humble dealings with others are its capacity; ritual observances are its outward appearance; speech and conversation are its embellishment; song and music are its harmony; distributing one's possessions is its beneficence. The Confucian scholar possesses all these qualities together, yet still dares not claim to be benevolent. Such is his reverence and modesty.
Second Session
Discourse
“One who rules All-under-Heaven has three weighty responsibilities.”
Edicts, Letters of Appointment, and Memorials 〔One question in this category [?]〕
Compose an edict in the voice of a Han emperor establishing regular posts for the Thrice Venerable, the Filially Pious and Fraternally Dutiful, and the Diligent Farmers. 〔Emperor Wen, eleventh〕 year.
Compose a Tang letter of appointment making Chen Shuda, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left, Minister of Rites. 〔Sixth year of Zhenguan〕
Compose a Song memorial of thanks for an imperial edict lending grain to Chen Jing of the Righteous Household in Jiangzhou. 〔First year of Chunhua…〕

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
年
判語五條
官員赴任過限
任所置買田宅
致祭祀典神祇
縱放軍人歇役
失時不修隄防
第叁場
策五道
===
問戎者國之大事帝王不得已而用之三
代兵法至周愈備漢唐宋諸君因革損
益各隨所宜不知其法果合于古而亦
可行于今否歟我
太祖定鼎金陵設府建衛命諸臣議教練之律
太宗建都燕京纘承先業增置各營外衛官軍
更番京操具得居重馭輕之道二者可
悉言歟其後又有十團營之設不知其
法議于何人而亦何所見歟中間廢置
punctuated:
年。

判語五條：官員赴任過限；任所置買田宅；致祭祀典神祇；縱放軍人歇役；失時不修隄防。

第叁場
策五道

問：戎者，國之大事，帝王不得已而用之。三代兵法，至周愈備。漢唐宋諸君因革損益，各隨所宜。不知其法果合于古，而亦可行于今否歟？我太祖定鼎金陵，設府建衛，命諸臣議教練之律；太宗建都燕京，纘承先業，增置各營，外衛官軍更番京操，具得居重馭輕之道。二者可悉言歟？其後又有十團營之設，不知其法議于何人，而亦何所見歟？中間廢置
translation_en:
…year.

Five legal judgments:
An official exceeding the prescribed time for reporting to his post; purchasing land and houses at one’s place of appointment; offering sacrifices to deities listed in the sacrificial canon; allowing soldiers to take leave from duty without authorization; failing to repair dikes and embankments at the proper time.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: Warfare is a great affair of state, and emperors and kings resort to it only when they have no alternative. The military institutions of the Three Dynasties became increasingly complete under the Zhou. The rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song retained or altered, reduced or expanded them as circumstances required. Did their institutions truly accord with antiquity, and could they also be implemented today?

Our Taizu established his capital at Jinling, instituted military commissions and guards, and ordered his ministers to deliberate on regulations for military training. Taizong established his capital at Yanjing, continued the undertaking of his predecessor, and established additional camps. Officers and soldiers of the provincial guards took turns drilling at the capital. Both arrangements embodied the principle of concentrating strength at the center to control the less powerful forces outside it. Can you explain both in detail?

Later, the Ten Regimental Camps were established. Who proposed this system, and what considerations informed it? In the intervening period, there were abolitions and reestablishments…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
卒增爲十二營法愈備而制愈精矣在
營之兵月支歲計糧費不貲一遇有警
則營多缺伍而將乏調用可無法以處
之歟況近者大同之變雖幸而仰仗
天威遂以平定然不知何以爲經久之計常治
之策歟爲臣子者思患預防之謀自不
容已諸生尚悉言之以觀經濟之學
問讀史所以考見理亂興衰是非同異之
故而折衷之以施諸行事也若尋行數
===
墨既讀之後與未讀無異則亦何貴於
讀史也今未暇悉舉姑即一二疑似者
與多士籌之鄴下之議與隆中之論孰
優淮肥之捷與澶淵之役孰是給貶欽
若與詔除丁謂其心同歟抗論揚億與
力排牛僧孺其說類歟錢學士之致仕
與二疏請老得失何歸王子明之平章
與王曾相業優劣奚辨不欲人主預聞
善惡之筆似矣何又有大臣日録抄送
punctuated:
卒增爲十二營，法愈備而制愈精矣。在營之兵，月支歲計，糧費不貲；一遇有警，則營多缺伍，而將乏調用，可無法以處之歟？況近者大同之變，雖幸而仰仗天威，遂以平定，然不知何以爲經久之計、常治之策歟？爲臣子者，思患預防之謀，自不容已。諸生尚悉言之，以觀經濟之學。

問：讀史所以考見理亂興衰、是非同異之故，而折衷之，以施諸行事也。若尋行數墨，既讀之後，與未讀無異，則亦何貴於讀史也？今未暇悉舉，姑即一二疑似者，與多士籌之。鄴下之議與隆中之論，孰優？淮肥之捷與澶淵之役，孰是？給貶欽若與詔除丁謂，其心同歟？抗論揚億與力排牛僧孺，其說類歟？錢學士之致仕與二疏請老，得失何歸？王子明之平章與王曾相業，優劣奚辨？不欲人主預聞善惡之筆，似矣，何又有大臣日録抄送
translation_en:
…eventually they were increased to twelve camps, making the regulations ever more complete and the organization ever more refined. For the troops in these camps, monthly disbursements and annual accounts involve enormous expenditure on grain. Yet whenever an alarm arises, many camp units are under strength, and commanders lack troops available for deployment. Can there be no method for dealing with this? Moreover, although the recent disturbance at Datong was fortunately pacified through reliance on imperial might, what plan will secure enduring stability, and what policy will ensure lasting order? Those who serve as subjects cannot cease devising ways to anticipate troubles and forestall them. You candidates should explain these matters fully, so that we may assess your learning in statecraft.

Question: Reading history enables us to examine the causes of order and disorder, rise and decline, right and wrong, agreement and difference, and to arrive at sound judgments for application in practical affairs. If one merely follows the lines and counts the written characters, remaining no different after reading from what one was before, what value is there in reading history? There is no time now to enumerate every case; let us take one or two doubtful instances and consider them with you candidates. Which was superior: the deliberation at Yexia or the discussion at Longzhong? Which was the sounder course: the victory at Huai-Fei or the campaign at Chanyuan? Did the demotion of Qinruo [?] and the appointment of Ding Wei by imperial edict arise from the same intention? Were the arguments in the outspoken criticism of Yang Yi and the vigorous opposition to Niu Sengru similar? How should we judge the merits and faults of Academician Qian’s retirement and the two Shu officials’ requests to retire? How can we distinguish the relative merits of Wang Ziming’s service as chief councillor and Wang Zeng’s achievements in that office? It seems reasonable that the ruler should not be informed in advance of what historians write concerning good and evil. Why, then, were there daily records kept by high officials that were copied and sent…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
史館者乎不欲後世盡信史官之言固
矣何又有額命大事深疑戳斧者乎儀
度俊雅一見而擢秘書者何獨傾心於
貌陋之士責直取名不察而疑唐楨者
何獨鑒別於妬嫉之臣出補淮陽與以
宋均爲尚書令微意何存召歸諫院與
留賈充爲車騎將軍其故安在即日就
道忠矣而因人之言戎服登舟者謂非
忠絶不言兵智矣而既歸廬山銳然起
===
用者似非智邊臣之陷驍將或謂其同
華合比之術黄歇之代子芊或謂其襲
呂不韋之計有諫止遷都之行者或謂
與邵彤獻策同心有決遷占城之意者
或謂與張子房從漢同志則夫實錄不
敗數字誠直筆也乃至有諱婦翁之惡
而乞罷春秋科者何耶兄在中書遽求
外補誠見幾也乃至有以婦兄之親而
引入爲侍郎者何耶遣歸宋使亦曰追
punctuated: 史館者乎？不欲後世盡信史官之言，固矣，何又有額命大事、深疑戳斧者乎？儀度俊雅，一見而擢秘書者，何獨傾心於貌陋之士？責直取名，不察而疑唐楨者，何獨鑒別於妬嫉之臣？出補淮陽與以宋均爲尚書令，微意何存？召歸諫院與留賈充爲車騎將軍，其故安在？即日就道，忠矣，而因人之言，戎服登舟者，謂非忠；絶不言兵，智矣，而既歸廬山，銳然起用者，似非智。邊臣之陷驍將，或謂其同華合比之術；黄歇之代子芊，或謂其襲呂不韋之計。有諫止遷都之行者，或謂與邵彤獻策同心；有決遷占城之意者，或謂與張子房從漢同志。則夫實錄不敗數字，誠直筆也，乃至有諱婦翁之惡而乞罷春秋科者，何耶？兄在中書，遽求外補，誠見幾也，乃至有以婦兄之親而引入爲侍郎者，何耶？遣歸宋使，亦曰追
translation_en:
…to the Historiographical Office? It is certainly reasonable not to wish later generations to believe everything historians say; yet why, concerning great affairs of testamentary appointment [?], are there also profound suspicions about an axe killing [?]? Why did one who promoted a man to the Palace Library at first sight for his handsome bearing and refined appearance nevertheless set his heart upon an ugly-looking scholar? Why did one who reproached frankness as a bid for fame and, without examining the matter, suspected Tang Zhen, nevertheless discern the character of a jealous minister? What subtle intentions lay behind sending someone out to serve in Huaiyang and appointing Song Jun Director of the Department of State Affairs? What reasons lay behind recalling someone to the Remonstrance Bureau and retaining Jia Chong as General of Chariots and Cavalry? Setting out that very day was loyal; yet someone who, following another’s advice, boarded a boat in military dress was called disloyal. Never discussing military affairs was wise; yet someone who, after returning to Mount Lu, eagerly resumed office seems to have been unwise.

Some say that a frontier official’s entrapment of a valiant general employed the same technique as “Hua’s forming a clique” [?]; some say that Huang Xie’s substitution for Zi Qian [?] copied Lü Buwei’s scheme. Of one who remonstrated to stop the relocation of the capital, some say that his intentions matched those of Shao Tong when offering his plan. Of one determined to relocate to Zhancheng, some say that his aspirations matched those of Zhang Zifang in following the Han. Now, faithfully recording the few words “not defeated” was indeed honest historical writing; yet how could there also be someone who concealed his father-in-law’s wrongdoing and petitioned to abolish the examination category on the Spring and Autumn Annals? Seeking an outside appointment immediately because one’s elder brother was serving in the Secretariat certainly showed discernment of the first signs of trouble; yet how could there also be someone who brought a man into office as Vice Minister because he was his wife’s elder brother? Sending the Song envoy home was likewise said to follow in the footsteps…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
蹤於蘇武隱居終南果能媲美於子陵
徙豪傑於茂陵而四豪之遊何以未除
詔典領五經而九流七畧何以不去倡
豐亨豫大之說與統領花石殊乎養夷
狄腥膻之類與幽沉仁義異乎凡此諸
士子讀史之餘當有折衷之說請著于
篇以觀稽古之學
問禦戎莫重于兵而用兵莫急于馬成周
之世天子諸侯大夫皆有馬載之周禮
者可考也漢之馬政復古法令日嚴消
耗日甚及于唐創置坊監馬得蕃息今
其地固在也可得指而言歟抑可講求
而修復之歟宋之保馬之法爲害於民
其弊安在我
朝陝西遼東設有寺監政爲周備其後裁省
以致牧馬之地散之于民不能復舊今
可得其法歟原額牧馬草場且有頃畝
後漸消沒養馬軍數後漸缺乏此豈無
punctuated:
蹤於蘇武，隱居終南，果能媲美於子陵？徙豪傑於茂陵，而四豪之遊何以未除？詔典領五經，而九流七畧何以不去？倡豐亨豫大之說，與統領花石殊乎？養夷狄腥膻之類，與幽沉仁義異乎？凡此，諸士子讀史之餘，當有折衷之說，請著于篇，以觀稽古之學。
問：禦戎莫重于兵，而用兵莫急于馬。成周之世，天子、諸侯、大夫皆有馬，載之《周禮》者可考也。漢之馬政復古，法令日嚴，消耗日甚。及于唐，創置坊監，馬得蕃息。今其地固在也，可得指而言歟？抑可講求而修復之歟？宋之保馬之法，爲害於民，其弊安在？我朝陝西、遼東設有寺監，政爲周備。其後裁省，以致牧馬之地散之于民，不能復舊。今可得其法歟？原額牧馬草場，且有頃畝，後漸消沒；養馬軍數，後漸缺乏。此豈無
translation_en:
…in the footsteps of Su Wu. In retiring to Zhongnan, could he truly rival Ziling? Eminent and powerful men were moved to Maoling; why, then, were associations with the four eminent men not eliminated? An edict ordered the administration of the Five Classics; why, then, were the Nine Schools and Seven Summaries not discarded? Was advocating the doctrine of abundant prosperity and magnificent grandeur any different from supervising the collection of flowers and ornamental rocks? Was nurturing those rank-smelling barbarians any different from consigning benevolence and righteousness to oblivion? On all these matters, you candidates should, after reading history, have a considered judgment to offer. Please set it down in writing, so that we may assess your learning in the investigation of antiquity.
Question: In resisting foreign peoples, nothing matters more than troops; in employing troops, nothing is more urgent than horses. In the age of Zhou, the Son of Heaven, the feudal lords, and the grandees all possessed horses. The accounts recorded in the Rites of Zhou can be examined. Horse administration under the Han restored ancient practices, yet as laws and regulations grew stricter by the day, losses grew ever greater. Under the Tang, breeding establishments and supervisory directorates were newly established, and horses multiplied. Those lands surely still exist today: can you identify and discuss them? Or might the arrangements be investigated and restored? The Song system of household horse keeping harmed the people. Where did its defects lie? Our dynasty established courts and directorates for horse administration in Shaanxi and Liaodong, making comprehensive administrative provision. Subsequently, these institutions were reduced or abolished, so that horse pastures were dispersed among the people and the former arrangements could not be restored. Can a method for doing so now be found? The originally allotted horse pastures had their areas recorded in qing and mu, yet these gradually disappeared; the complement of soldiers assigned to rear horses likewise gradually fell short. Can this be without…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
故歟如之何可以復補之歟夫徒耗養
馬之費遇變而無可用之馬可無法以
處之歟有謂增種馬及牧軍者不知合
祖宗之法否歟是皆邊方之急務爾諸士宜究
心者可慎言之毋畧
問言之不文行之不遠文者聖賢之所不
廢也六經尚矣左氏傳國語戰國策皆
先秦古文也乃有作非國語及左氏浮
誇戰國策縱横捭闔之許何歟昔人謂
===
三代之文至戰國而病其然歟班固氏
謂大漢之文炳焉與三代同風矣賈誼
董仲舒司馬相如尤西京之傑然者也
或謂治安策失之疎上林子虛賦失之
靡三策失之緩何歟孟堅之言可盡信
歟晋宋以來之文唐宋爲盛唐以文名
家者多矣而起八代之衰者何以獨歸
之韓昌黎氏歟宋西崑之體亦奇矣歐
陽氏乃痛抑茁軋之句其意何歟我
punctuated:
故歟？如之何可以復補之歟？夫徒耗養馬之費，遇變而無可用之馬，可無法以處之歟？有謂增種馬及牧軍者，不知合祖宗之法否歟？是皆邊方之急務，爾諸士宜究心者，可慎言之，毋畧。
問：言之不文，行之不遠。文者，聖賢之所不廢也。六經尚矣，《左氏傳》《國語》《戰國策》皆先秦古文也。乃有作《非國語》及左氏浮誇、戰國策縱横捭闔之許，何歟？昔人謂三代之文至戰國而病，其然歟？班固氏謂大漢之文炳焉，與三代同風矣。賈誼、董仲舒、司馬相如，尤西京之傑然者也。或謂《治安策》失之疎，《上林》《子虛》賦失之靡，三策失之緩，何歟？孟堅之言可盡信歟？晋宋以來之文，唐宋爲盛。唐以文名家者多矣，而起八代之衰者，何以獨歸之韓昌黎氏歟？宋西崑之體亦奇矣，歐陽氏乃痛抑茁軋之句，其意何歟？我
translation_en:
…without a cause? How can these be restored and replenished? If funds for raising horses are merely squandered, yet no horses are available for use when an emergency arises, can we dispense with measures to address this? Some propose increasing the numbers of breeding horses and military herdsmen; would this accord with the institutions of our imperial ancestors? These are all urgent matters for the frontier, to which you candidates should give careful thought. Discuss them thoughtfully, omitting nothing.
Question: “If words lack literary refinement, they will not travel far.” Literary refinement is something the sages and worthies never dispensed with. The Six Classics stand supreme. The Zuo Commentary, Discourses of the States, and Strategies of the Warring States are all ancient writings from before the Qin. Yet someone wrote Critique of the Discourses of the States, and there are assessments [?] that the Zuo Commentary is extravagant and exaggerated, and that Strategies of the Warring States concerns diplomatic maneuvering and persuasive manipulation. Why is this? A writer of former times said that the literature of the Three Dynasties became diseased by the Warring States period. Was this so? Ban Gu said that the literature of the great Han shone brilliantly, sharing the spirit of the Three Dynasties. Jia Yi, Dong Zhongshu, and Sima Xiangru were especially outstanding figures of the Western Han. Some, however, say that the Policy Essay on Order and Security is deficient in precision, that the rhapsodies Shanglin Park and Master Zixu are excessively ornate, and that the Three Policy Responses are too dilatory. Why is this? Can the words of Mengjian [Ban Gu] be trusted entirely? Among the writings produced since the Jin and Liu Song, those of the Tang and Song flourished most. Many Tang writers attained distinction in literature; why, then, is Han Changli [Han Yu] alone credited with reversing the decline of eight dynasties? The Song dynasty’s Xikun style was also remarkable, yet Ouyang [Xiu] vehemently rejected its awkwardly contorted phrases [?]. What was his intention? Our …

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
國家以文取士崇雅黜浮百餘年來文章彬彬
彬乎盛矣然邇來枝葉茂而本根微視
昔不能無少變焉識者憂之
皇上屢勤
詔諭欲變時習而還爾雅天下固將翕然丕變
乎然亦有未盡變者何歟茲欲一洗時
文之陋本之六經駕漢唐宋而出其上
如何而後可也
問理財者立國之大經故傳曰生之者衆
===
食之者寡爲之者疾用之者舒此固萬
世理財之大道也不知於周人九賦斂
財賄九式均節財用之法合歟否歟後
世理財之說不遺餘算若漢之計相唐
之度支宋之計省當時經費盈縮之數
與夫取民多寡之制果有合於古而裕
於用否歟唐陸贄嘗有豐財之說李翱
嘗有平賦之書其亦有所本歟方今府
庫空虛黎氏凋瘵可謂公私俱困矣宋
punctuated:
國家以文取士，崇雅黜浮，百餘年來文章彬彬彬乎盛矣。然邇來枝葉茂而本根微，視昔不能無少變焉，識者憂之。皇上屢勤詔諭，欲變時習而還爾雅，天下固將翕然丕變乎？然亦有未盡變者，何歟？茲欲一洗時文之陋，本之六經，駕漢唐宋而出其上，如何而後可也？

問：理財者，立國之大經。故傳曰：「生之者衆，食之者寡，爲之者疾，用之者舒。」此固萬世理財之大道也。不知於周人九賦斂財賄、九式均節財用之法，合歟否歟？後世理財之說，不遺餘算。若漢之計相、唐之度支、宋之計省，當時經費盈縮之數，與夫取民多寡之制，果有合於古而裕於用否歟？唐陸贄嘗有豐財之說，李翱嘗有平賦之書，其亦有所本歟？方今府庫空虛，黎氏凋瘵，可謂公私俱困矣。宋
translation_en:
…Our dynasty selects men for office through literary composition, honoring refinement and rejecting superficiality. For more than a hundred years, writing has flourished in cultivated splendor. Yet recently its branches and leaves have grown luxuriant while its roots have weakened. Compared with earlier times, it has undergone some change, which troubles discerning observers. His Majesty has repeatedly taken pains to issue edicts, seeking to transform prevailing habits and restore correctness and refinement. Surely all under Heaven should respond together with a great transformation? Yet some have still not fully changed. Why is this? If we now wish to sweep away the defects of contemporary examination prose, ground it in the Six Classics, and surpass the writing of the Han, Tang, and Song, how can this be achieved?

Question: Managing wealth is a fundamental principle of establishing a state. Thus the commentary says: “Let those who produce it be many and those who consume it few; let those who make it work swiftly and those who spend it do so slowly.” This is indeed the great way of managing wealth for all ages. But does it accord with the Zhou methods of collecting wealth and goods through the nine levies and regulating expenditure equitably through the nine standards? Later generations’ discussions of financial management left no calculation unconsidered. Consider the Han Fiscal Chancellor, the Tang Bureau of Revenue, and the Song Finance Commission: did their balances of revenue and expenditure, and their rules governing how much was exacted from the people, truly accord with antiquity while providing ample resources for use? Lu Zhi of the Tang once advanced proposals for increasing wealth, and Li Ao wrote on equalizing taxation. Did these, too, have a foundation in earlier principles? Today the treasuries and storehouses are empty, and the common people [?; the transcription reads 黎氏] are impoverished and afflicted. It may well be said that public and private resources alike are exhausted. In the Song…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
司馬光所謂不在官則在民之言非歟
無亦有耗財之事非光之所能悉究歟
玆欲稍蠲民租以振其窮而又使
國用無乏諸士子當必有稽古之策也其詳
言之毋隱
punctuated: 司馬光所謂「不在官則在民」之言非歟？無亦有耗財之事，非光之所能悉究歟？玆欲稍蠲民租以振其窮，而又使國用無乏，諸士子當必有稽古之策也，其詳言之，毋隱。
translation_en: …was Sima Guang’s statement that “what is not held by the government is held by the people” mistaken? Might there also be activities that deplete wealth which Guang could not fully investigate? We now wish to remit some of the people’s taxes to relieve their poverty, while also ensuring that funds for state expenditure do not fall short. You candidates surely have proposals grounded in a study of antiquity. Set them forth in detail, withholding nothing.

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人九十五名
第一名周　儒　吉安府學增廣生　易
第二名蕭希曜　泰和縣學附學生　書
第三名余文獻　九江府學生　詩
第四名湯惟允　安仁縣學生　禮記
第五名朱　璜　新淦縣學生　春秋
第六名黃　朏　豐城縣學增廣生　易
第七名陳九成　樂平縣學生　詩
===
第八名徐良傅　撫州府學生　書
第九名王子清　寧州學生　春秋
第十名陸夢豹　豐城縣學增廣生　詩
第十一名賴朝陽　萬安縣學生　易
第十二名熊　炅　新建縣學生　書
第十三名王　治　清江縣學生　詩
第十四名劉逢愷　泰和縣學生　易
第十五名趙安卿　弋陽縣學生　書
第十六名馬　泗　建昌府學生　詩
punctuated:
中式舉人九十五名。

第一名周　儒，吉安府學增廣生，易。第二名蕭希曜，泰和縣學附學生，書。第三名余文獻，九江府學生，詩。第四名湯惟允，安仁縣學生，禮記。第五名朱　璜，新淦縣學生，春秋。第六名黃　朏，豐城縣學增廣生，易。第七名陳九成，樂平縣學生，詩。第八名徐良傅，撫州府學生，書。第九名王子清，寧州學生，春秋。第十名陸夢豹，豐城縣學增廣生，詩。第十一名賴朝陽，萬安縣學生，易。第十二名熊　炅，新建縣學生，書。第十三名王　治，清江縣學生，詩。第十四名劉逢愷，泰和縣學生，易。第十五名趙安卿，弋陽縣學生，書。第十六名馬　泗，建昌府學生，詩。
translation_en:
Ninety-five successful candidates qualifying as provincial graduates (juren).

門人於聖人之閒居而必記其容色焉蓋聖人一身道之所寓也其於燕居從容中道焉自有不期然而然者矣昔吾夫子之在魯也名通朝籍身爲世家想當大庭初下之時政務暫解於攝行而優游可以自適門墻清晏固將托之爲偃息矣太廟既出之後禮文不勞於每問而從

同考試官教諭戴批：此題容色二字，作者類不能分別，惟此篇獨有條理，非素有沉潛之功者不能卒到。
同考試官教諭趙批：文體老成，語意峻潔，善形容聖人氣象者。
考試官教諭陳批：論語義似易實難，此作可謂體認親切矣。
考試官學正楊批：語明意足。

門人於聖人之閒居，而必記其容色焉。蓋聖人一身，道之所寓也。其於燕居，從容中道焉，自有不期然而然者矣。昔吾夫子之在魯也，名通朝籍，身爲世家。想當大庭初下之時，政務暫解於攝行，而優游可以自適；門墻清晏，固將托之爲偃息矣。太廟既出之後，禮文不勞於每問，而從
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“When the Master was at leisure, his bearing was relaxed and his expression cheerful.”
Zhou Ru

Comment by Associate Examiner Dai, Instructor: In treating this topic, writers generally fail to distinguish the two terms, bodily bearing and facial expression. This essay alone handles them in an orderly way. Without long practice in deep reflection, one could not attain this all at once.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor: The style is mature, the language and thought forceful and clean. This is a writer skilled at depicting the sage’s presence.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: Discussing the meaning of the Analects seems easy but is actually difficult. This composition may be said to embody an intimate understanding.

Comment by Examiner Yang, School Director: The language is clear and the meaning fully expressed.

When recording the sage’s life at leisure, his disciples invariably noted his bearing and expression. For the sage’s person is where the Way resides. In his hours of leisure, his unhurried conduct accorded with the Way: this happened naturally, without any intention of making it so.

Formerly, when our Master was in Lu, his name was entered on the court rolls, and he belonged to an eminent family. Imagine him just withdrawing from the great court: temporarily relieved of the governmental duties he was performing, he could take his ease and enjoy himself. Within his gates all was quiet and peaceful; surely he would make this his place of repose. After leaving the Grand Ancestral Temple, the details of ritual no longer required him to ask about every matter, and his ease …

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
容過於私門室堂邃深蓋有藉之以閑燕矣斯
時也翼翼之敬既舒肅肅之容一變但見展布
於四體者血氣爲之動盪而志氣常存若無拘
也而實無累也若無事也而實無怠也中正之
所敷宣形神與之俱妙矣自我而觀殆申申如
也申申之外不能有所言而亦不能有所見也
發舒於面目者清明爲之呈露而神明自全若
可望也而亦可親也若可敬也而亦可愛也和
平之所蘊藉光輝自爾宣著矣自予而言殆天
===
夭如也夭夭之外不可得而名而亦不可得而
知也孔門弟子可謂善觀聖人者矣亦可謂善
言德行者矣抑論聖人之道猶天然善言天者
有曰雨露雪霜無非教也今夫燕居所記鄉黨
所書其所以教天下教後世者至矣雖然此特
吾夫子安常處順中和之氣象耳受圍於匡絃
誦不絕伐木於宋微服而過其間氣象尤有學
教存焉學者誠能羹墻而寤寐之其殆庶幾矣
乎
punctuated: 容過於私門，室堂邃深，蓋有藉之以閑燕矣。斯時也，翼翼之敬既舒，肅肅之容一變，但見展布於四體者，血氣爲之動盪，而志氣常存。若無拘也，而實無累也；若無事也，而實無怠也。中正之所敷宣，形神與之俱妙矣。自我而觀，殆申申如也。申申之外，不能有所言，而亦不能有所見也。發舒於面目者，清明爲之呈露，而神明自全。若可望也，而亦可親也；若可敬也，而亦可愛也。和平之所蘊藉，光輝自爾宣著矣。自予而言，殆天夭如也。夭夭之外，不可得而名，而亦不可得而知也。孔門弟子可謂善觀聖人者矣，亦可謂善言德行者矣。抑論聖人之道，猶天然。善言天者有曰：「雨露雪霜，無非教也。」今夫燕居所記，鄉黨所書，其所以教天下、教後世者至矣。雖然，此特吾夫子安常處順中和之氣象耳。受圍於匡，絃誦不絕；伐木於宋，微服而過。其間氣象，尤有學教存焉。學者誠能羹墻而寤寐之，其殆庶幾矣乎？
translation_en: …at ease, he passed through the gate of his private residence. Its chambers and halls were deep and secluded, providing a place for quiet repose. At such a time, his vigilant reverence relaxed, and his solemn bearing changed completely. One saw only how, as ease spread through his limbs, his blood and vital energies stirred freely, while his purposeful spirit remained constant. He seemed unconstrained, yet was truly free of encumbrance; he seemed unoccupied, yet was truly free of indolence. As centrality and correctness unfolded, his bodily form and spirit alike attained a wondrous state. To my eyes, he was indeed “relaxed in manner.” Beyond “relaxed,” nothing further could be said, nor could anything further be discerned. What unfolded in his face allowed clarity and brightness to manifest themselves, while his spiritual luminosity remained whole of itself. He seemed worthy of being gazed upon, yet also approachable; worthy of reverence, yet also lovable. From the harmony and serenity harbored within, radiance naturally shone forth. In my words, he was indeed “cheerful in countenance” [?]. Beyond “cheerful,” nothing further could be named, nor could anything further be known. The disciples of Confucius may indeed be called skilled observers of the sage, and skilled describers of virtuous conduct. Moreover, the Way of the sage is like Heaven. One who spoke well of Heaven said: “Rain, dew, snow, and frost—none is without instruction.” Now, what is recorded of his life at leisure, and what is written in “Xiangdang” (Village Life), reaches the utmost in teaching the world and later generations. Even so, this is merely the appearance of equilibrium and harmony displayed by our Master while resting in ordinary circumstances and dwelling amid favorable conditions. When surrounded at Kuang, he continued playing the strings and reciting without interruption; when the tree was felled in Song, he passed on in plain clothes. His bearing in these circumstances contains still further lessons for study [?]. If students could truly keep him before them as though seeing him in their soup and against the wall, contemplating him waking and sleeping, might they not come close to attaining this?

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
中也者天下之大本也和也者天下之達
道也
熊炅
同考試官教諭高　批　此題不難於富麗而難於
切實此作發揮大本達道處不假雕琢而意自足
是究心於理學者
同考試官教諭蘇　批　理明而詞順是亦文之中
和者也
考試官教諭陳　批　說理精到
===
考試官學正　批　善作中庸義者
中庸指性情之德爲道之體用以見道之不可
離也夫性情人之所必有也而道之體用具焉
道豈可離也哉昔子思子述所傳之意以立言
至此謂夫人之所以離乎道者以道遠於人也
而不知其本於性情之德今夫喜怒哀樂情也
其未發性也方其未發無所偏倚固謂之中矣
是中也至一之地有以涵萬有之紛紜至靜之
中有以立百感之樞紐大之莫能載而小之莫
punctuated:
「中也者，天下之大本也；和也者，天下之達道也。」
熊炅
同考試官教諭高批：「此題不難於富麗，而難於切實。此作發揮大本達道處，不假雕琢而意自足，是究心於理學者。」
同考試官教諭蘇批：「理明而詞順，是亦文之中和者也。」
考試官教諭陳批：「說理精到。」
考試官學正批：「善作中庸義者。」
中庸指性情之德爲道之體用，以見道之不可離也。夫性情，人之所必有也，而道之體用具焉，道豈可離也哉？昔子思子述所傳之意以立言，至此謂夫人之所以離乎道者，以道遠於人也，而不知其本於性情之德。今夫喜怒哀樂，情也；其未發，性也。方其未發，無所偏倚，固謂之中矣。是中也，至一之地，有以涵萬有之紛紜；至靜之中，有以立百感之樞紐。大之莫能載，而小之莫
translation_en:
“Equilibrium is the great foundation of all under Heaven; harmony is the universally applicable Way of all under Heaven.”
Xiong Jiong
Associate Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: “The difficulty of this topic lies not in elaborate embellishment but in substantive precision. In expounding the great foundation and the universally applicable Way, this essay fully conveys its meaning without resorting to ornament. Its author has devoted himself to the study of principle.”
Associate Examiner Su, Instructor, comments: “The principles are clear and the language flows smoothly. This, too, is equilibrium and harmony in writing.”
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The exposition of principle is precise and thorough.”
The Examiner, a School Instructor, comments: “An accomplished writer of essays on the meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean.”
The Doctrine of the Mean identifies the virtues of human nature and the feelings as the substance and functioning of the Way, thereby showing that the Way cannot be departed from. Human nature and the feelings are necessarily possessed by everyone, and within them the substance and functioning of the Way are fully present. How, then, could the Way be departed from? In former times, Master Zisi set forth in words the meaning of the teachings transmitted to him. At this point, he meant that people depart from the Way because they consider it remote from human beings, failing to understand that it is rooted in the virtues of human nature and the feelings. Joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure are feelings; before they arise, there is human nature. Before they arise, there is no deviation or leaning to either side: this is indeed called equilibrium. This equilibrium, in its utmost unity, can encompass the teeming multiplicity of all existence; in its utmost stillness, it can establish the pivot of the hundred responses. What is so great that nothing can contain it, and what is so small that nothing …

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
能破者皆於此乎權輿也昭之顯於有而幽之
入於無者皆於此乎統會也中非天下之大本
而爲道之體耶及其旣發無所乖戾固謂之和
矣是和也率其本然之性而行無不宜充其道
心之微而施無不當達之天下合百慮而一致
蓋有由之而不知者也驗之古今曠百世而相
符未有舍之而不由者也和非天下之達道而
爲道之用耶夫中曰大本率性之道所從出也
和曰達道天命之性所由行也道不外於性情
===
而性情實統于一心道不可離夫何疑哉抑致
中和以位天地育萬物此百聖相傳之心法也
至子思之時則去聖遠而異端作大有可憂者
矣故以所得于父師者作爲中庸而首發其體
要欲學者卽吾心之動靜而交修之以會斯道
之全以續不傳之緒其衛道之心何如哉嗚呼
以此爲防後世猶有外性情而求道於虛無寂
滅者
是故君子有終身之憂無一朝之患也乃
punctuated:
能破者，皆於此乎權輿也。昭之顯於有，而幽之入於無者，皆於此乎統會也。中非天下之大本，而爲道之體耶？及其旣發，無所乖戾，固謂之和矣。是和也，率其本然之性而行，無不宜；充其道心之微而施，無不當。達之天下，合百慮而一致，蓋有由之而不知者也；驗之古今，曠百世而相符，未有舍之而不由者也。和非天下之達道，而爲道之用耶？夫中曰大本，率性之道所從出也；和曰達道，天命之性所由行也。道不外於性情，而性情實統于一心，道不可離，夫何疑哉？抑致中和，以位天地、育萬物，此百聖相傳之心法也。至子思之時，則去聖遠而異端作，大有可憂者矣。故以所得于父師者，作爲《中庸》，而首發其體要，欲學者卽吾心之動靜而交修之，以會斯道之全，以續不傳之緒。其衛道之心何如哉！嗚呼！以此爲防，後世猶有外性情而求道於虛無寂滅者。

是故君子有終身之憂，無一朝之患也。乃
translation_en:
…be split apart—all have their beginnings here. Whether manifest, appearing in the realm of being, or hidden, entering the realm of nonbeing, all are gathered together here. Is equilibrium not the great foundation of all under Heaven and the substance of the Way? Once the feelings have been aroused, if there is nothing discordant, this is indeed called harmony. Such harmony follows one’s original nature in action, so that nothing is inappropriate; it fully develops the subtle moral mind in practice, so that nothing is improper. Extended throughout the world, it brings a hundred deliberations into a single accord; indeed, some follow it without knowing it. Tested against past and present, it remains consistent across a hundred generations; none has ever discarded it and ceased to follow it. Is harmony not the universal Way of all under Heaven and the functioning of the Way?

Equilibrium is called the great foundation because it is the source from which the Way of following one’s nature proceeds. Harmony is called the universal Way because it is that through which the nature conferred by Heaven is put into practice. The Way does not lie outside human nature and feelings, and nature and feelings are truly united in the single mind. What doubt can there be that the Way cannot be departed from? Moreover, bringing equilibrium and harmony to their utmost, thereby establishing Heaven and Earth in their proper places and nourishing the myriad things, is the teaching of the mind transmitted from sage to sage. By the time of Zisi, however, the sages were remote and heterodox teachings had arisen: there was much cause for concern. Thus, drawing upon what he had received from his father and teacher, he composed the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), setting forth its essential principles at the outset. He wished learners to cultivate both the activity and the stillness of their own minds, thereby comprehending this Way in its entirety and continuing the thread of its interrupted transmission. How profound was his resolve to defend the Way! Alas! Even with this safeguard, later generations still included those who sought the Way outside human nature and feelings, in emptiness, nonbeing, and extinction.

Therefore, the gentleman has lifelong concern, but no anxiety over the troubles of a single morning. As for…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
若所憂則有之舜人也我亦人也舜爲
法於天下可傳於後世我由未免爲鄉
人也是則可憂也憂之如何如舜而已
矣若夫君子所患則亡矣非仁無爲也
非禮無行也如有一朝之患則君子不
患矣
陸夢豹
同考試官教諭尤　批　此題不難於敷衍而貴於〔整齊〕〔士子所作率多牽制錯亂惟此篇最爲得體〕
===
同考試官教諭張　批　格古而句新言約而意盡〔蓋素有定見者也〕
同考試官教諭鄭　批　君子所以有憂無患者專〔於治己而不責人務內之學也此篇發揮殆盡是〕〔當是作手〕
考試官教諭陳　批　文不求奇而自有人所不〔能到者宜置高選〕〔用錄之以爲程式〕
考試官學正楊　批　老成文字
punctuated:
若所憂，則有之：舜，人也；我，亦人也。舜爲法於天下，可傳於後世；我由未免爲鄉人也，是則可憂也。憂之如何？如舜而已矣。若夫君子所患，則亡矣。非仁無爲也，非禮無行也。如有一朝之患，則君子不患矣。

陸夢豹

同考試官教諭尤批：此題不難於敷衍，而貴於〔整齊〕〔士子所作，率多牽制錯亂，惟此篇最爲得體。〕

同考試官教諭張批：格古而句新，言約而意盡，〔蓋素有定見者也。〕

同考試官教諭鄭批：君子所以有憂無患者，專〔於治己而不責人，務內之學也。此篇發揮殆盡，是〕〔當是作手。〕

考試官教諭陳批：文不求奇，而自有人所不〔能到者，宜置高選。〕〔用錄之以爲程式。〕

考試官學正楊批：老成文字。
translation_en:
…As for what he has cause to be concerned about, there is indeed something: Shun was a human being, and I too am a human being. Shun became a model for all under Heaven, worthy of being handed down to later generations; yet I have still not risen above being an ordinary villager. This, then, is cause for concern. How should one address this concern? Simply by becoming like Shun. As for the troubles that beset the gentleman, however, there are none. He does nothing contrary to benevolence and undertakes nothing contrary to ritual propriety. Should some sudden trouble arise, the gentleman is not troubled by it.

Lu Mengbao 陸夢豹

Comment by Associate Examiner You, Instructor: “The difficulty of this topic lies not in elaboration; what matters is [orderly arrangement]. [Candidates’ compositions are mostly constrained and confused; this essay alone is especially well structured.]”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Its style is antique, yet its phrasing is fresh; its language is concise, yet its meaning is fully expressed. [This is surely someone who has long held settled views.]”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “The reason the gentleman has concerns but no troubles lies in concentrating [on governing himself without making demands on others: this is learning directed inward. This essay expounds the matter almost exhaustively. This] [must be an accomplished writer [?].]”

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “The composition does not strive for novelty, yet naturally possesses qualities that others [cannot attain. It deserves a high ranking.] [It is therefore recorded here as a model.]”

Comment by Examiner Yang, School Instructor: “Mature writing.”

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
太祖所議教練之律也今考其法指揮所轄萬
人使其武備不精一千至六千人者罰俸
有差至七千人者降級有差千戶所轄千
人以百爲限百戶所轄百人以十爲限故
當時謀臣勇將布滿京營衛皆精兵兵皆
可用雖不必盡泥諸古而巳合古人之法
矣厥後承平日久法寖以衰正統巳巳之
變虜騎衝突若履無人之境兵部尚書于
謙因軍政廢弛乃立爲十團營挑選各營
===
之精壯驍勇者充之其老瘞疲弱不堪戰
敵者退還原營謂之老家天順初年罷之
三年復置七年又罷之成化初年復置後
增爲十二營凡有征調則十營之兵以次
啓行謂之老家者廼爲宿衛守衛之用也
其法亦可謂備其制亦可謂精矣夫法久
而敝勢所必至變通之宜正在今日試以
今日團營之弊言之可謂名存實亡者矣
老瘞疲弱充斥十二則團營與老家又何
punctuated:
太祖所議教練之律也。今考其法，指揮所轄萬人，使其武備不精，一千至六千人者罰俸有差，至七千人者降級有差。千戶所轄千人，以百爲限；百戶所轄百人，以十爲限。故當時謀臣勇將布滿京營，衛皆精兵，兵皆可用。雖不必盡泥諸古，而巳合古人之法矣。
厥後承平日久，法寖以衰。正統巳巳之變，虜騎衝突，若履無人之境。兵部尚書于謙因軍政廢弛，乃立爲十團營，挑選各營之精壯驍勇者充之。其老瘞疲弱不堪戰敵者，退還原營，謂之老家。天順初年罷之，三年復置，七年又罷之。成化初年復置，後增爲十二營。凡有征調，則十營之兵以次啓行，謂之老家者廼爲宿衛守衛之用也。其法亦可謂備，其制亦可謂精矣。
夫法久而敝，勢所必至，變通之宜正在今日。試以今日團營之弊言之，可謂名存實亡者矣。老瘞疲弱充斥十二，則團營與老家又何
translation_en:
…was the statute on military training deliberated upon by Taizu. Examining its provisions now, we find that a commander had ten thousand men under his jurisdiction. If their military preparedness was deficient, he was penalized by graded forfeitures of salary when the number concerned ranged from one thousand to six thousand, and by graded demotions when it reached seven thousand. A battalion commander had one thousand men under his jurisdiction, with each hundred serving as the unit for assessing penalties; a company commander had one hundred men, with each ten serving as the unit. Thus, at that time, resourceful advisers and valiant generals filled the capital camps; every guard had crack troops, and every soldier was fit for service. Although these arrangements did not necessarily adhere rigidly to ancient practice in every respect, they already accorded with the methods of the ancients.
Afterward, as peace endured, these regulations gradually fell into decline. During the crisis of the Zhengtong reign in the year given here as sisi [?], enemy cavalry swept through as though traversing an uninhabited land. Because military administration had fallen into neglect, Minister of War Yu Qian established ten combined camps, filling them with strong and valiant men selected from the various camps. Those who were aged and infirm [?], exhausted or weak, and unfit to fight the enemy were sent back to their original camps, which were called the “old home camps.” The combined camps were abolished early in the Tianshun reign, restored in its third year, and abolished again in its seventh year. They were restored early in the Chenghua reign and later increased to twelve camps. Whenever troops were called out on campaign, the soldiers of the ten camps set out in succession, while those belonging to the so-called old home camps were employed for palace guard and garrison duties. These methods could indeed be called comprehensive, and these arrangements carefully devised.
That regulations deteriorate over time is an inevitable tendency; today is precisely the time to adapt them to changing circumstances. Consider the defects of the combined camps today: they may be said to survive in name while having ceased to exist in substance. The aged and infirm [?], exhausted and weak fill all twelve camps. Then what difference is there between the combined camps and the old home camps…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
異途一遞征調雖盡十二營而挑選之不
能百一則團營雖多又何益也近者大同
之變雖
天威震悼遂以平定然愚聞其倉卒事變之初
固有遣官募兵之令矣亦有借輸太倉之
籌矣亦有備調延綏寧夏之兵者矣夫軍
出力以衛民也民出力以養軍也今在營
之兵月食米八萬一千五百有餘石歲計
之食米九十七萬八千餘石是皆百姓之
膏血而緩急不足恃卒紛紛焉此豈
===
祖宗之法也哉
祖宗特邊儲充實士卒用命若太倉天庫之蓄
惟爲根本之防今邊塞有警運以太倉萬
一京師有事又將何以備之此非
祖宗之法也夫延綏者中原之藩籬寧夏者中
原之障蔽不可一日忘修者也今大同有
變借調延寧萬一延寧有事又將何以借
之此非
punctuated:
異？途一遞征調，雖盡十二營，而挑選之不能百一，則團營雖多，又何益也？近者大同之變，雖天威震悼，遂以平定，然愚聞其倉卒事變之初，固有遣官募兵之令矣，亦有借輸太倉之籌矣，亦有備調延綏、寧夏之兵者矣。夫軍出力以衛民也，民出力以養軍也。今在營之兵，月食米八萬一千五百有餘石，歲計之，食米九十七萬八千餘石，是皆百姓之膏血，而緩急不足恃，卒紛紛焉，此豈祖宗之法也哉？
祖宗特邊儲充實，士卒用命，若太倉天庫之蓄，惟爲根本之防。今邊塞有警，運以太倉，萬一京師有事，又將何以備之？此非祖宗之法也。夫延綏者，中原之藩籬；寧夏者，中原之障蔽，不可一日忘修者也。今大同有變，借調延寧，萬一延寧有事，又將何以借之？此非
translation_en:
…different? Whenever troops are called up for a campaign [?], even if all twelve camps are drawn upon, not one man in a hundred can be selected as fit for service. What benefit, then, is there in having so many combined training camps? During the recent disturbance at Datong, imperial might struck terror [?], and the disturbance was consequently suppressed. Yet I have heard that, when the crisis first broke out so suddenly, orders were indeed issued to dispatch officials to recruit troops; plans were also made to borrow and transport supplies from the Grand Granary; and preparations were made to call up troops from Yansui and Ningxia. Soldiers exert themselves to protect the people, and the people exert themselves to support the soldiers. The troops now in the camps consume more than 81,500 shi of rice each month, amounting to more than 978,000 shi annually. All this is the lifeblood of the common people, yet in an emergency these troops cannot be relied upon, and in the end all is confusion. Can this possibly be the system of the imperial ancestors?
The imperial ancestors ensured [?] that frontier stores were ample and that soldiers obeyed their commands. As for the reserves of the Grand Granary and the imperial treasury, these were solely for defending the heart of the realm. Now, when an alarm arises on the frontier, supplies are transported from the Grand Granary. If something should happen in the capital, what would then remain to provide for its defense? This is not the system of the imperial ancestors. Yansui is the fence protecting the Central Plain, and Ningxia its defensive barrier; their defenses must not be neglected for even a single day. Now, because a disturbance has arisen at Datong, troops are borrowed from Yansui and Ningxia. If trouble should arise in Yansui and Ningxia, from where could troops then be borrowed? This is not…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
祖宗之法也固不能不有望于我
皇上修復而變通之矣今團營之法晝一具在
愚願
勑下兵部推選才力大臣如于謙者特司其事
精加汰擇毋令影射彼强壯驍勇役使于
私家者奪之疲癃殘疾充列於行伍者汰
之乃若敵忾惡體負甲而不能行者盡行
挑選定爲冊籍而尤嚴賣放之律使收納
月錢臨期顧募以應一時之點視者無所
===
售其奸重科尅之禁使百計需索假公務
以剥削軍士者無所滋其弊如是則兵爲
有用可以應敵而制勝矣至我
太祖教練之律舊章如新愚願
勑下兵部查議舉行先行省諭令其操練三年
之後責之巡按御史歲一監閱如前降罰
冊名上
聞有能操習勤勞閱有勤効則祿之可也旌之
可也加之陞授及其終身亦可也天下孰
punctuated:
祖宗之法也。固不能不有望于我皇上修復而變通之矣。今團營之法，晝一具在。愚願勑下兵部，推選才力大臣如于謙者，特司其事，精加汰擇，毋令影射。彼强壯驍勇役使于私家者，奪之；疲癃殘疾充列於行伍者，汰之。乃若敵忾惡體，負甲而不能行者，盡行挑選，定爲冊籍，而尤嚴賣放之律，使收納月錢、臨期顧募以應一時之點視者，無所售其奸。重科尅之禁，使百計需索、假公務以剥削軍士者，無所滋其弊。如是則兵爲有用，可以應敵而制勝矣。
至我太祖教練之律，舊章如新。愚願勑下兵部查議舉行，先行省諭，令其操練。三年之後，責之巡按御史，歲一監閱，如前降罰，冊名上聞。有能操習勤勞，閱有勤効，則祿之可也，旌之可也，加之陞授及其終身亦可也。天下孰
translation_en:
…the laws of the imperial ancestors. We cannot but look to Our Emperor to restore them and adapt them to present circumstances. The regulations for the consolidated military camps are now all still extant [?]. I humbly wish that an edict be issued to the Ministry of War to select a high minister of ability and strength, such as Yu Qian, and give him special charge of this matter. He should carefully weed out and select the troops, allowing no fraudulent enrollment. Strong and valiant men employed in private households should be taken back; the infirm and disabled filling the ranks should be discharged. As for those described as “hostile to the enemy, impaired in body” [?], who cannot march under the weight of their armor, all should undergo screening, and registers should be established. Above all, strictly enforce the laws against selling exemptions from service, so that those who collect monthly payments and hire substitutes when an inspection approaches have no opportunity to carry out their fraud. Strengthen the prohibitions against exactions, so that those who devise countless demands and exploit soldiers under the pretext of official business have no opportunity to perpetuate their abuses. In this way the troops will become useful, capable of confronting the enemy and securing victory.
As for the training regulations of Our Taizu, those old statutes remain as pertinent as newly issued ones. I humbly wish that an edict be issued to the Ministry of War to investigate, deliberate, and put them into effect. First issue admonitions ordering the troops to drill. After three years, charge the Regional Inspectors with supervising an inspection once each year, imposing punishments as previously prescribed and submitting registers of names for imperial notice. Those who train diligently and whose efforts prove effective upon inspection may be rewarded with emoluments or publicly commended; they may also be granted promotion and appointment for life. Who under Heaven …

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
不樂賞惡罰且忍其棄其父祖所遺之爵
祿而不思所以保全圖報之乎如是則兵
可日精而軍官軍士之冗食亦可省矣至
其欲實邊儲則屯種可廣矣鹽法可通矣
欲謹邊防則河套可守矣邊墻可治矣是
故欲興屯種則屯田之議可講也欲通鹽
法則
祖宗之舊可復也欲治邊墻則任人之說可行
也欲守河套則連結之虜可虞也夫懷之
以德邊士恤矣畏之以威法令嚴矣示之
以信賞罰明矣若夫脩德柔遠安內攘外
尤在我
皇上惕厲憂勤綱紀四方安不忘危治不忘亂
而已矣愚生草野之見不識執事可轉而
聞之于
上否謹對
第二問
徐良傳
punctuated:
不樂賞惡罰？且忍其棄其父祖所遺之爵祿，而不思所以保全圖報之乎？如是，則兵可日精，而軍官軍士之冗食亦可省矣。至其欲實邊儲，則屯種可廣矣，鹽法可通矣；欲謹邊防，則河套可守矣，邊墻可治矣。是故欲興屯種，則屯田之議可講也；欲通鹽法，則祖宗之舊可復也；欲治邊墻，則任人之說可行也；欲守河套，則連結之虜可虞也。夫懷之以德，邊士恤矣；畏之以威，法令嚴矣；示之以信，賞罰明矣。若夫脩德柔遠，安內攘外，尤在我皇上惕厲憂勤，綱紀四方，安不忘危，治不忘亂而已矣。愚生草野之見，不識執事可轉而聞之于上否？謹對。

第二問
徐良傳
translation_en:
…does not delight in rewards and hate punishments? And could anyone bear to abandon the rank and emoluments bequeathed by his father and forefathers, without considering how to preserve them and repay imperial favor? In this way, the troops could become more proficient by the day, and the expense of maintaining superfluous officers and soldiers could also be reduced. As for replenishing frontier stores, cultivation in military agricultural colonies could be expanded and the salt system made to function effectively. To strengthen frontier defenses, the Hetao region could be held and the frontier walls put in order. Thus, to promote cultivation in military colonies, proposals for military agricultural settlements should be deliberated; to make the salt system work effectively, the ancestral precedents could be restored; to repair the frontier walls, proposals for appointing suitable men could be implemented; and to hold Hetao, precautions could be taken against the allied enemy peoples.

Win them over through virtue, and the frontier soldiers will receive care; make them stand in awe through authority, and laws and orders will be strict; demonstrate trustworthiness, and rewards and punishments will be clear. As for cultivating virtue and winning over distant peoples, securing the realm within and repelling enemies without, these depend above all upon our Emperor remaining vigilant, diligent, and mindful of his responsibilities, maintaining order throughout the realm, never forgetting danger in times of peace or disorder in times of good government. These are the views of an ignorant student living far from court. I do not know whether you, honored examiners, might convey them to His Majesty. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Second Question
Xu Liangchuan

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭高　批　藻鑑評品子其兼三長而
冠三等乎於以覘尚友之學
同考試官教諭蘇　批　古人瑕瑜莫掩子能涇渭
之可與言史矣
考試官教諭陳　批　精詳信傳
考試官學正楊　批　博據
有作史之法有讀史之法知作史之法者
始可以讀史矣知讀史之法者始可與言
史矣史其可以易言哉請因明問而備陳
===
之鄧禹之議於鄴下也其延攬英雄之數
語當矣而武侯荆益之圖尤有得乎天下
之計事業成敗之跡安可論哉謝玄之捷
於淮淝也其大敗秦兵之百萬是矣而萊
公澶淵之役尤有近於萬全之謀風鶴一
時之幸安足恃哉丁謂以卜思見君之言
紿貶欽若匹夫之私憤也〔王欽若〕以擅移皇
堂之故計除丁謂忠臣之謀國也烏得而
同耶楊億欲棄靈州而何亮非之孤城不
punctuated:
同考試官教諭高　批：藻鑑評品，子其兼三長而冠三等乎？於以覘尚友之學。
同考試官教諭蘇　批：古人瑕瑜莫掩，子能涇渭之，可與言史矣。
考試官教諭陳　批：精詳信傳。
考試官學正楊　批：博據。
有作史之法，有讀史之法。知作史之法者，始可以讀史矣；知讀史之法者，始可與言史矣。史其可以易言哉？請因明問而備陳之。鄧禹之議於鄴下也，其延攬英雄之數語當矣，而武侯荆益之圖，尤有得乎天下之計，事業成敗之跡安可論哉？謝玄之捷於淮淝也，其大敗秦兵之百萬是矣，而萊公澶淵之役，尤有近於萬全之謀，風鶴一時之幸安足恃哉？丁謂以卜思見君之言紿貶欽若，匹夫之私憤也；〔王欽若〕以擅移皇堂之故計除丁謂，忠臣之謀國也，烏得而同耶？楊億欲棄靈州，而何亮非之，孤城不
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: “In your discerning appraisal and assessment, do you combine the three strengths and rank foremost in the three grades? Here we can discern your learning through friendship with the ancients.”
Associate Examiner Su, Instructor, comments: “You conceal neither the faults nor the virtues of the ancients. You can distinguish them as clearly as the Jing and Wei rivers; you are someone with whom history can be discussed.”
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Precise and detailed; a trustworthy account.”
Examiner Yang, School Instructor, comments: “Broadly supported by evidence.”
There is a method for writing history, and a method for reading history. Only those who understand the method of writing history can begin to read it; only those who understand the method of reading history can begin to discuss it. Can history be discussed lightly? Allow me to respond to your illuminating question with a full exposition.
When Deng Yu offered his counsel at Ye, his few words about recruiting outstanding men were apt. Yet the Marquis of Wu’s plan for Jing and Yi had an even firmer grasp of strategy for the realm. How could one judge solely by the outward record of success or failure? In Xie Xuan’s victory in the Huai and Fei region, he did indeed inflict a crushing defeat on Qin’s million troops. Yet Duke Lai’s conduct of the campaign at Chanyuan came closer to a strategy ensuring complete security. How could one rely on the fleeting good fortune of an enemy terrified by the wind and the cries of cranes?
Ding Wei used the statement about “not wishing to see the ruler” [?] to contrive Qinruo’s demotion through deception: this was the private resentment of an ordinary man. [Small annotation: Wang Qinruo] [?] used the unauthorized relocation of the imperial burial chamber as grounds for plotting Ding Wei’s removal: this was a loyal minister’s planning for the state. How could the two be treated as equivalent? Yang Yi wished to abandon Lingzhou, but He Liang opposed this: an isolated city cannot …

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
可黍也牛僧孺欲棄維州而德裕排之不
信不可執也奚而不類耶錢若水四十致
仕宋之二疏也即其一時風節其翺黃鵠
於秋雲者乎王旦兼玉清宮使王曾之罪
人也玫其立朝建明其玷白璧於微瑕者
乎褚遂良不欲人主預聞史筆是矣扈蒙
乞委宰相抄送史館則宰相即史官政事
堂即史館又何取於鑒戒乎李遜學不欲
後世盡信史書宜矣劉定之於戳斧一事
===
深惡太宗然則弟有次及之望兄無付託
之誠亦難免乎猜疑矣德宗識後雅之李
潞而獨不覺盧杞之奸邪無因明通蔽之
學明皇疎忠直之宋璟而又能識李林甫
之妬嫉亦好同惡異之心汲黯出補淮陽
與以宋均爲尚書令一以嚴而見憚一以
寬而見褒也黯何愧於均耶唐介召歸諫
院與賈充留爲騎將一本仁宗不遠之復
一由荀勗夕陽亭之語也充何敢望介耶
punctuated: 可黍也。牛僧孺欲棄維州，而德裕排之，不信不可執也。奚而不類耶？錢若水四十致仕，宋之二疏也。即其一時風節，其翺黃鵠於秋雲者乎？王旦兼玉清宮使，王曾之罪人也。玫其立朝建明，其玷白璧於微瑕者乎？褚遂良不欲人主預聞史筆，是矣。扈蒙乞委宰相抄送史館，則宰相即史官，政事堂即史館，又何取於鑒戒乎？李遜學不欲後世盡信史書，宜矣。劉定之於戳斧一事深惡太宗，然則弟有次及之望，兄無付託之誠，亦難免乎猜疑矣。德宗識後雅之李潞，而獨不覺盧杞之奸邪，無因明通蔽之學。明皇疎忠直之宋璟，而又能識李林甫之妬嫉，亦好同惡異之心。汲黯出補淮陽，與以宋均爲尚書令，一以嚴而見憚，一以寬而見褒也，黯何愧於均耶？唐介召歸諫院，與賈充留爲騎將，一本仁宗不遠之復，一由荀勗夕陽亭之語也，充何敢望介耶？
translation_en:
…could not be maintained [?]. Niu Sengru wished to abandon Weizhou, but Li Deyu opposed him: a position involving a breach of faith could not be upheld. Why should these cases not be considered alike? Qian Ruoshui retired from office at forty: he was the Song dynasty’s counterpart to the two Shus. Judging by the integrity he displayed in his day, was he not like a yellow swan soaring amid autumn clouds? Wang Dan concurrently served as Commissioner of the Yuqing Palace, and by Wang Zeng’s standard stood condemned. Yet, considering [?] his service at court and the proposals he advanced, was this not merely a slight blemish on white jade?

Chu Suiliang was right to wish that the ruler should not have advance knowledge of what the historians wrote. Hu Meng requested that the chief councilors be entrusted with copying material and forwarding it to the Historiography Institute. But then the chief councilors would themselves be the historians, and the Administration Hall would itself be the Historiography Institute: what value would remain in history as a source of admonition? Li Xunxue [?] was justified in wishing that later generations should not believe everything in historical works. Liu Dingzhi deeply abhorred Taizong for the affair of the axe [?]. Yet if the younger brother expected to succeed in turn, while the elder brother had no sincere intention of entrusting the succession to him, suspicion could scarcely be avoided.

Dezong recognized the refinement [?] of Li Lu [?], yet alone failed to perceive Lu Qi’s treachery: he lacked the learning needed to extend clear perception to matters obscured from him. Minghuang distanced himself from the loyal and upright Song Jing, yet could recognize Li Linfu’s jealousy: this too reflected a disposition to favor those who agreed with him and dislike those who differed.

Ji An was sent out to fill a post in Huaiyang, while Song Jun was appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs. The former was feared for his severity; the latter was praised for his leniency. Why should Ji An feel inferior to Song Jun? Tang Jie was recalled to the Court of Remonstrance, while Jia Chong was retained as a cavalry general. The former resulted from Renzong’s returning to the right path before straying far; the latter resulted from Xun Xu’s words at Xiyang Pavilion. How could Jia Chong dare aspire to equal Tang Jie?

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
閫佩以虔亮之邀而戎服登舟乃勉而效
忠焉可比於卽日就道之子儀乎岳武穆
居廬山之隱而復起效用此行權之智曷
嘗若口不言兵之世忠乎曹翰陳牲酒
於野以間驍將使元昊疑忌而殺之其與
寺人柳之逐華合比夫何異黃歇受李園
之妹以獻楚王使芊楚以黃而代之其與
呂不韋之易嬴秦又何殊李綱爲留守之
計猶耶彤決河北之留也宋高宗惑於二
===
豎而不及光武惜哉張世傑爲宋復讎而
趨占城猶子房爲韓報讎而從漢也海陵
山颶風大作而弗克自全天乎吳兢不從
張說之請信直筆矣蔡卞爲彰婦翁之惡
而罷山谷之春秋一指可以障乎天地乎曾
肇不入曾布之黨知引嫌矣蔡京〔儵以婦兄〕
之親而以韓侶爲侍郎〔獨〕思可以逃公議
乎家鉉翁之歸宋欲擬蘇武而不知茫茫
堪輿果孰爲故國之土耶盧藏用之隱終
punctuated: 閫佩以虔亮之邀，而戎服登舟，乃勉而效忠焉，可比於卽日就道之子儀乎？岳武穆居廬山之隱，而復起效用，此行權之智，曷嘗若口不言兵之世忠乎？曹翰陳牲酒於野，以間驍將，使元昊疑忌而殺之，其與寺人柳之逐華合比，夫何異？黃歇受李園之妹以獻楚王，使芊楚以黃而代之，其與呂不韋之易嬴秦，又何殊？李綱爲留守之計，猶耶彤決河北之留也。宋高宗惑於二豎，而不及光武，惜哉！張世傑爲宋復讎而趨占城，猶子房爲韓報讎而從漢也。海陵山颶風大作，而弗克自全，天乎？吳兢不從張說之請，信直筆矣。蔡卞爲彰婦翁之惡，而罷山谷之春秋，一指可以障乎天地乎？曾肇不入曾布之黨，知引嫌矣。蔡京〔儵以婦兄〕之親，而以韓侶爲侍郎，〔獨〕思可以逃公議乎？家鉉翁之歸宋，欲擬蘇武，而不知茫茫堪輿，果孰爲故國之土耶？盧藏用之隱終
translation_en:
…the insignia of military command [?], at the invitation of Qian Liang [?]; he boarded the boat in military dress and only reluctantly rendered loyal service. Could he compare with Ziyi, who set out that very day? Yue Wumu emerged from his retirement on Mount Lu to serve once again. This was wisdom in adapting to circumstances: how was he ever like Shizhong, who would not speak of military affairs? Cao Han [?] set out sacrificial animals and wine in the countryside to sow distrust of a valiant general, causing Yuanhao to suspect and kill him. How did this differ from the palace eunuch Liu’s expulsion of Hua Hebi? Huang Xie took Li Yuan’s younger sister and presented her to the king of Chu, causing the Huang lineage to replace Chu’s Qian lineage [?]. How did this differ from Lü Buwei’s substitution for the Ying lineage of Qin? Li Gang’s plan to remain and defend the capital was like Ye Tong’s [?] decision to remain in Hebei. Emperor Gaozong of Song was misled by two scoundrels and failed to measure up to Guangwu. What a pity!

Zhang Shijie went toward Zhancheng to avenge the Song, just as Zifang followed the Han to avenge the state of Han. A violent hurricane arose at Mount Hailing, and he could not save himself. Was this Heaven’s doing? Wu Jing refused Zhang Yue’s request: truly, his was an upright historian’s pen. Cai Bian, to expose his father-in-law’s wickedness [?], suppressed Shangu’s historical chronicle. Can a single finger conceal heaven and earth? Zeng Zhao would not join Zeng Bu’s faction: he understood the need to avoid suspicion of partiality. Cai Jing, through his family connection 〔“suddenly, as his wife’s elder brother” [?]〕, made Han Lü [?] a Vice Minister. Did he 〔alone〕 think he could escape public judgment? In returning to the Song, Jia Xuanweng wished to emulate Su Wu, yet did he not realize that, throughout the vast expanse of heaven and earth, it was uncertain what land still belonged to his former country? Lu Cangyong’s retirement on Zhong…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
南欲方于陵而不知自有佳處又何取捷
徑之讖耶漢武徙豪傑於茂陵而四豪三
游固已馳騁於王道之久廢成帝詔典領
五經而九流七畧又嘗蕪穢於正學之未
崇倡豐亨豫大之蔡京與統領花石之朱
勔貽害何殊石五胡亂華之劉淵與幽沈
仁義之王何債事無異凡若此者皆是非
同異之所以分治亂興衰之所由寓苟於
是而知所權衡焉則善可以爲法惡可以
爲戒上焉而可以爲君下焉而可以爲臣
於王霸之異道邪正之異學舉皆於是乎
辨矣雖進而讀諸經可矣管見如斯進退
惟命
第三問
===
佘文獻
同考試官教諭尤　批　牧政今日之務考據詳而
議論切者無踰此篇
同考試官教諭張　批　馬耆息而民不擾學集之
punctuated:
南，欲方于陵，而不知自有佳處，又何取捷徑之讖耶？漢武徙豪傑於茂陵，而四豪三游固已馳騁於王道之久廢；成帝詔典領五經，而九流七畧又嘗蕪穢於正學之未崇。倡豐亨豫大之蔡京，與統領花石之朱勔，貽害何殊？石五胡亂華之劉淵，與幽沈仁義之王何，債事無異。凡若此者，皆是非同異之所以分，治亂興衰之所由寓。苟於是而知所權衡焉，則善可以爲法，惡可以爲戒；上焉而可以爲君，下焉而可以爲臣。於王霸之異道、邪正之異學，舉皆於是乎辨矣。雖進而讀諸經，可矣。管見如斯，進退惟命。
第三問
佘文獻
同考試官教諭尤批：牧政，今日之務，考據詳而議論切者，無踰此篇。
同考試官教諭張批：馬耆息而民不擾，學集之
translation_en:
…Zhongnan, wishing to compare himself with the recluse of Yuling, yet unaware that there was already a fine place for him: why, then, invite the prophetic remark about a “shortcut” to office? Emperor Wu of Han relocated powerful and outstanding men to Maoling, yet the four grandees and three kinds of itinerants had already ranged freely while the Way of the Kings had long been abandoned. Emperor Cheng ordered the Five Classics placed under official supervision, yet the Nine Schools and Seven Summaries had also become overgrown with weeds while orthodox learning remained unhonored. How did the harm bequeathed by Cai Jing, who advocated lavish prosperity and expansive indulgence, differ from that caused by Zhu Mian, who supervised the collection of flowers and ornamental rocks? Liu Yuan, who brought about the Five Hu’s disruption of China [?], and Wang and He—Wang Bi and He Yan—who submerged benevolence and righteousness in obscurity, were no different in the consequences of their actions [?].
All such cases reveal the distinctions between right and wrong, similarity and difference; within them lie the causes of order and disorder, flourishing and decline. If one knows how to weigh them properly, goodness can serve as a model and evil as a warning. In a superior position, one can thereby act as a ruler; in a subordinate position, as a minister. The different paths of true kingship and hegemony, and the different teachings of heterodoxy and orthodoxy, can all be distinguished through these cases. One may then even advance to reading the Classics. Such is my limited view; whether it is accepted or rejected, I await your judgment.
Third Policy Question
She Wenxian
Comment by Associate Examiner You, Instructor: “The administration of horse pastures is an urgent matter today. No essay surpasses this one in the thoroughness of its supporting evidence and the pertinence of its argument.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Horses multiply [?] without the people being disturbed; the accumulation of learning …”

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
善者也此子能言之
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔我〕
朝馬政實盛前代而獨盛者此篇敷對無遺而每致深意焉用世
〔之文也故錄〕
考試官教諭陳　批〔知以馬富國者〕
考試官學正楊　批〔得人意良是〕
馬政今天下之大務也而明問及之蓋求
天下之大計也顧愚何足以知之雖然嘗
聞周書曰司馬掌邦政夫馬以名官則知
===
武備之弗可忽者也考之周禮四井爲邑
四邑爲丘四丘爲甸天子畿內可得馬四
萬諸侯之國可得四千大夫之家可得四
百此成周天子諸侯大夫之馬數也衛風
之詩曰秉心塞淵騋牝三千有以知文公
牧馬之盛矣魯頌之詩曰駉駉牡馬在坰
之野有以知僖公牧馬之盛矣漢初稍復
古制養馬一匹者復卒三人平居則免三
人之算有事則當三人之卒至于邊塞則
punctuated:
善者也，此子能言之。
同考試官教諭鄭批：〔我〕朝馬政實盛前代，而獨盛者，此篇敷對無遺，而每致深意焉，用世〔之文也，故錄。〕
考試官教諭陳批：〔知以馬富國者。〕
考試官學正楊批：〔得人意，良是。〕
馬政，今天下之大務也，而明問及之，蓋求天下之大計也。顧愚何足以知之？雖然，嘗聞周書曰：「司馬掌邦政。」夫馬以名官，則知武備之弗可忽者也。考之周禮，四井爲邑，四邑爲丘，四丘爲甸。天子畿內可得馬四萬，諸侯之國可得四千，大夫之家可得四百，此成周天子、諸侯、大夫之馬數也。衛風之詩曰：「秉心塞淵，騋牝三千。」有以知文公牧馬之盛矣。魯頌之詩曰：「駉駉牡馬，在坰之野。」有以知僖公牧馬之盛矣。漢初稍復古制，養馬一匹者，復卒三人。平居則免三人之算，有事則當三人之卒。至于邊塞則
translation_en:
…one skilled in this. This candidate can articulate it.

Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “Our dynasty’s horse administration indeed surpasses that of previous dynasties. This essay sets out exhaustively the features that make it preeminent, repeatedly conveying profound insights. It is writing suited to practical government, and therefore has been selected.”

Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “One who understands how to enrich the state through horses.”

Examiner Yang, School Director, comments: “It captures what one has in mind; very sound indeed.”

Horse administration is a great concern of the realm today. Your discerning question addresses it, surely seeking a comprehensive plan for the realm. Yet how could someone as ignorant as I be adequate to understand it? Nevertheless, I have heard it said in the Documents of Zhou: “The Minister of War directs the government of the state.” Since horses give this office its name, we know that military preparedness must not be neglected. Examining the Rites of Zhou, we find that four well-field units constitute a settlement, four settlements a tract, and four tracts a district. Within the Son of Heaven’s royal domain, forty thousand horses could be obtained; in a regional lord’s state, four thousand; and in a grandee’s estate, four hundred. These were the numbers of horses belonging to the Son of Heaven, the regional lords, and the grandees in the fully established Zhou order. A poem in the Airs of Wei says: “His heart is steadfast and profound; his tall horses and mares number three thousand.” From this we can understand the flourishing state of horse breeding under Duke Wen. A poem in the Hymns of Lu says: “Sturdy are the stallions, in the fields beyond the outskirts.” From this we can understand the flourishing state of horse breeding under Duke Xi.

At the beginning of the Han, the ancient system was gradually restored. A person who raised one horse secured exemption from military service for three men. In ordinary times, this meant exemption from the poll tax for three men; when military service was required, the horse stood in place of three soldiers. As for the frontier regions, …

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
縱民畜牧而官不禁以至衆庶有馬阡陌
成羣故邊郡之盛則三十六苑分置西北
武帝承平窮兵黷武既數出師馬大消乏
雖法令日嚴而竟不能復其舊矣唐初創
置八坊八坊之馬爲四十八監而馬多地
狹又析八監列布河西豐曠之野故自貞
觀麟德四十年之間得馬七十萬餘匹天
寶之後諸軍戰馬動以萬計秦漢以來未
之聞也宋之馬萬不及唐至于户馬之法
===
行于熈寧保馬之法行于元豐焉未必得
而民已受其害矣是故賦之以地弗可均
也歛之以課歲有歉也户配一馬弗可蓄
也馬弗可蓄民俱困也馬斃必償民弗堪
也是故保馬之害滋也我
朝建都燕京以來陜西遼東各設苑馬寺寺
管六監監管四苑大苑養馬萬匹中苑七
千小苑一千馬不下十三萬匹其原額草
塲十有三萬三千七百七十七頃六十畝
punctuated:
縱民畜牧而官不禁，以至衆庶有馬，阡陌成羣。故邊郡之盛，則三十六苑分置西北。武帝承平，窮兵黷武，既數出師，馬大消乏，雖法令日嚴，而竟不能復其舊矣。唐初創置八坊，八坊之馬爲四十八監，而馬多地狹，又析八監，列布河西豐曠之野。故自貞觀、麟德四十年之間，得馬七十萬餘匹。天寶之後，諸軍戰馬動以萬計，秦漢以來未之聞也。宋之馬萬不及唐。至于户馬之法行于熈寧，保馬之法行于元豐，焉未必得，而民已受其害矣。是故賦之以地，弗可均也；歛之以課，歲有歉也；户配一馬，弗可蓄也。馬弗可蓄，民俱困也；馬斃必償，民弗堪也。是故保馬之害滋也。
我朝建都燕京以來，陜西、遼東各設苑馬寺，寺管六監，監管四苑，大苑養馬萬匹，中苑七千，小苑一千，馬不下十三萬匹。其原額草塲十有三萬三千七百七十七頃六十畝。
translation_en:
…the people were allowed to raise livestock without official prohibition, so that ordinary people owned horses, and herds gathered along the paths between the fields. Thus, at the height of horse breeding in the frontier commanderies, thirty-six pastures were established throughout the northwest. Emperor Wu, inheriting a peaceful realm, exhausted his resources in warfare and resorted recklessly to arms. After repeated campaigns, the horses were severely depleted. Although the laws grew stricter by the day, their former numbers could never be restored. Early in the Tang, eight breeding establishments were founded, with their horses organized under forty-eight supervisory offices. As the horses became numerous and the land insufficient, eight additional supervisory offices were separated out and distributed across the fertile, open country of Hexi. Thus, in the forty years between the Zhenguan and Linde reign periods, more than 700,000 horses were obtained. After the Tianbao period, the warhorses of the various armies regularly numbered in the tens of thousands—something unheard of since the Qin and Han. The Song's horse numbers fell far short of the Tang's. As for the household-horse system implemented during the Xining period and the horse-guarantee system implemented during the Yuanfeng period, horses were not necessarily obtained [?], yet the people had already suffered the harm.
Thus, assigning obligations according to landholdings could not distribute them equitably; levying them as quotas encountered years of poor harvest; and assigning one horse to each household left households unable to maintain it. When horses could not be maintained, the people were all impoverished; when a horse died and compensation was required, the people could not bear the burden. Thus the harms of the horse-guarantee system multiplied.
Since our dynasty established its capital at Yanjing, Directorates of Pasturage have been established in both Shaanxi and Liaodong. Each directorate administers six supervisory offices, and each office administers four pastures. A large pasture maintains 10,000 horses, a medium pasture 7,000, and a small pasture 1,000, with no fewer than 130,000 horses in all. The original allotment of pastureland was 133,777 qing and 60 mu.
