title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
養馬恩隊軍人一千二百二十名正統初
年始將監苑裁省止存二監天順初年復
將苑馬寺併革而原撥恩軍亦遷設矣至
成化間所在種馬止三千匹弘治間所存
草場止六萬六千八百八十八頃八十畝
所存軍人止七百四十五名以致牧馬之
地盡散之民而致終不能復
祖宗之舊矣馬政廢弛邊防甚踈當國計者可
爲寒心宜有以厪執事下問之惓惓也爲
===
今之計則唐坊監之故地可復也兩京河
南山東養馬之政宋保馬之遺也可革也
原額之草場可復也原設之恩軍可補也
必如大學士楊一清所議種馬可增以廣
蓄也牧軍可增以養馬也是故唐之坊監
即岐豳涇寧也今陝西之鳳翔西安之邠
州平凉之涇州慶陽之寧州即其地也而
又有隴西金城平凉三水皆水草膏腴之
田可爲牧放之所者誠得人以往求之經
punctuated:
養馬恩隊軍人一千二百二十名。正統初年，始將監苑裁省，止存二監。天順初年，復將苑馬寺併革，而原撥恩軍亦遷設矣。至成化間，所在種馬止三千匹；弘治間，所存草場止六萬六千八百八十八頃八十畝，所存軍人止七百四十五名。以致牧馬之地盡散之民，而致終不能復祖宗之舊矣。馬政廢弛，邊防甚踈，當國計者可爲寒心，宜有以厪執事下問之惓惓也。
爲今之計，則唐坊監之故地可復也；兩京、河南、山東養馬之政，宋保馬之遺也，可革也；原額之草場可復也；原設之恩軍可補也。必如大學士楊一清所議，種馬可增以廣蓄也，牧軍可增以養馬也。是故唐之坊監，即岐、豳、涇、寧也。今陝西之鳳翔、西安之邠州、平凉之涇州、慶陽之寧州，即其地也。而又有隴西、金城、平凉、三水，皆水草膏腴之田，可爲牧放之所者。誠得人以往求之，經
translation_en:
…and 1,220 soldiers of the en detachments [?] assigned to rear horses. In the early Zhengtong reign, the directorates and pastures began to be reduced, leaving only two directorates. In the early Tianshun reign, the Court of Imperial Studs was also abolished through consolidation, and the originally assigned en troops [?] were likewise relocated. By the Chenghua reign, only 3,000 breeding horses remained in these places. During the Hongzhi reign, only 66,888 qing and 80 mu of pastureland remained, together with just 745 soldiers. Consequently, the horse pastures were all dispersed into civilian hands, and the arrangements established by the imperial ancestors could never be restored. Horse administration has fallen into neglect, and frontier defenses are gravely deficient. Those responsible for planning the affairs of the state have cause to shudder. This surely warrants the earnest concern expressed in your question.
For present purposes, the former lands of the Tang horse-breeding establishments and directorates can be reclaimed. The horse-rearing arrangements in the two capitals, Henan, and Shandong are a survival of the Song system of entrusting horses to households and can be abolished. The original allotment of pastureland can be restored, and the original complement of en troops [?] can be replenished. We must follow the proposals of Grand Secretary Yang Yiqing: increase the breeding horses to enlarge the stock, and increase the herding troops to care for them. The Tang horse-breeding establishments and directorates were located in Qi, Bin, Jing, and Ning. Their sites correspond to present-day Fengxiang in Shaanxi, Binzhou under Xi’an, Jingzhou under Pingliang, and Ningzhou under Qingyang. There are also Longxi, Jincheng, Pingliang, and Sanshui, all fertile lands with abundant water and grass, suitable for grazing. If capable men could indeed be sent to seek out these lands and plan…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
晝周詳則唐之坊監可復無慮乎貞觀麟
德之馬弗盛于今日矣若夫宋人保馬之
法官馬給之免其別役今則論丁養馬而
仍科賦征役矣尤乃生必報數死必責償
一馬未償而一馬又斃生者未倸而駒歲
又續生者歲增將奚爲給死者日繼陪償
無已其將何以生生乎嗟乎敝民以養馬
馬可用也猶可言也民力既斃馬弗獲用
傷財害民爲困滋甚誠能復古之政改圖
===
而更革之則馬爲有用而民力亦庶乎其
少甦矣至于草塲之消沒者豪强之兼併
也恩軍之缺乏者官司之占役也誠能遣
知馬政大臣備查歷代冊籍勘實清理使
山林原隰堪爲牧地者咸復其舊恩軍閃
避者咸補其役則我
祖宗原額草塲牧軍之數或者其有復乎夫馬
種既多而後孳息可蕃也養必得人而後
虧失可少也誠能
punctuated: 晝周詳，則唐之坊監可復，無慮乎貞觀、麟德之馬弗盛于今日矣。若夫宋人保馬之法，官馬給之，免其別役；今則論丁養馬，而仍科賦征役矣。尤乃生必報數，死必責償，一馬未償，而一馬又斃；生者未倸，而駒歲又續。生者歲增，將奚爲給？死者日繼，陪償無已，其將何以生生乎？嗟乎！敝民以養馬，馬可用也，猶可言也；民力既斃，馬弗獲用，傷財害民，爲困滋甚。誠能復古之政，改圖而更革之，則馬爲有用，而民力亦庶乎其少甦矣。至于草塲之消沒者，豪强之兼併也；恩軍之缺乏者，官司之占役也。誠能遣知馬政大臣，備查歷代冊籍，勘實清理，使山林原隰堪爲牧地者咸復其舊，恩軍閃避者咸補其役，則我祖宗原額草塲牧軍之數，或者其有復乎？夫馬種既多，而後孳息可蕃也；養必得人，而後虧失可少也。誠能
translation_en:
…if the planning is thorough [?], the Tang system of horse-breeding establishments and supervisory offices can be restored. There would then be no fear that horses as plentiful as those of the Zhenguan and Linde eras could not flourish today.

Under the Song system of household horse keeping, government horses were entrusted to households, which were exempted from other service obligations. Today, however, horse-rearing obligations are assigned according to the number of adult males, while taxes and service obligations are still imposed. Worse still, births must be reported by number, and deaths invariably require compensation. Before one horse has been paid for, another dies; the living horses have not yet been dealt with [?], yet more foals arrive each year. As the living increase annually, how are they to be provided for? As deaths follow day after day and compensation has no end, how are the people to sustain their livelihoods? Alas! Exhausting the people to raise horses might still be defensible if the horses were usable. But the people's strength is already exhausted, while the horses cannot be put to use: wealth is wasted, the people are harmed, and their distress grows ever worse. If ancient policies could truly be restored and the arrangements reconsidered and reformed, the horses would become useful, and the people's strength might recover somewhat.

As for the disappearance of pasturelands, this results from their absorption by powerful families; the shortage of enjun troops [?] results from officials appropriating their labor. If high officials knowledgeable about horse administration could be dispatched to examine comprehensively the registers of successive dynasties, investigate the actual circumstances, and put matters in order, then all wooded uplands, plains, and lowlands suitable for grazing could be restored to their former use, and all service vacancies left by evading enjun troops [?] could be filled. Might the original quotas of pasturelands and herdsmen soldiers established by our imperial ancestors then be restored? Only when breeding stock is plentiful can its offspring multiply; only when suitable people are entrusted with rearing the horses can losses be reduced. If it were truly possible to…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
敕下太臣查照一清之議設法舉行則我
國初得馬之數或者其有復乎雖然一清之
所議尤不止是也夫創邊方之馬廐以便
收息則虜寇無侵而風雪可蔽矣愼監苑
之久任以責成功則事無因循而官無覬
望矣此皆今日邊方之急務而愚生就執
事之問者言之也若欲悉舉而極求之則
懷慶彰德大名滑濮古衛地也兗州滄海
高密古魯地也汧嵐石濕漢之太原也今
===
之同州唐之沙苑也校人牧師趣馬巫馬
馬質之法周禮在也時其出入謹其飼養
節其勞逸辨其良雜儒臣丘文莊之說可
考也固非風簷之下所能盡述也雖然猶
有說焉兵貴馬也尤貴將也誠得其將則
教練之下步可勝騎夫以岳飛之數萬人
而金人所謂拐子馬者盡于一旦馬何爲
哉如其無將馬將焉御故今日之邊防執
事患其無馬而愚生尤患其無將也易曰
punctuated:
敕下太臣，查照一清之議，設法舉行，則我國初得馬之數，或者其有復乎？雖然，一清之所議尤不止是也。夫創邊方之馬廐，以便收息，則虜寇無侵而風雪可蔽矣；愼監苑之久任，以責成功，則事無因循而官無覬望矣。此皆今日邊方之急務，而愚生就執事之問者言之也。若欲悉舉而極求之，則懷慶、彰德、大名、滑、濮，古衛地也；兗州、滄海、高密，古魯地也；汧、嵐、石、濕，漢之太原也；今之同州，唐之沙苑也。校人、牧師、趣馬、巫馬、馬質之法，《周禮》在也。時其出入，謹其飼養，節其勞逸，辨其良雜，儒臣丘文莊之說可考也。固非風簷之下所能盡述也。

雖然，猶有說焉。兵貴馬也，尤貴將也。誠得其將，則教練之下，步可勝騎。夫以岳飛之數萬人，而金人所謂拐子馬者盡于一旦，馬何爲哉？如其無將，馬將焉御？故今日之邊防，執事患其無馬，而愚生尤患其無將也。《易》曰：
translation_en:
… issue an edict to the high ministers [?], directing them to consult Yiqing’s proposals and devise means to implement them, might we perhaps recover the number of horses obtained at the founding of our dynasty? Yet Yiqing’s proposals go still further. Building stables on the frontier to facilitate sheltering and breeding horses would protect them from enemy incursions and provide shelter from wind and snow. Taking care to retain the officials supervising the horse parks in long tenure, and holding them responsible for results, would prevent affairs from languishing through routine neglect and officials from coveting other appointments. These are all urgent matters for the frontier today; I, your humble student, discuss them in response to your question. If one wished to enumerate all the possibilities and investigate them fully, Huaiqing, Zhangde, Daming, Hua, and Pu were the territory of ancient Wei; Yanzhou, Canghai, and Gaomi were the territory of ancient Lu; Qian, Lan, Shi, and Shi [?] were the Taiyuan region of the Han; and present-day Tongzhou was the Shayuan pastureland of the Tang. The regulations for the Director of Horses (jiaoren), Pasture Master (mushi), Horse Trainer (quma), Horse Healer (wuma), and Horse Appraiser (mazhi) survive in the Rites of Zhou. On bringing horses out and taking them in at the proper times, carefully managing their feeding, regulating their work and rest, and distinguishing good stock from mixed stock, the proposals of the Confucian minister Qiu Wenzhuang may be consulted. These matters certainly cannot be fully expounded beneath the wind-swept eaves of the examination hall.

Yet there is something further to say. In warfare, horses are valued, but commanders are valued still more. If the right commander is found, then with training infantry can defeat cavalry. With only several tens of thousands of men, Yue Fei wiped out in a single day what the Jin called their guaizi cavalry. What use were their horses? Without a commander, how are horses to be directed? Thus, concerning frontier defense today, you worry about the lack of horses, while I, your humble student, worry still more about the lack of commanders. The Book of Changes says: …

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
長子帥師以中行也又曰王三錫命懷萬
邦也敢以擇將一言爲今日之大計
獻執事以爲何如
第四問
朱瓚
同考試官教諭陳　批　天下無離道之文否則藝
焉耳矣此文章盛衰之所以分也執此論文如執權
衡以較輕重若子其積學之士乎
同考試官教諭楊　批　識見超邁而詞足以發之
===
可與言文者
考試官教諭陳　批　文字溫淳如大羹玄酒其
有志於崇雅者乎
考試官學正楊　批　論文一策正欲觀士子之
志此篇直欲本之道以六經四書爲宗若不滿於因
文見道者其志可謂遒出矣異時有鳴
國家之盛者必子也夫
古之文出於一今之文出於二何則六經
之所載者道也而未嘗無文夫是之謂一
punctuated:
長子帥師，以中行也。又曰：「王三錫命，懷萬邦也。」敢以擇將一言爲今日之大計，獻執事，以爲何如？

第四問
朱瓚

同考試官教諭陳批：天下無離道之文，否則藝焉耳矣。此文章盛衰之所以分也。執此論文，如執權衡以較輕重。若子，其積學之士乎！

同考試官教諭楊批：識見超邁，而詞足以發之，可與言文者。

考試官教諭陳批：文字溫淳，如大羹玄酒，其有志於崇雅者乎！

考試官學正楊批：論文一策，正欲觀士子之志。此篇直欲本之道，以六經四書爲宗，若不滿於因文見道者，其志可謂遒出矣。異時有鳴國家之盛者，必子也夫！

古之文出於一，今之文出於二。何則？六經之所載者，道也，而未嘗無文，夫是之謂一。
translation_en:
…“The eldest son commands the army because he acts in accordance with the mean.” It also says: “The king thrice bestows commands, cherishing the myriad states.” I venture to offer you the single proposal of selecting generals as the great strategic priority of the present day. What do you think of it?

Fourth Policy Question
Zhu Zan

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: There is no true writing under Heaven that is divorced from the Way; otherwise, it is merely a craft. This is what distinguishes the flourishing of literature from its decline. To judge writing by this principle is like using a balance to compare weights. Surely you are a scholar of accumulated learning!

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: His insights are outstanding, and his language is fully adequate to express them. Here is someone with whom one can discuss literature.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: His writing is gentle and pure, like unseasoned sacrificial broth and the plain water used in ritual offerings. Surely he aspires to uphold classical elegance!

Comment by Examiner Yang, School Director: This policy question on literature was intended precisely to reveal the candidates’ aspirations. This essay seeks to root literature directly in the Way, taking the Six Classics and Four Books as its guiding authorities, as though dissatisfied with merely discerning the Way through writing. His aspiration may indeed be called exceptional. If in times to come someone gives voice to the flourishing of our state, it will surely be you!

The writing of antiquity issued from unity; the writing of today issues from division. Why is this? What the Six Classics contain is the Way, yet they have never lacked literary expression. This is what is meant by unity.

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
諸子百家非不文也而無取於明道夫昇
之謂二一則醇醇則法二則雜雜則趨於
變也極矣是故大雅渾厚之風纖巧靡麗
之作非但與時高下而實所以爲時之高
下也有世道之責者宜不能忘情斯文焉
此我
皇上
詔旨殷勤深戒時文之弊欲一變而還之古者
大哉
===
王言乎一哉
王心乎執事發策以問豈非抱世道之深憂者
乎諸生學爲文章者敢略陳之夫文之所
繫亦大矣深於道者未有不文者也不深
於道而能文者非文之至也三代而上六
經之文尚矣是故易繇爻象而陰陽之道
著書載典謨而政事之道舉詩本詠歌而
性情之道彰春秋道名分而百王之法昭
禮謹節文而三千三百之理顯是其布在
punctuated:
諸子百家非不文也，而無取於明道，夫昇之謂二。一則醇，醇則法；二則雜，雜則趨於變也極矣。是故大雅渾厚之風、纖巧靡麗之作，非但與時高下，而實所以爲時之高下也。有世道之責者，宜不能忘情斯文焉。此我皇上詔旨殷勤，深戒時文之弊，欲一變而還之古者。大哉，王言乎！一哉，王心乎！執事發策以問，豈非抱世道之深憂者乎？諸生學爲文章者，敢略陳之。
夫文之所繫亦大矣。深於道者，未有不文者也；不深於道而能文者，非文之至也。三代而上，六經之文尚矣。是故易繇爻象而陰陽之道著，書載典謨而政事之道舉，詩本詠歌而性情之道彰，春秋道名分而百王之法昭，禮謹節文而三千三百之理顯。是其布在
translation_en:
…The philosophers of the various schools are not without literary accomplishment, yet their writings do not serve to illuminate the Way: this is what is called duality [?]. Unity produces purity, and purity provides a model; duality produces mixture, and mixture tends toward change to the utmost degree. Thus, styles of grand elegance and unaffected richness, and works of delicate ingenuity and lavish ornament, do more than rise and fall with their age: they actually help determine the elevation or decline of that age. Those responsible for the moral order of the world ought never to cease caring about this literary tradition. This is why our Emperor, in his earnest edict, has sternly warned against the faults of contemporary examination writing, wishing to transform it and restore it to antiquity. How great are the royal words! How single-minded is the royal heart! You gentlemen have issued a policy question on this subject: surely you too harbor deep concern for the moral order of the world? As students learning to compose literary works, we venture to offer a brief account.
Much indeed depends upon writing. No one profoundly versed in the Way has ever lacked literary accomplishment; those who can write well without being profoundly versed in the Way have not attained the highest excellence in writing. From the Three Dynasties back into antiquity, the writing of the Six Classics was exalted indeed. Thus, through its line statements and images, the Book of Changes makes manifest the Way of yin and yang; by recording canons and counsels, the Book of Documents sets forth the Way of government; grounded in chanting and song, the Book of Odes reveals the Way of human nature and feelings; by expounding titles and proper distinctions, the Spring and Autumn Annals makes clear the standards for all kings; and by attending carefully to ceremonial forms, the ritual classics reveal the principles of the three thousand minor observances and three hundred major rites. These writings are set down in…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
方冊者猶菽粟之於饑也布帛之於寒也
未耜釜甑之於陶冶也一不足而生民之
道缺矣此無意於文而不得不文者也三
代而下有意爲文亦藝焉而已矣故先秦
之文莫如左氏國語戰國策然左傳誣矣
而韓退之以爲誇國語工矣而柳子厚實
非之戰國策文矣而縱橫捭闔之習不能
免焉三書且然況其他乎唐人謂三代之
文至戰國而病正以是爾漢之文莫過於
===
董賈司馬氏然治安之策其志大矣而三
表五餌失之疎上林子虛之賦其旨微矣
而瑰瑋萬象失之靡天人之對有正誼明
道之言其說似矣然而柔行巽入人以爲
失之緩三子且然況其下乎班固謂漢文
與三代同風豈其然乎唐之文承江左餘
風絺章繪句揣合低昂其變極矣韓愈氏
興力去陳言以追古作善乎蘇氏謂其文
起八代之衰也然以博愛爲仁則不知仁
punctuated:
方冊者，猶菽粟之於饑也，布帛之於寒也，未耜釜甑之於陶冶也。一不足，而生民之道缺矣。此無意於文而不得不文者也。三代而下，有意爲文，亦藝焉而已矣。故先秦之文，莫如左氏、國語、戰國策。然左傳誣矣，而韓退之以爲誇；國語工矣，而柳子厚實非之；戰國策文矣，而縱橫捭闔之習不能免焉。三書且然，況其他乎？唐人謂三代之文至戰國而病，正以是爾。
漢之文，莫過於董、賈、司馬氏。然治安之策，其志大矣，而三表五餌失之疎；上林、子虛之賦，其旨微矣，而瑰瑋萬象失之靡；天人之對，有正誼明道之言，其說似矣，然而柔行巽入，人以爲失之緩。三子且然，況其下乎？班固謂漢文與三代同風，豈其然乎？
唐之文，承江左餘風，絺章繪句，揣合低昂，其變極矣。韓愈氏興，力去陳言，以追古作。善乎蘇氏謂其文起八代之衰也！然以博愛爲仁，則不知仁
translation_en:
…what is set out in written volumes is like beans and grain to the hungry, cloth and silk to the cold, and ploughshares[?], cauldrons, and steamers in relation to pottery and metalworking. If even one is lacking, the means of sustaining the people’s lives are incomplete. Such writing arises without a deliberate intention to produce literary compositions, yet cannot help taking literary form. After the Three Dynasties, people deliberately composed literature, but this amounted merely to an art. Thus, among pre-Qin writings, none surpass those of Master Zuo, the Discourses of the States, and the Strategies of the Warring States. Yet the Commentary of Zuo contains falsehoods, and Han Tuizhi considered it exaggerated; the Discourses of the States is accomplished, yet Liu Zihou indeed criticized it; the Strategies of the Warring States possesses literary elegance, yet cannot escape the habits of alliance-building and manipulative persuasion. If even these three books are like this, how much more so the others? A Tang writer said that the literature of the Three Dynasties became diseased in the Warring States period: precisely for this reason.
Among Han writings, none surpass those of Dong Zhongshu, Jia Yi, and Sima Xiangru. Yet although the Policy Essay on Good Government and Security is grand in its aspirations, its proposals for the “three demonstrations and five baits” err in their impracticality. Although the rhapsodies Imperial Park and Master Zixu are subtle in their intent, their extravagant depiction of myriad things errs in excessive ornamentation. The Responses on Heaven and Humanity speak of rectifying righteousness and illuminating the Way, and their arguments appear sound; nevertheless, their gentle approach and deferential insinuation led people to consider them excessively slow to take effect. If even these three masters are like this, how much more so those beneath them? Ban Gu said that Han literature shared the spirit of the Three Dynasties. Could that really be so?
Tang literature inherited the lingering influence of the region south of the Yangzi: embroidering its passages and adorning its phrases, calculating how to please and when to raise or lower its tone, it carried these developments to their utmost extreme. Han Yu arose and strove to eliminate stale expressions in pursuit of ancient compositions. Well did Master Su say that his writing revived literature after eight dynasties of decline! Yet, in taking universal love to constitute benevolence, he did not understand benevolence…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
之所以爲仁其於道何如也雖然原道一
篇達聖人之用佛骨一表排釋氏之非謂
之全無所見不可也宋之文習西崑之體
而至天地軋萬物茁其變極矣歐陽氏出
痛抑浮怪務還渾厚宜乎劉暈因之而改
鉤棘之體也然謂教人性非所先則不知
性之所以爲性其於道何如也雖然本論
之作足以裨治功朋黨之論有以定國是
謂之全無所見亦不可也蓋二子本因文
以見道而非明道以爲文故其終身從事
不過曰光王襲罔情孔思而已矣不過論
事似陸贄記事似司馬遷詩賦似李白而
已矣是蓋二之也安能彷彿六經之文哉
嗚呼彼一時也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝以道德化人以六經造士其諭
林詹同之言曰古人爲文章或以明道德
或以通當世之務如典謨之言皆明白易
知無深怪險僻之語至如諸葛孔明出師
punctuated:
之所以爲仁，其於道何如也？雖然，《原道》一篇達聖人之用，《佛骨》一表排釋氏之非，謂之全無所見，不可也。宋之文習西崑之體，而至天地軋、萬物茁，其變極矣。歐陽氏出，痛抑浮怪，務還渾厚，宜乎劉暈因之而改鉤棘之體也。然謂教人性非所先，則不知性之所以爲性，其於道何如也？雖然，《本論》之作足以裨治功，《朋黨》之論有以定國是，謂之全無所見，亦不可也。蓋二子本因文以見道，而非明道以爲文，故其終身從事，不過曰光王襲罔情孔思而已矣，不過論事似陸贄、記事似司馬遷、詩賦似李白而已矣。是蓋二之也，安能彷彿六經之文哉！
嗚呼！彼一時也。洪惟我太祖高皇帝，以道德化人，以六經造士。其諭林詹同之言曰：「古人爲文章，或以明道德，或以通當世之務，如典謨之言，皆明白易知，無深怪險僻之語。至如諸葛孔明《出師
translation_en:
…what makes benevolence benevolence: how, then, did he stand in relation to the Way? Nevertheless, his essay “An Inquiry into the Way” (Yuan dao) conveyed the practical application of the sages’ teaching, and his memorial on the Buddha’s bone refuted the errors of Buddhism. One cannot say that he had no insight whatsoever. The writing of the Song followed the Xikun style, until it reached such expressions as “Heaven and Earth grind against one another; the myriad things sprout.” Its transformations had reached an extreme. Ouyang Xiu emerged, vigorously suppressing superficiality and strangeness and striving to restore substance and integrity. It was fitting that Liu Yun [?] should consequently abandon his hooked and thorny style. Yet, in saying that teaching people about human nature was not the first priority, he failed to understand what makes human nature what it is. How, then, did he stand in relation to the Way? Nevertheless, his “Essay on Fundamentals” (Ben lun) could contribute to effective government, and his “Discourse on Factions” (Pengdang lun) could establish the correct course for the state. Nor can one say that he had no insight whatsoever. These two men essentially sought to perceive the Way through writing, rather than writing from an enlightened understanding of the Way. Thus, their lifelong endeavors amounted to no more than “glorifying kings, inheriting …, and thinking the thoughts of Confucius” [?]; no more than discussing affairs like Lu Zhi, recording events like Sima Qian, and composing poetry and rhapsodies like Li Bai. This was to treat the two as separate. How could their writing possibly resemble that of the Six Classics?
Alas! That was another age. We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao transformed people through the Way and virtue and trained scholars through the Six Classics. In his admonition to Zhan Tong, designated here as “Lin” [?], he said: “When the ancients composed writings, some sought to illuminate the Way and virtue, while others sought to comprehend the affairs of their own time. For example, the words of the Canons and Counsels were all clear and easy to understand, without obscure, strange, tortuous, or abstruse expressions. As for Zhuge Kongming’s ‘Memorial on Dispatching the Army’…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
表亦何嘗雕刻爲文而誠意溢出至今使
人誦之自然忠義感激近世文士不究道
德之本不達當世之務故詞雖艱深意實
淺近即使過揚雄司馬相如何裨實用此
我
高皇之道也而亦我
高皇之文也是故百餘年間風聲所漸士大夫
務經術而重行誼前輩爲文皆典雅平易
如太羹玄酒有欲工而未能之意故永樂
===
宣德之間風俗厚而士氣昌彬彬乎可謂
盛矣邇來枝葉日盛而根本日微無左氏
之富也而學其浮華無國語之詞也而學
其刻削無戰國策之權謀也而學其變化
無董賈之學識也而學其馳騁無相如之
巨麗也而學其誇誕無韓歐之雄深也而
學其弁放又其甚也不量力而雅相標榜
不知恥而工爲蓋欺拾斷章剩語以爲道
學之文習減句換字以爲高古之文是非
punctuated:
表，亦何嘗雕刻爲文？而誠意溢出，至今使人誦之，自然忠義感激。近世文士不究道德之本，不達當世之務，故詞雖艱深，意實淺近。即使過揚雄、司馬相如，何裨實用？」此我高皇之道也，而亦我高皇之文也。是故百餘年間，風聲所漸，士大夫務經術而重行誼，前輩爲文皆典雅平易，如太羹玄酒，有欲工而未能之意。故永樂、宣德之間，風俗厚而士氣昌，彬彬乎可謂盛矣。
邇來枝葉日盛，而根本日微。無左氏之富也，而學其浮華；無國語之詞也，而學其刻削；無戰國策之權謀也，而學其變化；無董賈之學識也，而學其馳騁；無相如之巨麗也，而學其誇誕；無韓歐之雄深也，而學其弁放。又其甚也，不量力而雅相標榜，不知恥而工爲蓋欺。拾斷章剩語，以爲道學之文；習減句換字，以爲高古之文。是非
translation_en:
…memorial: was it ever composed with elaborate literary ornament? Yet sincerity overflows from it, so that even today those who recite it are naturally stirred to loyalty and righteousness. Literary men of recent times do not investigate the foundations of morality or comprehend the affairs of their age. Thus, although their language is difficult and abstruse, their meaning is actually shallow. Even if they surpassed Yang Xiong and Sima Xiangru, what contribution would they make to practical use?” Such is the Way of our Emperor Gao, and such, too, is his writing. Thus, for more than a hundred years, as his influence spread, scholar-officials devoted themselves to classical learning and valued moral conduct. The writings of earlier generations were all dignified, elegant, plain, and accessible, like unseasoned sacrificial broth and the plain water offered as ritual wine: they conveyed the impression of aspiring to literary skill without quite attaining it. Hence, during the Yongle and Xuande reigns, customs were sound and the spirit of the scholars flourished. This harmonious union of refinement and substance could indeed be called a golden age.
Recently, branches and leaves have flourished daily, while the roots have daily weakened. Writers lack the richness of Master Zuo but imitate his florid ornament; lack the diction of the Discourses of the States (Guoyu) but imitate its painstaking verbal carving; lack the strategic resourcefulness of the Strategies of the Warring States (Zhanguo ce) but imitate its transformations; lack the learning and insight of Dong Zhongshu and Jia Yi but imitate their sweeping rhetorical flights; lack the magnificent splendor of Sima Xiangru but imitate his extravagant exaggeration; lack the power and depth of Han Yu and Ouyang Xiu but imitate their unrestrained expression [?]. Worse still, without gauging their abilities, they habitually acclaim one another; without knowing shame, they become adept at concealment and deception [?]. They gather isolated passages and leftover phrases and pass them off as writings on the Learning of the Way; they practice shortening sentences and substituting words and pass this off as writing of lofty antiquity. Is this not [?] …

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
雖無得於道而於後世之文去之亦遠矣
其於一時之士習遂將潰倒而莫障焉嗚
呼此何時也今日之文章異日之事功也
今日之士子他日之卿相也此有識之士
不得不以爲憂而我
皇上之
詔旨亦屢下也海內士固宜欽
德向風以復我
祖宗之舊矣轉移化導之機不其神哉昔韓子
===
有曰本之深者其末茂膏之沃者其光燁
仁義道德之言藹如也此非有見於一者
之言乎有志於文者必也收心養氣以植
其本格物窮理以充其量求之六經以深
其源博之學庸語孟以會其歸庶幾文王
孔子之所謂文者不俟多岐雜出而可以
得之矣經之爲德行行之爲事業雖躋其
世於三代之上可也夫如是然後不愧我
太祖諄諄訓諭之言然後不負我
punctuated: 雖無得於道，而於後世之文去之亦遠矣。其於一時之士習，遂將潰倒而莫障焉。嗚呼！此何時也？今日之文章，異日之事功也；今日之士子，他日之卿相也。此有識之士不得不以爲憂，而我皇上之詔旨亦屢下也。海內士固宜欽德向風，以復我祖宗之舊矣。轉移化導之機，不其神哉？昔韓子有曰：「本之深者，其末茂；膏之沃者，其光燁。仁義道德之言，藹如也。」此非有見於一者之言乎？有志於文者，必也收心養氣以植其本，格物窮理以充其量，求之六經以深其源，博之學庸語孟以會其歸。庶幾文王、孔子之所謂文者，不俟多岐雜出而可以得之矣。經之爲德行，行之爲事業，雖躋其世於三代之上可也。夫如是，然後不愧我太祖諄諄訓諭之言，然後不負我
translation_en:
…Although they have gained nothing of the Way, they are also far removed from the literary achievements of later ages. As for the habits of the scholars of our time, these will consequently collapse, with no one to check their decline. Alas! What a time this is! Today's literary compositions are tomorrow's practical achievements; today's scholars are tomorrow's ministers and grand councilors. Discerning men cannot but regard this with concern, and our Emperor has repeatedly issued edicts on the matter. Scholars throughout the realm should indeed reverence his virtue and respond to his influence, restoring the old ways of our imperial ancestors. How wondrous is the means by which such change and moral transformation can be brought about!

Master Han once said: “When the roots are deep, the branches flourish; when the oil is abundant, the light shines brightly. Words of benevolence, righteousness, the Way, and virtue flow forth abundantly.” Are these not the words of one who has perceived their underlying unity? Those who aspire to literary achievement must gather in their minds and nurture their vital energy to establish their roots; investigate things and fathom principles to enlarge their capacity; seek understanding in the Six Classics to deepen their source; and extend their learning through the Great Learning, the Doctrine of the Mean, the Analects, and the Mencius to comprehend their common purport. Then perhaps what King Wen and Confucius called “culture” may be attained without waiting for a profusion of divergent approaches. Woven into one's life, it becomes virtuous conduct; put into practice, it becomes practical achievement. One could even raise one's age above the Three Dynasties. Only thus would we be worthy of our Taizu's earnest words of instruction, and only then would we not fail our…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
皇上作新之意是則草茅之所以自待者如此
而方就正焉謹對
第五問
湯惟允
同考試官教授徐　批〔理財之道經傳格言具在深知後世之所由弊而思爲救弊之策以求不失〕
乎聖賢之意如此篇者可以聞之
上矣
考試官教諭陳　批〔議論有梓〕
===
國計
考試官學正楊　批〔酌古準今老成之見也〕
用天下之財成天下之事者也節天下之
財周天下之事者也夫財以濟事而節以
養財此天地自然之理而古今必然之勢
也是故用財而不得其理與棄財同理財
而不得其方與奪人之財同是則今日司
國計者之所宜留意而古帝王之大經大法
亦不外是而可求矣請因明問而陳之自
punctuated:
皇上作新之意。是則草茅之所以自待者如此，而方就正焉。謹對。

第五問
湯惟允
同考試官教授徐批〔理財之道，經傳格言具在，深知後世之所由弊，而思爲救弊之策，以求不失〕乎聖賢之意。如此篇者，可以聞之上矣。
考試官教諭陳批〔議論有梓〕

國計
考試官學正楊批〔酌古準今，老成之見也〕
用天下之財，成天下之事者也；節天下之財，周天下之事者也。夫財以濟事，而節以養財，此天地自然之理，而古今必然之勢也。是故用財而不得其理，與棄財同；理財而不得其方，與奪人之財同。是則今日司國計者之所宜留意，而古帝王之大經大法，亦不外是而可求矣。請因明問而陳之。自
translation_en:
…His Majesty’s intention to bring about renewal. Such, then, are the standards that one living in obscurity sets for himself; I now submit these views for correction. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Fifth Question
Tang Weiyun
Associate Examiner Xu, Prefectural School Instructor, comments: 〔The way to manage wealth is fully set out in the exemplary sayings of the classics and their commentaries. This essay deeply understands the causes of abuses in later ages and considers measures to remedy them, seeking to remain faithful〕 to the intentions of the sages and worthies. An essay such as this may be brought to His Majesty’s attention.
Examiner Chen, County School Instructor, comments: 〔The argument has substance [?].〕

State Finances
Examiner Yang, Departmental School Instructor, comments: 〔Weighing antiquity against the present: this is a seasoned judgment.〕
To use the wealth of the realm is to accomplish the affairs of the realm; to economize on the wealth of the realm is to provide for all its affairs. Wealth enables affairs to be carried out, while economy sustains wealth. This is the natural principle of Heaven and Earth and the necessary course of things, past and present. Thus, to use wealth without grasping the proper principle is no different from throwing it away; to manage wealth without finding the proper method is no different from seizing other people’s wealth. These are matters to which those in charge of state finances today should attend. The great guiding principles and methods of the ancient sage kings likewise go no further than this and may be sought here. Allow me to set out my views in response to your discerning question. From…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
古理財之說黄虞而上不可詳已曾子嘗
人也其傳大學曰生之者衆食之者寡爲
之者疾用之者舒宋儒朱子解曰國無遊
民則生者衆矣朝無倖位則食者寡矣不
奪農時則爲之疾矣量入爲出則用之舒
矣二家之言簡明詳盡眞萬世法程也無
容議矣而執事猶欲合之周禮者蓋嘗考
之太宰以九賦斂財賄一曰邦中之賦二
曰四郊之賦三曰邦甸之賦四曰家削之
===
賦五曰邦縣之賦六曰邦都之賦七曰關
市之賦八曰山澤之賦九曰幣餘之賦以
九式均節財用一曰祭祀之式二曰賓客
之式三曰喪荒之式四曰羞服之式五曰
工事之式六曰幣帛之式七曰芻秣之式
八曰匪頒之式九曰好用之式夫九賦爲
賦賦若多矣然以口率出錢而各因所有
非既使之貢而又賦之也大學之所謂生
者衆而爲者疾不有合乎九式致用用若
punctuated: 古理財之說，黄虞而上不可詳已。曾子嘗人也，其傳《大學》曰：「生之者衆，食之者寡，爲之者疾，用之者舒。」宋儒朱子解曰：「國無遊民，則生者衆矣；朝無倖位，則食者寡矣；不奪農時，則爲之疾矣；量入爲出，則用之舒矣。」二家之言，簡明詳盡，眞萬世法程也，無容議矣。而執事猶欲合之《周禮》者，蓋嘗考之：太宰以九賦斂財賄，一曰邦中之賦，二曰四郊之賦，三曰邦甸之賦，四曰家削之賦，五曰邦縣之賦，六曰邦都之賦，七曰關市之賦，八曰山澤之賦，九曰幣餘之賦。以九式均節財用，一曰祭祀之式，二曰賓客之式，三曰喪荒之式，四曰羞服之式，五曰工事之式，六曰幣帛之式，七曰芻秣之式，八曰匪頒之式，九曰好用之式。夫九賦爲賦，賦若多矣，然以口率出錢，而各因所有，非既使之貢而又賦之也。《大學》之所謂生者衆而爲者疾，不有合乎？九式致用，用若
translation_en:
…ancient teachings on managing wealth cannot be known in detail for the time of Huangdi and Shun or earlier. The wording concerning Zengzi here is unclear [?]. His commentary on the Great Learning says: “Let those who produce be many and those who consume be few; let production be swift and expenditure slow.” The Song Confucian scholar Zhu Xi explained: “If the state has no idle people, producers will be many; if the court has no posts held through favoritism, consumers will be few; if agricultural work is not interrupted, production will be swift; if expenditure is measured against revenue, spending will be slow.” These two masters’ statements are concise and clear, thorough and complete: truly standards for all ages, admitting of no dispute.

Yet you, sir, still wish to reconcile them with the Rites of Zhou. I have examined that work: the Grand Steward collects money and goods through nine levies. The first is the levy on the capital; the second, on the four suburban districts; the third, on the royal agricultural domain; the fourth, on the domains of noble houses [?]; the fifth, on the outlying districts; the sixth, on the great domains; the seventh, on passes and markets; the eighth, on mountains and marshes; and the ninth, on surplus valuables. He regulates and restrains expenditure through nine standards: first, the standard for sacrifices; second, for guests; third, for funerals and famine relief; fourth, for delicacies and clothing; fifth, for construction and craft work; sixth, for gifts of valuables and silk; seventh, for hay and grain fodder; eighth, for distributions of provisions; and ninth, for goodwill gifts.

With nine levies constituting taxation, the taxes might seem numerous. Yet money is assessed per person, with each levy adapted to what the people possess; they are not first made to render tribute and then taxed again. Does this not accord with what the Great Learning calls making producers numerous and production swift? The nine standards govern expenditure, and expenditure seems…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
廣矣然均爲濼式而節以制度使財供於
有司而濼持於大學大學之所謂食者寡
而用者舒不有合乎先王經制盡在此書
彼謂爲戰國之陰謀豈足信哉若夫後世
之理財者異於是漢有計相唐有度支宋
有計省似矣然以武帝之多欲明皇之淫
奢徽宗之靡侈是豈有合於九式之濼乎
告緡算舟車之令間架借商稅之濼經總
月椿錢之類密矣然以桑孔之朘削劉晏
之巧深王安石之頭會箕斂是豈有合於
九賦之式乎斯皆罔民之術宜君子所不
===
道也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝準古建官悉遵周禮我
太宗文皇帝嗣統遷都善爲繼述
列聖相承率由舊章我
皇上之入正大統也禮文憲度損益百王賦稅
則歸之戶部工役則董之工部令格則掌
之禮部良濼美意眞足以陋漢唐宋於下
punctuated:
廣矣，然均爲濼式而節以制度，使財供於有司而濼持於大學。《大學》之所謂「食者寡而用者舒」，不有合乎？先王經制盡在此書，彼謂爲戰國之陰謀，豈足信哉？若夫後世之理財者，異於是。漢有計相，唐有度支，宋有計省，似矣。然以武帝之多欲、明皇之淫奢、徽宗之靡侈，是豈有合於九式之濼乎？告緡算舟車之令、間架借商稅之濼、經總月椿錢之類，密矣。然以桑孔之朘削、劉晏之巧深、王安石之頭會箕斂，是豈有合於九賦之式乎？斯皆罔民之術，宜君子所不道也。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝準古建官，悉遵《周禮》。我太宗文皇帝嗣統遷都，善爲繼述。列聖相承，率由舊章。我皇上之入正大統也，禮文憲度，損益百王。賦稅則歸之戶部，工役則董之工部，令格則掌之禮部。良濼美意，眞足以陋漢唐宋於下
translation_en:
…extensive indeed. Yet uniform rules [?] were established, and expenditure was restrained through institutions and regulations, so that funds were supplied to the responsible offices while the rules [?] were maintained in the Great Learning [?]. Does this not accord with what the Great Learning calls “few who consume and unhurried expenditure”? The institutions of the former kings are all contained in this book. How could those who call it a covert scheme of the Warring States period deserve belief?
Those who managed finances in later ages acted differently. The Han had a Fiscal Chancellor, the Tang a Directorate of Public Revenue, and the Song a finance agency: these appear similar. Yet considering Emperor Wu’s many desires, Emperor Minghuang’s extravagant indulgence, and Emperor Huizong’s lavish excesses, how could these accord with the rules [?] of the nine categories of expenditure? The orders encouraging denunciations of concealed taxable wealth and taxing boats and carts, the measures [?] taxing rooms and extracting loans from merchants, and such levies as the General Administration funds and monthly reserve payments were elaborate indeed. Yet considering the exactions of Sang and Kong, Liu Yan’s ingenious and exacting methods, and Wang Anshi’s levies assessed by the head and gathered as if with a winnowing basket, how could these accord with the standards of the nine levies? These were all devices for ensnaring the people, which a gentleman rightly refuses to discuss.
We reverently consider how our Emperor Taizu Gao established offices on ancient models, following throughout the Rites of Zhou. Our Emperor Taizong Wen succeeded to the throne and moved the capital, ably carrying forward his predecessor’s work. The successive sage emperors followed one another, all adhering to the established statutes. When our reigning emperor assumed his rightful place in the imperial succession, he adapted the ceremonial forms, laws, and institutions of the kings of all ages, making additions and reductions. Taxes are assigned to the Ministry of Revenue; construction and labor services are supervised by the Ministry of Works; ordinances and regulations are administered by the Ministry of Rites. These excellent rules [?] and fine intentions truly suffice to make the Han, Tang, and Song seem inferior…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
風矣又況列之廟堂者臯夔濟濟宜乎周
公所未盡行之志發揮於今太有爲之時
矣邇來荒歉頻仍師旅繼作夫何府庫空
虛蒸民凋瘵誠有如執事所謂公私俱困
者愚則以爲我
朝取民之制於周人九賦之遺尚存而用財
之方於周人九式之法宜講自今言之勸
課農桑矣天下宜無遊民也而緇衣黃冠
者果盡歸隴畝乎䆫陬幽明矣天下宜無
===
倖位也而醉醲飽鮮者果盡屬擯斥乎征
榷鹽茶矣山澤宜無遺利也而田畝荒蕪
者果盡皆開墾乎四禮有制矣民庶宜無
僭分也而甲第侯王者果盡能儉約乎凡
此皆害財之尤而時已先因矣萬一國有
大事不得不重取之於民而天下之事始
有不可勝言者矣故陸贄爲豐財之說有
曰取之有度用之有節則常足取之無度
用之無節則常不足李翶平賦之書有曰
punctuated: 風矣。又況列之廟堂者，臯夔濟濟，宜乎周公所未盡行之志，發揮於今太有爲之時矣。邇來荒歉頻仍，師旅繼作，夫何府庫空虛，蒸民凋瘵，誠有如執事所謂公私俱困者？愚則以爲，我朝取民之制，於周人九賦之遺尚存，而用財之方，於周人九式之法宜講。自今言之，勸課農桑矣，天下宜無遊民也，而緇衣黃冠者果盡歸隴畝乎？䆫陬幽明矣，天下宜無倖位也，而醉醲飽鮮者果盡屬擯斥乎？征榷鹽茶矣，山澤宜無遺利也，而田畝荒蕪者果盡皆開墾乎？四禮有制矣，民庶宜無僭分也，而甲第侯王者果盡能儉約乎？凡此皆害財之尤，而時已先因矣。萬一國有大事，不得不重取之於民，而天下之事始有不可勝言者矣。故陸贄爲豐財之說，有曰：「取之有度，用之有節，則常足；取之無度，用之無節，則常不足。」李翶《平賦》之書有曰：
translation_en:
…in an inferior position. Moreover, the court is filled with men like Gao and Kui. Surely the aspirations that the Duke of Zhou could not fully realize should find expression today, in an age capable of great achievements. Recently, however, crop failures and famine have repeatedly occurred, and military campaigns have followed one another. Why, then, are the treasuries empty and the common people impoverished and afflicted, just as you have said: public and private resources alike are exhausted? In my humble view, our dynasty’s system of levying contributions from the people still preserves something of the Zhou people’s nine categories of taxation, but its methods of expenditure ought to be examined in light of their nine standards of expenditure.

To speak of present circumstances: agriculture and sericulture are encouraged and supervised, so there ought to be no idle people in the realm; yet have all those in black robes and yellow caps—the Buddhist monks and Daoist priests—truly returned to the fields? The obscure and the illustrious have been distinguished [?], so there ought to be no positions gained through undeserved favor in the realm; yet have all those who get drunk on strong wine and gorge themselves on delicacies truly been dismissed? Salt and tea are taxed and subjected to monopolies, so no source of profit in the mountains and marshes ought to remain untapped; yet have all the neglected fields truly been brought under cultivation? The four rites are regulated, so the common people ought not to overstep the distinctions of rank; yet have those whose grand residences rival those of marquises and princes [?] truly all practiced frugality? All these are especially harmful to financial resources, and already the times are straitened [?]. Should some great affair of state arise, heavier exactions from the people would become unavoidable, and the resulting troubles throughout the realm would then be beyond recounting.

Thus Lu Zhi, in discussing how to increase financial resources, said: “If collections have limits and expenditure is restrained, there will always be enough; if collections have no limits and expenditure is unrestrained, there will never be enough.” Li Ao, in his writing On Equalizing Taxation, said: …

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
人皆知重歛之爲可以得財而不知輕歛
之得財愈多蓋爲唐事論也至司馬光乃
曰天之生財止有此數不在於民則在於
官蓋爲經筵論也嗚呼唐宋之事無及矣
爲今之計宜循傳者之言倣周人之意以
求合於陸贄李翺司馬光之說則周官太
平豈難致哉若夫鹽粗之說特一偏耳何
者國額有限而民欲無窮以有限之額待
無窮之民固已難矣且富人多田而窮民
===
無稅有繼富之虛無周急之實又何取焉
况夫影射那移之弊端里書吏胥之騙局
所謂杯水救輿薪也不得已而爲之筭則
關市之商販可抑也山場之封禁可啓也
冶鑄之場務可尋也是皆爲開財之源乎
不急之土木可停也無名之賞賚可罷也
坐食之冗員可省也是皆爲節財之流乎
夫然庶幾乎不傷於生民之心以竊附於
經禮之意故曰成天下之事者在財而理
punctuated: 「人皆知重歛之爲可以得財，而不知輕歛之得財愈多。」蓋爲唐事論也。至司馬光乃曰：「天之生財，止有此數；不在於民，則在於官。」蓋爲經筵論也。嗚呼！唐宋之事無及矣。爲今之計，宜循傳者之言，倣周人之意，以求合於陸贄、李翺、司馬光之說，則周官太平，豈難致哉？若夫鹽粗之說，特一偏耳。何者？國額有限，而民欲無窮，以有限之額待無窮之民，固已難矣。且富人多田，而窮民無稅，有繼富之虛，無周急之實，又何取焉？况夫影射那移之弊端，里書吏胥之騙局，所謂杯水救輿薪也。不得已而爲之筭，則關市之商販可抑也，山場之封禁可啓也，冶鑄之場務可尋也，是皆爲開財之源乎？不急之土木可停也，無名之賞賚可罷也，坐食之冗員可省也，是皆爲節財之流乎？夫然，庶幾乎不傷於生民之心，以竊附於經禮之意。故曰：「成天下之事者在財，而理
translation_en:
…“Everyone knows that heavy levies can yield revenue, but they do not know that light levies yield still more.” This was an argument concerning affairs under the Tang. Sima Guang, in turn, said: “The wealth that Heaven produces amounts only to this fixed quantity. If it is not with the people, it is with the government.” This was an argument presented at the imperial lectures. Alas! Nothing can now be done about the affairs of the Tang and Song. In devising measures for the present, we should follow the commentators’ words and emulate the intentions of the people of Zhou, seeking accord with the views of Lu Zhi, Li Ao, and Sima Guang. Would the great peace embodied in the Offices of Zhou then be difficult to attain?

As for the proposal concerning “salt and coarse [goods?]” [?], it addresses only one aspect. Why? The state’s quota is limited, while the people’s wants are limitless. To provide for a limitless populace with a limited quota is already difficult. Moreover, the rich possess much land, while the poor have no tax liability: there is the hollow appearance of adding to the wealth of the rich, but no substantive relief for those in urgent need. What, then, recommends it? Still less can it succeed amid abuses involving false claims and transfers of funds, and the fraudulent schemes of village clerks and petty functionaries. This is what is meant by trying to save a cartload of burning firewood with a cup of water.

If, having no alternative, we devise a plan, then merchants trading at customs barriers and markets could be restrained, prohibitions closing off mountain tracts could be lifted, and smelting and casting establishments could be investigated. Would these not all open sources of revenue? Nonessential construction could be halted, rewards bestowed without justification could be abolished, and superfluous officials who draw sustenance without working could be reduced. Would these not all curb the outflow of wealth?

By acting thus, we might avoid wounding the hearts of the people and humbly bring our measures into accord with the intent of the canonical rites. Hence it is said: “Accomplishing the affairs of the realm depends upon wealth, while managing…”

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text: 天下之財者在節謹對
punctuated: 天下之財者在節。謹對。
translation_en: …the management of the wealth of all under Heaven depends on restraint in expenditure. Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
是歲甲午〔錠〕以聘來江西謬
承試事試事既成御史則錄
諸有事者姓名及諸生中式
者幷選其文且
獻
闕下而〔錠〕以故事當序于後惟
===
江西在寰中是稱名省而于
其間最雄據者莫如廬山最
匯澤者莫如彭蠡彭蠡之大
洪濤稽天吞吐日月而廬山
周亘幾百里名勝之稱等于
列嶽蓄靈出異時鍾爲人以
成俊德而垂榮名者往往故
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

是歲甲午，〔錠〕以聘來江西，謬承試事。試事既成，御史則錄諸有事者姓名及諸生中式者，幷選其文，且獻闕下。而〔錠〕以故事當序于後。惟江西在寰中，是稱名省，而于其間最雄據者莫如廬山，最匯澤者莫如彭蠡。彭蠡之大，洪濤稽天，吞吐日月；而廬山周亘幾百里，名勝之稱等于列嶽。蓄靈出異，時鍾爲人，以成俊德而垂榮名者往往，故
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In this jiawu year, I, Ding 〔錠〕, came to Jiangxi by invitation and undeservedly received responsibility for the examination. Once the examination was completed, the censor recorded the names of all those who had served in its administration and of the successful candidates, and selected their essays, intending to present these at the imperial court. Following established precedent, I, Ding 〔錠〕, was to write a postface.

Within the realm, Jiangxi is renowned as a distinguished province. Among its features, none occupies a more imposing position than Mount Lu, and none gathers waters more abundantly than Pengli Lake. Such is Pengli’s vastness that its mighty waves reach the heavens [?], swallowing and disgorging the sun and moon. Mount Lu extends for several hundred li, its reputation for scenic beauty equaling that of the sacred peaks. These places store up spiritual potency and bring forth marvels; from time to time that potency concentrates in human beings. Those who thereby attain outstanding virtue and leave glorious names to posterity have often appeared. Thus …

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
多臣邦範俗之良雄傑不群
之士是故雅量若徐穉陶潛
文章若歐陽脩曾鞏黃庭堅
汪藻虞集問學若陸九淵吳
澄陳澔勳名若陶侃敦諒若
胡銓忠節若文天祥洪皓謝
枋得乃歐陽之文尤與天地
===
齊其終極而不但當列于盧
山彭蠡之間與二靈者爭雄
長也
國朝設科以文取士得人之盛
每曰江西而〔錠〕乃今得縱觀
江西士子者且其挾藝而來
者三千餘人其稱先王陳說
punctuated:
多臣邦範俗之良、雄傑不群之士。是故雅量若徐穉、陶潛，文章若歐陽脩、曾鞏、黃庭堅、汪藻、虞集，問學若陸九淵、吳澄、陳澔，勳名若陶侃，敦諒若胡銓，忠節若文天祥、洪皓、謝枋得。乃歐陽之文，尤與天地齊其終極，而不但當列于盧山、彭蠡之間，與二靈者爭雄長也。
國朝設科，以文取士，得人之盛，每曰江西。而〔錠〕乃今得縱觀江西士子者，且其挾藝而來者三千餘人，其稱先王、陳說
translation_en:
…many worthy men who served the state [?] and set an example for its customs, and outstanding men of exceptional ability. Thus, for magnanimity there were Xu Zhi and Tao Qian; for literary accomplishment, Ouyang Xiu, Zeng Gong, Huang Tingjian, Wang Zao, and Yu Ji; for scholarship, Lu Jiuyuan, Wu Cheng, and Chen Hao; for meritorious achievement and renown, Tao Kan; for sincerity and trustworthiness, Hu Quan; and for loyalty and integrity, Wen Tianxiang, Hong Hao, and Xie Fangde. Ouyang’s writings, in particular, will endure as long as Heaven and Earth. They should not merely be ranked alongside Mount Lu and Lake Pengli, contending for preeminence with these two numinous powers.
Our dynasty established the examinations to select men through their writing. Whenever the abundance of worthy men thus obtained is discussed, Jiangxi is invariably mentioned. And I, Ding 〔錠〕, have now had the opportunity to survey the scholars of Jiangxi at large. More than three thousand have come bearing their literary skills; they invoke the former kings and expound…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
世務者人人莫不能是其得
之于意而昌之于辭者或駸
駸然有作者之志錠益以見
明時教化之功而庶歐陽氏之澤
之未泯也蓋非徒山川之發
爲祥哲人之作于始而問學
之功炳然已徵于是將履之
===
而爲雅潔之名蓄之而爲敦
諒精誠之志出之而爲莫大
之勲斯有司者于諸士于昔
之是行也不能無望焉爾矣
廣東韶州府仁化縣儒學教
諭陳錠謹序
punctuated:
世務者，人人莫不能。是其得之于意而昌之于辭者，或駸駸然有作者之志。錠益以見明時教化之功，而庶歐陽氏之澤之未泯也。蓋非徒山川之發爲祥、哲人之作于始，而問學之功炳然已徵于是。將履之而爲雅潔之名，蓄之而爲敦諒精誠之志，出之而爲莫大之勲。斯有司者于諸士于昔之是行也，不能無望焉爾矣。
廣東韶州府仁化縣儒學教諭陳錠謹序。
translation_en:
…as for discussing the affairs of the age, every one of them is capable. Among those who grasp these matters in their minds and give them flourishing expression in words, some are steadily advancing with the ambition of becoming accomplished writers. I, Ding, see all the more clearly the achievements of moral instruction in this enlightened age, and cherish the hope that the legacy of Ouyang has not faded. For it is not merely that the mountains and rivers have manifested auspicious influences, or that wise men arose at the beginning: the achievements of learning and inquiry are already brilliantly evident here. They will put this learning into practice to establish reputations for refinement and purity, nurture it within themselves as a resolve grounded in generosity, trustworthiness, and utter sincerity, and bring it forth in deeds of the greatest merit. Thus, we officials cannot but entertain hopes for these scholars on this undertaking [?].
Preface respectfully composed by Chen Ding, Instructor of the Confucian School of Renhua County, Shaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong.

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖德當新十兩五風
國有九年之蓄
千秋萬歲人歌五福之全臣兢無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叄場
===
策五道
第一問
黃腦
同考試官教諭戴　批　敘歷代兵制與我
朝立法之善歷歷如見至末有脩復變通之說尤非庸見所及
同考試官教諭趙　批　以優恤簡閱之政爲
今日治兵之急務可以知子胷中之經畧矣
考試官教諭陳　批　論兵政具有的見
考試官學正楊　批　是可與談兵者
punctuated:
聖德當新，十兩五風，國有九年之蓄，千秋萬歲，人歌五福之全。臣兢無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叄場
策五道
第一問
黃腦

同考試官教諭戴批：敘歷代兵制與我朝立法之善，歷歷如見。至末有脩復變通之說，尤非庸見所及。

同考試官教諭趙批：以優恤簡閱之政爲今日治兵之急務，可以知子胷中之經畧矣。

考試官教諭陳批：論兵政，具有的見。

考試官學正楊批：是可與談兵者。
translation_en:
…Your Majesty’s sagely virtue is renewed; “ten liang and five winds” [?], and the state has reserves sufficient for nine years. For a thousand autumns and ten thousand years, the people sing of the fullness of the five blessings. Your servant, trembling, looks toward Heaven and reverently up to Your Majesty, overwhelmed by fervent emotion and profound trepidation. I respectfully submit this memorial expressing thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions
First Question
Huang Nao

Comment by Associate Examiner Dai, Instructor: “His account of the military institutions of successive dynasties and the excellence of our dynasty’s legislation is so clear that they seem before our eyes. His concluding proposals for restoration and adaptation are especially beyond the reach of ordinary understanding.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “He identifies generous care for the troops and their inspection and training as the urgent tasks of military administration today. This reveals the strategic understanding he possesses.”

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “His discussion of military administration displays sound insights throughout.”

Comment by Examiner Yang, Instructor: “Here is someone with whom one can discuss military affairs.”

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
天下未嘗有廢法之治而帝王未嘗無致
治之法自古立法創制之君豈不欲以貽
之子孫以爲萬世利哉顧事機之來不盡
如初意雖良法有時而窮非法之窮也勢
也順其勢而導之與昧其勢而强之此則
治亂存亡之所由繫前事可以鑒矣執事
發策秋闈而以歷代兵法及我
祖宗經制下詢此豈章句書生所能辨哉雖然
敢述所聞以對周禮小司徒會萬民之卒
===
伍而用之以起軍旅以作田役以比追胥
以令貢賦乃均出地以籍其人民而周知
其數上中下地家各以其數任人凡起徒
役毋過家一人以其餘爲羨成周出軍之
制大畧若此自是之後兵甲内政古意漸
失漢興踵秦雖南北兩軍調之于民而七
校樓船材官騎士之制去古遠矣唐之府
兵稍合古制一變而爲彍騎再變而爲藩
鎮卒至强臣悍將布滿天下弗可制已宋
punctuated:
天下未嘗有廢法之治，而帝王未嘗無致治之法。自古立法創制之君，豈不欲以貽之子孫，以爲萬世利哉？顧事機之來，不盡如初意，雖良法有時而窮。非法之窮也，勢也。順其勢而導之，與昧其勢而强之，此則治亂存亡之所由繫，前事可以鑒矣。執事發策秋闈，而以歷代兵法及我祖宗經制下詢，此豈章句書生所能辨哉？雖然，敢述所聞以對。
《周禮》小司徒會萬民之卒伍，而用之，以起軍旅，以作田役，以比追胥，以令貢賦。乃均出地，以籍其人民，而周知其數。上中下地，家各以其數任人。凡起徒役，毋過家一人，以其餘爲羨。成周出軍之制，大畧若此。自是之後，兵甲内政，古意漸失。漢興踵秦，雖南北兩軍調之于民，而七校、樓船、材官、騎士之制，去古遠矣。唐之府兵稍合古制，一變而爲彍騎，再變而爲藩鎮，卒至强臣悍將布滿天下，弗可制已。宋
translation_en:
There has never been orderly government in the realm that dispensed with laws, nor have emperors and kings ever lacked laws for bringing about good government. From antiquity, did rulers who established laws and created institutions not wish to bequeath them to their descendants as a benefit for ten thousand generations? Yet circumstances as they unfold do not always accord with the original intent, and even good laws sometimes reach their limits. It is not the laws themselves that are exhausted: it is circumstances that bring this about. Whether one follows circumstances and guides them, or remains blind to circumstances and forces matters, determines order or disorder, survival or destruction. Past events offer a mirror. You, honored examiners, have posed a policy question in the autumn Provincial Examination, graciously asking about the military institutions of successive dynasties and the established institutions of our imperial ancestors. How could a scholar versed merely in textual passages and phrases elucidate these matters? Nevertheless, I venture to set forth what I have heard in reply.
In the Rites of Zhou, the Junior Minister of Education organized the people into units of one hundred and five, employing them to mobilize armies, undertake agricultural labor services, organize pursuit and apprehension, and impose tribute and levies. He then apportioned the land contributions [?], registered the population, and obtained a complete knowledge of its numbers. For land of upper, middle, and lower quality, each household supplied men for service according to its prescribed number. Whenever labor service was mobilized, no more than one man was taken from each household; the remainder were held in reserve. Such, in broad outline, was the system by which the Zhou mobilized armies. Thereafter, the ancient intention of incorporating military organization into civil administration gradually disappeared. When the Han arose, it followed the Qin. Although the Southern and Northern Armies were levied from the people, the institutions of the Seven Colonels, tower ships, picked infantry, and cavalry were far removed from antiquity. The Tang militia system, or fubing, accorded somewhat with ancient institutions. One transformation turned it into the expanded cavalry, or kuoqi; another turned it into regional military commands. In the end, powerful ministers and fierce generals filled the realm and could no longer be controlled. The Song…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
之初有禁軍廂軍鄉軍藩兵承平之後日
益驕惰南渡以來土宇日蹙兵雖多門無
能爲已夫歷代兵法因革損益各隨所宜
使其後人變而通之豈有弊乎若吾
祖宗之法用之百六十年亦屢變矣奚俟他求
哉在乎因其勢以捄其弊故曰神而明之
存乎人亦惟我
太祖久歷戎行洞諳兵事故其爲法也精有非
歷代所能及者是故內設五府建四十八
===
衛外有都指揮司指揮各衛及千百户所
總小旗之制既又
命中書省臣同大都督府御史臺六部官定議
教練之律具在也嗣我
太宗建都燕京纘成先業仍立五府增七十二
衛設五軍神機三千大營又以河南山東
中都大寧四都司官軍輪聚京師歲教月
練眞得居重馭輕之宜矣夫以四都司之
迭操著即我
punctuated: 之初，有禁軍、廂軍、鄉軍、藩兵。承平之後，日益驕惰；南渡以來，土宇日蹙，兵雖多門，無能爲已。夫歷代兵法，因革損益，各隨所宜，使其後人變而通之，豈有弊乎？若吾祖宗之法，用之百六十年，亦屢變矣，奚俟他求哉？在乎因其勢以捄其弊，故曰：「神而明之，存乎人。」亦惟我太祖久歷戎行，洞諳兵事，故其爲法也精，有非歷代所能及者。是故內設五府，建四十八衛；外有都指揮司，指揮各衛及千百户所、總小旗之制。既又命中書省臣同大都督府、御史臺、六部官定議教練之律，具在也。嗣我太宗建都燕京，纘成先業，仍立五府，增七十二衛，設五軍、神機、三千大營。又以河南、山東、中都、大寧四都司官軍輪聚京師，歲教月練，眞得居重馭輕之宜矣。夫以四都司之迭操著，即我
translation_en:
…at the beginning of the Song, there were palace armies, prefectural armies, local armies, and tribal troops. After a period of peace, they grew increasingly arrogant and indolent. Since the court’s retreat southward, the territory dwindled daily; although troops belonged to many different branches, they could accomplish nothing. Military institutions throughout successive dynasties retained or changed, reduced or augmented their arrangements as circumstances required. If their successors had adapted these institutions and made them work, how could abuses have arisen? The institutions of our imperial ancestors have been in use for 160 years and have likewise undergone repeated changes. Why need we seek elsewhere? What matters is to remedy their defects in accordance with circumstances. Thus it is said: “Making them wondrously effective and bringing them to full realization rests with the person.”

Our Taizu had long served in the ranks and thoroughly understood military affairs. Consequently, the institutions he established were so finely devised that in some respects no previous dynasty could match them. At the capital he established the Five Chief Military Commissions and forty-eight guards. Outside the capital there were Regional Military Commissions directing the various guards, together with a system of battalion and company offices and company and platoon commanders. He subsequently ordered officials of the Secretariat, together with officials of the Chief Military Commission, the Censorate, and the Six Ministries, to deliberate upon and establish statutes for military training. These remain fully available.

Thereafter our Taizong established the capital at Yanjing and carried forward the work of his predecessor. He retained the Five Chief Military Commissions, added seventy-two guards, and established the great camps of the Five Armies, the Firearms Corps, and the Three Thousand. He also had officers and soldiers from the four Regional Military Commissions of Henan, Shandong, Zhongdu, and Daning assemble in rotation at the capital, receiving instruction yearly and drilling monthly. This truly achieved the proper arrangement whereby a strong center controlled the lesser forces elsewhere. Now, the established practice [?] of alternating drills among these four Regional Military Commissions was precisely what our…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
太祖所議敎練之律也今考其法指揮所轄萬
人使其武備不精一千至六千人者罰俸
有差至七千人者降級有差千戶所轄千
人以百爲限百戶所轄百人以十爲限故
當時謀臣勇將布滿京營衛皆精兵兵皆
可用雖不必盡泥諸古而已合古人之法
矣厥後承平日久法寢以衰正統己巳之
變虜騎衝突若履無人之境兵部尚書于
謙因軍政廢弛迺立爲十團營挑選各營
===
之精壯驍勇者充之其老瘽疲弱不堪戰
敵者退還原營謂之老家天順初年罷之
三年復置七年又罷之成化初年復置後
增爲十二營凡有征調則十營之兵以次
啓行謂之老家者迺爲宿衛守衛之用也
其法亦可謂備其制亦可謂精矣夫法久
而敝勢所必至變通之宜正在今日試以
今日團營之弊言之可謂名存實亡者矣
老瘽疲弱充斥十二則團營與老家又何
punctuated:
太祖所議敎練之律也。今考其法，指揮所轄萬人，使其武備不精，一千至六千人者，罰俸有差；至七千人者，降級有差。千戶所轄千人，以百爲限；百戶所轄百人，以十爲限。故當時謀臣勇將布滿京營，衛皆精兵，兵皆可用。雖不必盡泥諸古，而已合古人之法矣。
厥後承平日久，法寢以衰。正統己巳之變，虜騎衝突，若履無人之境。兵部尚書于謙因軍政廢弛，迺立爲十團營，挑選各營之精壯驍勇者充之。其老瘽疲弱不堪戰敵者，退還原營，謂之老家。天順初年罷之，三年復置，七年又罷之。成化初年復置，後增爲十二營。凡有征調，則十營之兵以次啓行，謂之老家者迺爲宿衛守衛之用也。其法亦可謂備，其制亦可謂精矣。
夫法久而敝，勢所必至，變通之宜正在今日。試以今日團營之弊言之，可謂名存實亡者矣。老瘽疲弱充斥十二，則團營與老家又何
translation_en:
…the training regulations deliberated upon by Taizu. Now, examining these rules: a commander had ten thousand men under his authority. If their military preparedness was deficient, he incurred graded forfeitures of salary when the number concerned ranged from one thousand to six thousand, and graded demotions when it reached seven thousand. A battalion commander commanded one thousand men, with one hundred as the threshold; a company commander commanded one hundred men, with ten as the threshold. Thus, at that time, resourceful ministers and valiant generals filled the capital camps; every guard had elite troops, and every soldier was fit for service. Although these arrangements did not necessarily adhere slavishly to ancient precedents in every respect, they already accorded with the methods of the ancients.
Thereafter, prolonged peace gradually brought these regulations into decline. During the crisis of the jisi year of the Zhengtong reign [1449], enemy cavalry swept through as though traversing an uninhabited land. Because military administration had fallen into neglect, Yu Qian, Minister of War, established ten consolidated camps, filling them with men selected from the various camps for their vigor and valor. Those who were old, ill, exhausted, or weak and unable to face the enemy in battle were returned to their original camps, which were called the “old homes.” The consolidated camps were abolished early in the Tianshun reign, restored in its third year [1459], and abolished again in its seventh year [1463]. They were restored early in the Chenghua reign and subsequently increased to twelve camps. Whenever troops were called up for a campaign, the soldiers of the ten camps set out in sequence, while those called the “old homes” were employed for palace guard and other guard duties. These methods could indeed be called comprehensive, and these arrangements finely devised.
That regulations deteriorate with time is inevitable; the appropriate moment to adapt them is precisely today. Consider the defects of today’s consolidated camps: they may be said to exist in name alone, their substance gone. The old, ill, exhausted, and weak fill all twelve; how, then, do the consolidated camps and the “old homes” …

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
異途一遍經調戰盡十二營而挑選之不
能百一則團營雖多又何益也近者大同
之變雖
===
天威震怖遂以平定然愚聞其倉卒事變之初
固有遣官募兵之令矣亦有借輸太倉之
餉充之亦有備調延綏寧夏之兵者矣夫軍
出力以衛民也民出力以養軍也今在營
之兵月食米八萬一千五百有餘石歲計
之食米九十七萬八千餘石是皆百姓之
膏血而緩急不足恃卒紛紛焉此豈
祖宗之法也哉在
祖宗時邊儲充實士卒用命若太倉天庫之蓄
惟為根本之防今邊塵有警輒以太倉萬
一京師有事又將何以備之此非
祖宗之法也夫延綏者中原之藩籬寧夏者中
原之障蔽不可一日忘修者也今大同有
變借調延綏寧夏一有事又將何以借
之此非
punctuated: 異？途一遍經調戰，盡十二營而挑選之，不能百一，則團營雖多，又何益也？近者大同之變，雖天威震怖，遂以平定，然愚聞其倉卒事變之初，固有遣官募兵之令矣，亦有借輸太倉之餉充之，亦有備調延綏寧夏之兵者矣。夫軍出力以衛民也，民出力以養軍也。今在營之兵，月食米八萬一千五百有餘石，歲計之，食米九十七萬八千餘石，是皆百姓之膏血，而緩急不足恃，卒紛紛焉，此豈祖宗之法也哉？在祖宗時，邊儲充實，士卒用命，若太倉天庫之蓄，惟為根本之防。今邊塵有警，輒以太倉，萬一京師有事，又將何以備之？此非祖宗之法也。夫延綏者，中原之藩籬；寧夏者，中原之障蔽，不可一日忘修者也。今大同有變，借調延綏寧夏，一有事，又將何以借之？此非
translation_en:
…different? Once troops are mobilized for battle [?], a selection made from all twelve camps yields not even one man in a hundred. What benefit, then, is there in having so many combined training camps? In the recent disturbance at Datong, although the awe-inspiring imperial might struck terror and thus brought about its pacification, I have heard that, when the crisis first erupted unexpectedly, orders were indeed issued to dispatch officials to recruit soldiers. Funds destined for the Grand Granary were also borrowed to meet military expenses, and preparations were made to transfer troops from Yansui and Ningxia.

Soldiers exert themselves to protect the people; the people exert themselves to support the soldiers. The troops now in the camps consume more than 81,500 shi of rice each month, amounting to more than 978,000 shi annually. All this is the lifeblood of the common people, yet in an emergency these troops cannot be relied upon, and everything ends in confusion. Can this be the system of our imperial ancestors? In their time, frontier reserves were ample, and officers and soldiers faithfully carried out their orders. The stores of the Grand Granary and the imperial treasury were reserved solely for defending the foundations of the state. Now, whenever an alarm arises on the frontier, recourse is immediately had to the Grand Granary. Should trouble arise in the capital itself, what would remain with which to provide for its defense? This is not the system of our imperial ancestors.

Yansui is the fence protecting the Central Plain; Ningxia is its defensive screen. Their defenses must not be neglected for even a day. Now, because a disturbance has arisen at Datong, troops are borrowed from Yansui and Ningxia. Should trouble arise there, from where could troops then be borrowed? This is not…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
祖宗之法也固不能不有望于我
皇上修復而變通之矣今團營之法畫一具在
勑下兵部推選才力大臣如于謙者特司其事
精加汰擇毋令影射彼强壯驍勇役使于
私家者奪之疲癃殘疾充列於行伍者汰
之乃若敝衣惡體負甲而不能行者盡行
挑選定爲冊籍而尤嚴賣放之律使收納
月錢臨期顧募以應一時之點視者無所
售其奸重科尅之禁使百計需索假公務
以剥削軍士者無所滋其弊如是則兵爲
有用可以應敵而制勝矣至我
太祖教練之律舊章如新愚願
勑下兵部查議舉行先行省諭令其操練三年
之後責之巡按御史歲一監閱如前降罰
冊名上
聞有能操習勤勞閱有勤効則禄之可也旌之
可也加之陞授及其終身亦可也天下孰
punctuated:
祖宗之法也。固不能不有望于我皇上修復而變通之矣。今團營之法，畫一具在，勑下兵部，推選才力大臣如于謙者，特司其事，精加汰擇，毋令影射。彼强壯驍勇役使于私家者，奪之；疲癃殘疾充列於行伍者，汰之。乃若敝衣惡體，負甲而不能行者，盡行挑選，定爲冊籍，而尤嚴賣放之律，使收納月錢、臨期顧募以應一時之點視者，無所售其奸；重科尅之禁，使百計需索、假公務以剥削軍士者，無所滋其弊。如是，則兵爲有用，可以應敵而制勝矣。
至我太祖教練之律，舊章如新。愚願勑下兵部，查議舉行，先行省諭，令其操練。三年之後，責之巡按御史，歲一監閱，如前降罰，冊名上聞。有能操習勤勞，閱有勤効，則禄之可也，旌之可也，加之陞授及其終身亦可也。天下孰
translation_en:
…the laws of our ancestors. We therefore cannot but look to Our Emperor to restore them and adapt them to present circumstances. The regulations for the combined camps are now uniformly laid down and fully available. Let an edict be issued to the Ministry of War to select a high minister of talent and ability, such as Yu Qian, and give him special charge of this matter. He should carefully weed out and select the troops, allowing no fraudulent enrollment. Those strong, sturdy, and valiant men employed in private households should be reclaimed; those infirm or disabled men filling places in the ranks should be discharged. As for those in tattered clothing and poor physical condition, unable to walk under the weight of their armor, all should undergo selection, and registers should be established. Above all, strictly enforce the law against selling exemptions from service, so that those who collect monthly payments and, when inspection approaches, hire substitutes to satisfy that momentary muster have no opportunity to carry out their fraud. Strengthen the prohibition against extortion and deductions from soldiers’ pay, so that those who devise countless demands and exploit soldiers under the pretext of official business have no opportunity to perpetuate their abuses. In this way the troops will become serviceable, able to confront the enemy and secure victory.
As for our Taizu’s regulations for military training, these old statutes remain as applicable as ever. I humbly wish that an edict be issued to the Ministry of War to examine and deliberate upon their implementation. First issue clear instructions and order the troops to drill. After three years, charge the Regional Inspectors with supervising an annual review, imposing penalties as previously prescribed, and recording the names in a register for submission to the throne. Those who drill diligently and whose exertions prove effective upon review may be rewarded with emoluments or public distinction; they may also be granted promotion and appointment for the remainder of their lives. Who in all the realm…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
不樂賞惡罰且忍并棄其父祖所遺之爵
祿而不思所以保全圖報之乎如是則兵
可日精而軍官軍士之冗食亦可省矣至
其欲實邊儲則屯種可廣矣鹽法可通矣
欲謹邊防則河套可守矣邊墻可治矣是
故欲興屯種則屯田之議可講也欲通鹽
法則
祖宗之舊可復也欲治邊墻則任人之說可行
也欲守河套則連結之虜可虞也夫懷之
===
以德邊士恤矣畏之以威法令嚴矣示之
以信賞罰明矣若夫脩德柔遠安內攘外
尤在我
皇上惕勵憂勤綱紀四方安不忘危治不忘亂
而已矣愚生草野之見不識執事可轉而
聞之于
上否謹對
第二問
徐良傳
punctuated:
不樂賞惡罰？且忍并棄其父祖所遺之爵祿，而不思所以保全圖報之乎？如是，則兵可日精，而軍官軍士之冗食亦可省矣。至其欲實邊儲，則屯種可廣矣，鹽法可通矣；欲謹邊防，則河套可守矣，邊墻可治矣。是故欲興屯種，則屯田之議可講也；欲通鹽法，則祖宗之舊可復也；欲治邊墻，則任人之說可行也；欲守河套，則連結之虜可虞也。夫懷之以德，邊士恤矣；畏之以威，法令嚴矣；示之以信，賞罰明矣。若夫脩德柔遠，安內攘外，尤在我皇上惕勵憂勤，綱紀四方，安不忘危，治不忘亂而已矣。愚生草野之見，不識執事可轉而聞之于上否？謹對。

第二問

徐良傳
translation_en:
…does not delight in rewards and dislike punishments? Moreover, could they bear to cast aside the rank and emoluments bequeathed by their fathers and grandfathers, without considering how to preserve them and repay imperial favor? In this way, the troops could grow more proficient by the day, and the expense of maintaining superfluous officers and soldiers could also be reduced. As for replenishing frontier reserves, cultivation in military agricultural colonies could be expanded, and the salt administration could be made to function effectively. To strengthen frontier defenses, the Hetao region could be held, and the frontier walls put in good repair. Thus, to promote cultivation in military colonies, proposals concerning military agricultural lands could be deliberated; to make the salt administration function effectively, the old practices of the imperial ancestors could be restored; to repair the frontier walls, proposals concerning the appointment of personnel could be implemented; and to hold Hetao, precautions could be taken against the allied barbarians.

Win their allegiance through virtue, and the frontier soldiers will receive care; inspire awe through authority, and laws and orders will be strictly enforced; demonstrate trustworthiness, and rewards and punishments will be clear. As for cultivating virtue to conciliate distant peoples, securing the interior and repelling external enemies, these depend above all upon our Emperor remaining vigilant, diligent, and mindful of his responsibilities, maintaining order throughout the realm, remembering danger in times of peace and disorder in times of good government. These are the views of an unworthy student living far from court. I do not know whether you, honored officials, might convey them to His Majesty. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Second Policy Question

Xu Liangchuan

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭高　批　藻鑑評品子其兼三長而
冠三等乎於以覘尚友之學
同考試官教諭蘇　批　古人瑕瑜莫掩子能涇渭
之可與言史矣
考試官教諭陳　批　精詳信傳
考試官學正楊　批　博據
有作史之法有讀史之法知作史之法者
始可以讀史矣知讀史之法者始可與言
史矣史其可以易言哉請因明問而備陳
===
之鄧禹之議於鄴下也其延攬英雄之數
語當矣而武侯荊益之圖尤有得乎天下
之計事業成敗之跡安可論哉謝玄之捷
於淮淝也其大敗秦兵之百萬是矣而萊
公澶淵之役尤有近於萬全之謀風鶴一
時之幸安足恃哉丁謂以卜恩見君之言
給貶欽若匹夫之私憤也〔王欽若〕以擅移皇
堂之故計除丁謂忠臣之謀國也烏得而
同耶楊億欲棄靈州而何亮非之孤城不
punctuated:
同考試官教諭高　批：藻鑑評品，子其兼三長而冠三等乎？於以覘尚友之學。
同考試官教諭蘇　批：古人瑕瑜莫掩，子能涇渭之，可與言史矣。
考試官教諭陳　批：精詳信傳。
考試官學正楊　批：博據。
有作史之法，有讀史之法。知作史之法者，始可以讀史矣；知讀史之法者，始可與言史矣。史其可以易言哉？請因明問而備陳之。鄧禹之議於鄴下也，其延攬英雄之數語當矣；而武侯荊益之圖，尤有得乎天下之計，事業成敗之跡安可論哉？謝玄之捷於淮淝也，其大敗秦兵之百萬是矣；而萊公澶淵之役，尤有近於萬全之謀，風鶴一時之幸安足恃哉？丁謂以卜恩見君之言給貶欽若，匹夫之私憤也；〔王欽若〕以擅移皇堂之故計除丁謂，忠臣之謀國也。烏得而同耶？楊億欲棄靈州，而何亮非之，孤城不
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: “In discerning and appraising men, do you not combine the three strengths and stand foremost in the three grades? Here we may glimpse your learning in taking the ancients as friends.”
Associate Examiner Su, Instructor, comments: “You conceal neither the faults nor the virtues of the ancients. You distinguish them as clearly as the Jing and Wei rivers; one may indeed discuss history with you.”
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Precise and detailed, a trustworthy account.”
Examiner Yang, School Director, comments: “Broadly supported by evidence.”
There is a method for writing history, and there is a method for reading it. Only those who understand how to write history can begin to read it; only those who understand how to read history can begin to discuss it. Can history really be discussed lightly? Allow me to set this out fully in response to your illuminating question.
In Deng Yu’s deliberations at Ye, his few words about recruiting outstanding men were sound. Yet the Marquis of Wu’s plan concerning Jing and Yi grasped still more fully the strategy for the realm. How could one judge merely by the outward record of success or failure? In Xie Xuan’s victory in the Huai and Fei region, it is true that he decisively defeated Qin’s million troops. Yet the Duke of Lai’s conduct of the campaign at Chanyuan came still closer to a strategy ensuring complete success. How could one rely on the momentary good fortune of an enemy alarmed by the wind and the cries of cranes?
Ding Wei secured Qinruo’s demotion over remarks about divining imperial favor and seeking an audience with the ruler [?]: this was a common man’s private resentment. [Wang Qinruo] plotted Ding Wei’s removal because he had presumptuously moved the imperial burial chamber: this was a loyal minister’s planning for the state. How could the two be treated alike? Yang Yi wished to abandon Lingzhou, but He Liang opposed him: an isolated city cannot …

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
可黍也牛僧孺欲棄維州而德裕排之不
信不可執也奚而不類耶錢若水四十致
仕宋之二疏也郎其一時風節其翔黃鵠
於秋雲者乎王旦兼玉清宮使王曾之罪
人也攷其立朝建明其玷白璧於微瑕者
乎褚遂良不欲人主預聞史筆是矣厪蒙
乞委宰相抄送史舘則宰相即史官政事
堂即史舘又何取於鑒戒乎李遜學不欲
後世盡信史書宜矣劉定之於戳斧一事
===
深惡太宗然則弟有次及之望兄無付託
之誠亦難免乎猜疑矣德宗識後雅之李
潞而獨不覺盧杞之奸耶無因明通蔽之
學明皇疎忠直之宋璟而又能識李林甫
之媢嫉亦好同惡異之心汲黯出補淮陽
與以宋均爲尚書令一以嚴而見憚一以
寬而見褻也黯何愧於均耶唐介召歸諫
院與賈充留爲騎將一本仁宗不遠之復
一由荀勗夕陽亭之語也充何敢望介耶
punctuated: 可黍也。牛僧孺欲棄維州，而德裕排之，不信不可執也，奚而不類耶？錢若水四十致仕，宋之二疏也。郎其一時風節，其翔黃鵠於秋雲者乎？王旦兼玉清宮使，王曾之罪人也。攷其立朝建明，其玷白璧於微瑕者乎？褚遂良不欲人主預聞史筆，是矣。厪蒙乞委宰相抄送史舘，則宰相即史官，政事堂即史舘，又何取於鑒戒乎？李遜學不欲後世盡信史書，宜矣。劉定之於戳斧一事，深惡太宗，然則弟有次及之望，兄無付託之誠，亦難免乎猜疑矣。德宗識後雅之李潞，而獨不覺盧杞之奸耶？無因明通蔽之學。明皇疎忠直之宋璟，而又能識李林甫之媢嫉，亦好同惡異之心。汲黯出補淮陽，與以宋均爲尚書令，一以嚴而見憚，一以寬而見褻也，黯何愧於均耶？唐介召歸諫院，與賈充留爲騎將，一本仁宗不遠之復，一由荀勗夕陽亭之語也，充何敢望介耶？
translation_en: …could not be abandoned [?; the transcription reads 黍]. Niu Sengru wished to abandon Weizhou, but Deyu opposed him: a policy of breaking faith could not be upheld. Why should these cases not be considered alike? Qian Ruoshui retired from office at forty; he was the Song dynasty’s counterpart to the two Shus. Considering [?] his bearing and integrity in his day, was he not like a yellow swan soaring through autumn clouds? Wang Dan concurrently served as Commissioner of the Yuqing Palace, making him a sinner in Wang Zeng’s eyes. Yet, examining his service at court and the proposals he advanced, was this not merely a slight flaw blemishing white jade? Chu Suiliang was right to oppose letting the ruler know in advance what the historians were writing. Jin Meng [?] requested that the chief councilors be entrusted with copying material and forwarding it to the Historiography Institute. But if the chief councilors thereby became the historiographers, and the Administration Chamber became the Historiography Institute, what would remain of history’s function as a mirror and warning? Li Xunxue was right to wish that later generations would not believe everything in historical writings. Liu Dingzhi deeply detested Taizong over the affair of the stabbing and axe [?]. Yet if the younger brother expected to succeed in turn, while the elder brother had no sincere intention of entrusting the throne to him, suspicion would scarcely have been avoidable. Dezong recognized the refinement [?] of Li Lu [?], yet alone failed to perceive Lu Qi’s treachery! He lacked the learning needed to distinguish clear understanding from blindness [?]. Emperor Minghuang distanced himself from the loyal and upright Song Jing, yet could recognize Li Linfu’s jealousy: this too sprang from a disposition to favor those who agreed with him and dislike those who differed. Compare Ji An’s appointment away from court to Huaiyang with Song Jun’s appointment as Director of the Department of State Affairs: one was feared for his severity, while the other was treated slightingly for his leniency. What reason had An to feel inferior to Jun? Compare Tang Jie’s recall to the Court of Remonstrance with Jia Chong’s retention as a cavalry general: the former arose from Renzong’s returning to the right path before straying far; the latter resulted from Xun Xu’s words at Xiyang Pavilion. How could Chong dare aspire to equal Jie?

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
閫佩以庋亮之邀而戎服登舟乃勉而效
忠焉可比於卽日就道之子儀乎岳武穆
在廬山之隱而復起效用此行權之智曷
嘗若口不言兵之世忠乎曹彬陳桂渢
於野以閩驍將使元昊疑忌而殺之其與
寺人柳之逐華合比夫何異黃歇受李園
之妹以獻楚王使芊楚以黃而代之其與
呂不韋之易嬴秦又何殊李綱爲留守之
計猶邳彤決河北之留也宋高宗惑於二
===
豎而不及光武惜哉張世傑爲宋復讎而
趨占城猶子房爲韓報讎而從漢也海陵
山颶風大作而弗克自全天乎吳兢不從
張說之請信直筆矣蔡卞爲彰婦翁之惡
而罷山谷之春秋一指可以障天地乎曾
肇不入曾布之黨知引嫌矣蔡京〔以婦兄〕
之親而以韓侶爲侍郎〔稍〕思可以逃公議
乎家鉉翁之歸宋欲擬蘇武而不知茫茫
堪輿果孰爲故國之土耶盧藏用之隱終
punctuated: 閫佩以庋亮之邀，而戎服登舟，乃勉而效忠焉，可比於卽日就道之子儀乎？岳武穆在廬山之隱，而復起效用，此行權之智，曷嘗若口不言兵之世忠乎？曹彬陳桂渢於野，以閩驍將，使元昊疑忌而殺之，其與寺人柳之逐華合比，夫何異？黃歇受李園之妹以獻楚王，使芊楚以黃而代之，其與呂不韋之易嬴秦，又何殊？李綱爲留守之計，猶邳彤決河北之留也。宋高宗惑於二豎，而不及光武，惜哉！張世傑爲宋復讎而趨占城，猶子房爲韓報讎而從漢也。海陵山颶風大作，而弗克自全，天乎？吳兢不從張說之請，信直筆矣。蔡卞爲彰婦翁之惡，而罷山谷之春秋，一指可以障天地乎？曾肇不入曾布之黨，知引嫌矣。蔡京〔以婦兄〕之親，而以韓侶爲侍郎，〔稍〕思可以逃公議乎？家鉉翁之歸宋，欲擬蘇武，而不知茫茫堪輿，果孰爲故國之土耶？盧藏用之隱終
translation_en:
…“Kunpei,” at the invitation of Gui Liang [?], boarded a boat in military dress and only reluctantly rendered loyal service. Could he compare with Ziyi, who set out that very day? Yue Wumu emerged from seclusion on Mount Lu to serve again: this showed wisdom in adapting to circumstances. How was he ever like Shizhong, who would not speak of military affairs? Cao Bin deployed Gui Feng in the field to deal with a fierce general of Min [?], causing Yuanhao to suspect and kill him. How did this differ from the palace eunuch Liu’s expulsion of Hua Hebi? Huang Xie took Li Yuan’s younger sister and presented her to the king of Chu, thereby replacing the Qian [?] ruling house of Chu with the Huang family. How did this differ from Lü Buwei’s substitution of the ruling line of Qin’s Ying family? Li Gang’s plan to remain and defend the capital resembled Pi Tong’s resolve to remain in Hebei. Emperor Gaozong of Song was misled by two scoundrels and fell short of Guangwu. What a pity!

Zhang Shijie went toward Zhancheng to avenge the Song, just as Zifang followed the Han to avenge the state of Han. At Mount Hailing a great hurricane arose, and he could not save himself. Was this Heaven’s doing? Wu Jing refused Zhang Yue’s request: truly, his was an upright historian’s pen. Cai Bian, to expose his father-in-law’s wickedness [?], suppressed Shangu’s Spring and Autumn Annals. Can a single finger obscure Heaven and Earth? Zeng Zhao would not join Zeng Bu’s faction: he understood the need to avoid suspicion of partiality. Cai Jing, because of the kinship 〔of an elder brother of his wife〕, appointed Han Lü [?] Vice Minister. Could he, upon 〔a little〕 reflection, suppose that he could escape public judgment? Jia Xuanweng wished, in returning to the Song, to emulate Su Wu; yet did he not realize that, throughout the vast expanse of Heaven and Earth, no land could truly be called the soil of his former country? Lu Cangyong’s seclusion on Mount Zhong…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
南欲方子陵而不知自有佳處又何取捷
徑之譏耶漢武徙豪傑於茂陵而四豪三
游固已馳騁於王道之久廢成帝詔典領
五經而九流七畧又嘗蕪穢於正學之未
崇倡豐亨豫大之蔡京與統領花石之朱
勔貽害何殊石五胡亂華之劉淵與幽沈
仁義之王何債事無異凡若此者皆是非
同異之所以分治亂興衰之所由寓苟於
是而知所權衡焉則善可以爲法惡可以
爲戒上焉而可以爲君下焉而可以爲臣
於王霸之異道邪正之異學舉皆於是乎
辨矣雖進而讀諸經可矣管見如斯進退
===
惟命
第三問
余文獻
同考試官教諭尤　批　牧政今日今務考據詳而
議論切者無踰此篇
同考試官教諭張　批　馬番息而民不擾學製之
punctuated:
南，欲方子陵，而不知自有佳處，又何取捷徑之譏耶？漢武徙豪傑於茂陵，而四豪三游固已馳騁於王道之久廢；成帝詔典領五經，而九流七畧又嘗蕪穢於正學之未崇。倡豐亨豫大之蔡京，與統領花石之朱勔，貽害何殊？石五胡亂華之劉淵，與幽沈仁義之王何，債事無異。凡若此者，皆是非同異之所以分，治亂興衰之所由寓。苟於是而知所權衡焉，則善可以爲法，惡可以爲戒；上焉而可以爲君，下焉而可以爲臣。於王霸之異道、邪正之異學，舉皆於是乎辨矣。雖進而讀諸經，可矣。管見如斯，進退惟命。
第三問
余文獻
同考試官教諭尤　批：牧政今日今務，考據詳而議論切者，無踰此篇。
同考試官教諭張　批：馬番息而民不擾，學製之
translation_en:
…in Zhongnan, wishing to rival Ziling, yet unaware that there was already a fine place for him: why invite the ridicule of taking a shortcut to office? Emperor Wu of Han moved powerful and distinguished men to Maoling, yet the four magnates and the three sorts of wandering men [?] had already ranged unchecked during the long abandonment of the Kingly Way. Emperor Cheng ordered the Five Classics to be placed under scholarly supervision, yet the Nine Schools and Seven Summaries had also become overgrown with weeds while orthodox learning remained unhonored. What difference was there between the harm bequeathed by Cai Jing, who advocated lavish abundance and expansive grandeur, and by Zhu Mian, who directed the procurement of flowers and ornamental rocks? Liu Yuan, who brought disorder to China through the Five Hu peoples [preceding character 石 unclear], and Wang and He, who submerged benevolence and righteousness, were no different in their deeds [?].
All such cases reveal the distinctions between right and wrong, similarity and difference, and embody the causes of order and disorder, prosperity and decline. If one knows how to weigh them, good conduct can serve as a model and evil conduct as a warning. In a higher station, one can thereby act as a ruler; in a lower station, as a minister. The different paths of true kingship and hegemony, and the different teachings of heterodoxy and orthodoxy, can all be distinguished through this. One may then even advance to reading the Classics. Such is my limited understanding; whether I advance or withdraw, I await your command.
Third Question
Yu Wenxian
Comment by Associate Examiner You, an Instructor: Horse administration is an urgent concern of the present day [?]. For detailed examination of evidence and pertinent argument, no essay surpasses this one.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, an Instructor: Horses multiply while the people remain undisturbed; in learning the craft of government…

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
善者也此子能言之
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔我〕
朝馬政實盛前代而獨盛者此篇數對無遺而每致深意焉用世
〔之文也故錄〕
考試官教諭陳　批〔知以馬富國者〕
考試官學正楊　批〔得人意良是〕
馬政令天下之大務也而明問及之蓋求
天下之大計也顧愚何足以知之雖然嘗
聞周書曰司馬掌邦政夫馬以名官則知
===
武備之弗可忽者也考之周禮四井爲邑
四邑爲丘四丘爲甸天子畿內可得馬四
萬諸侯之國可得四千大夫之家可得四
百此成周天子諸侯大夫之馬數也衞風
之詩曰秉心塞淵騋牝三千有以知文公
牧馬之盛矣魯頌之詩曰駉駉牡馬在坰
之野有以知僖公牧馬之盛矣漢初稍復
古制養馬一匹者復卒三人平居則免三
人之筭有事則當三人之卒至于邊塞則
punctuated:
善者也，此子能言之。
同考試官教諭鄭批：〔我〕朝馬政實盛前代，而獨盛者，此篇數對無遺，而每致深意焉，用世〔之文也，故錄〕。
考試官教諭陳批：〔知以馬富國者〕。
考試官學正楊批：〔得人意，良是〕。
馬政令天下之大務也，而明問及之，蓋求天下之大計也。顧愚何足以知之？雖然，嘗聞《周書》曰：「司馬掌邦政。」夫馬以名官，則知武備之弗可忽者也。考之《周禮》，四井爲邑，四邑爲丘，四丘爲甸。天子畿內可得馬四萬，諸侯之國可得四千，大夫之家可得四百，此成周天子、諸侯、大夫之馬數也。《衞風》之詩曰：「秉心塞淵，騋牝三千。」有以知文公牧馬之盛矣。《魯頌》之詩曰：「駉駉牡馬，在坰之野。」有以知僖公牧馬之盛矣。漢初稍復古制，養馬一匹者復卒三人，平居則免三人之筭，有事則當三人之卒。至于邊塞，則
translation_en:
…one skilled in learning the art of government. This candidate is able to articulate it.
Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “Our dynasty’s horse administration indeed surpasses that of previous dynasties. This essay enumerates, without omission, the respects in which it is uniquely outstanding, and brings out profound implications at every turn. This is writing useful for governing the world; hence its inclusion.”
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “One who understands how horses enrich the state.”
Examiner Yang, School Director, comments: “It expresses what one has in mind—very sound indeed.”
Horse administration is a major concern of the realm [?], and your illuminating question addresses it, surely seeking a comprehensive plan for the realm. Yet how could someone as ignorant as I adequately understand it? Nevertheless, I have heard it said in the Documents of Zhou: “The Minister of War administers the government of the state.” Since horses give this office its name, we know that military preparedness must not be neglected. Examining the Rites of Zhou, we find that four well-field units make a yi, four yi make a qiu, and four qiu make a dian. Within the royal domain, the Son of Heaven could obtain forty thousand horses; a feudal lord’s state could obtain four thousand; and a grand officer’s household could obtain four hundred. These were the numbers of horses belonging to the Son of Heaven, the feudal lords, and the grand officers under the fully established Zhou order. A poem in the Airs of Wei says: “He holds his heart sincere and deep; his tall horses and mares number three thousand.” From this we can understand how flourishing horse rearing was under Duke Wen. A poem in the Eulogies of Lu says: “Stout and sturdy are the stallions, in the fields beyond the outskirts.” From this we can understand how flourishing horse rearing was under Duke Xi. In the early Han, the ancient system was gradually restored. A person who raised one horse received exemption from military service for three men: in ordinary times, three men were exempted from the poll tax; when military action arose, the horse counted in place of three men’s military service. As for the frontier regions, …

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
縱民畜牧而官不禁以至衆庶有馬阡陌
成羣故邊郡之盛則三十六苑分置西北
武帝承平窮兵黷武旣數出師馬大消乏
雖法令日嚴而竟不能復其舊矣唐初剏
置八坊八坊之馬爲四十八監而馬多地
狹又析八監列布河西豐曠之野故自貞
觀麟德四十年之間得馬七十萬餘匹天
寶之後諸軍戰馬動以萬計秦漢以來未
之聞也宋之馬萬不及唐至于户馬之法
===
行于熙寧保馬之法行于元豐焉未必得
而民已受其害矣是故賦之以地弗可均
也歛之以課歲有歉也户配一馬弗可蓄
也馬弗可蓄民俱困也馬斃必償民弗堪
也是故保馬之害滋也哉
朝建都燕京以來陝西遼東各設苑馬寺寺
管六監監管四苑大苑養馬萬匹中苑七
千小苑一千馬不下十三萬匹其原額草
塲十有三萬三千七百七十七頃六十畝
punctuated:
縱民畜牧，而官不禁，以至衆庶有馬，阡陌成羣。故邊郡之盛，則三十六苑分置西北。武帝承平，窮兵黷武，旣數出師，馬大消乏。雖法令日嚴，而竟不能復其舊矣。唐初剏置八坊，八坊之馬爲四十八監，而馬多地狹，又析八監，列布河西豐曠之野。故自貞觀、麟德四十年之間，得馬七十萬餘匹。天寶之後，諸軍戰馬動以萬計，秦漢以來未之聞也。宋之馬萬不及唐。至于户馬之法行于熙寧，保馬之法行于元豐，焉未必得，而民已受其害矣。是故賦之以地，弗可均也；歛之以課，歲有歉也；户配一馬，弗可蓄也；馬弗可蓄，民俱困也；馬斃必償，民弗堪也。是故保馬之害滋也哉！
朝建都燕京以來，陝西、遼東各設苑馬寺，寺管六監，監管四苑。大苑養馬萬匹，中苑七千，小苑一千，馬不下十三萬匹。其原額草塲十有三萬三千七百七十七頃六十畝。
translation_en:
…the people were allowed to raise livestock, and the authorities imposed no prohibition. Consequently, ordinary people owned horses, and herds gathered along the field paths. At the height of horse breeding in the frontier commanderies, thirty-six pastures were established throughout the northwest. Emperor Wu inherited an era of peace but exhausted his military resources in incessant warfare. After repeated campaigns, the horses were severely depleted. Although laws and regulations grew stricter by the day, their former numbers could never be restored.
Early in the Tang, eight horse-breeding establishments were founded, with their horses administered by forty-eight directorates. Because the horses were numerous and the land insufficient, eight further directorates were established and distributed across the rich, open country of Hexi. Thus, in the forty years between the Zhenguan and Linde reign periods, horse numbers reached more than 700,000. After the Tianbao reign period, the warhorses of the various armies regularly numbered in the tens of thousands—something unheard of since Qin and Han times. The Song's horses fell far short of the Tang's. The household-horse system was implemented during the Xining reign period, and the collective-guarantee horse system during the Yuanfeng reign period. Horses were not necessarily obtained [?], yet the people had already suffered the harm these measures caused. Thus, assessments based on land could not be equitable; levies imposed as quotas encountered years of poor harvests; assigning one horse to each household left households unable to support them. When horses could not be supported, the people were all impoverished; when horses died, compensation was required, and the people could not bear it. How greatly, then, did the harms of the collective-guarantee horse system multiply!
Since our dynasty established its capital at Yanjing, Offices of Imperial Parks have been established in both Shaanxi and Liaodong. Each office administers six directorates, and each directorate four pastures. A large pasture raises 10,000 horses, a medium one 7,000, and a small one 1,000, with no fewer than 130,000 horses in all. The original authorized extent of their grazing lands was 133,777 qing and 60 mu.

title: 嘉靖十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
養馬恩隊軍人一千二百二十名正統初
年始將監苑裁省止存二監天順初年復
將苑馬寺併革而原撥恩軍亦遷設矣至
成化間所在種馬止三千匹弘治間所存
草場止六萬六千八百八十八頃八十畝
所存軍人止七百四十五名以致牧馬之
地盡散之民而致終不能復
祖宗之舊矣馬政廢弛邊防甚踈當國計者可
為寒心宜有以厪執事下問之惓惓也為
===
今之計則唐坊監之故地可復也兩京河
南山東養馬之政宋保馬之遺也可革也
原額之草場可復也原設之恩軍可補也
必如大學士楊一清所議種馬可增以廣
蓄也牧軍可增以養馬也是故唐之坊監
即岐豳涇寧也今陝西之鳳翔西安之邠
州平涼之涇州慶陽之寧州即其地也而
又有隴西金城平涼三水皆水草膏腴之
田可為牧放之所者誠得人以往求之經
punctuated:
養馬恩隊軍人一千二百二十名。正統初年，始將監苑裁省，止存二監。天順初年，復將苑馬寺併革，而原撥恩軍亦遷設矣。至成化間，所在種馬止三千匹；弘治間，所存草場止六萬六千八百八十八頃八十畝，所存軍人止七百四十五名。以致牧馬之地盡散之民，而致終不能復祖宗之舊矣。馬政廢弛，邊防甚踈，當國計者可為寒心，宜有以厪執事下問之惓惓也。
為今之計，則唐坊監之故地可復也；兩京、河南、山東養馬之政，宋保馬之遺也，可革也；原額之草場可復也；原設之恩軍可補也。必如大學士楊一清所議，種馬可增以廣蓄也，牧軍可增以養馬也。是故唐之坊監，即岐、豳、涇、寧也。今陝西之鳳翔、西安之邠州、平涼之涇州、慶陽之寧州，即其地也。而又有隴西、金城、平涼、三水，皆水草膏腴之田，可為牧放之所者。誠得人以往求之，經
translation_en:
…and 1,220 soldiers of the en units [?] assigned to raise horses. Early in the Zhengtong reign, the directorates and pastures began to be reduced, leaving only two directorates. Early in the Tianshun reign, the Court of Horse Pasturage was also abolished through consolidation, and the originally assigned en troops [?] were relocated as well.
